description:
NZ's Top Dog Film Festival 2026, The beloved Top Dog Film Festival is back at the Roxy on WEDNESDAY night 5 Aug, 6.15pm for another heartwarming season, with a brand-new line-up of short films that celebrate the extraordinary connection between dogs and humans.

Get ready to fall in love all over again. The 2026 Top Dog Film Festival returns for the 10th year with an electrifying collection of films that prove dogs aren't just pets—they're heroes, healers, and the best friends we never knew we needed.

Witness jaw-dropping adventures, heart-melting rescues, and brilliant canines whose intelligence will leave you speechless. Meet the passionate humans dedicating their lives to helping our four-legged companions thrive, and discover stories so powerful they'll change how you see the world.

This 2+ hour cinematic experience brings you the finest short films from visionary independent filmmakers across the globe—each one a testament to the unbreakable connection between dogs and the people they choose to love.

From laugh-out-loud moments to tears of pure joy, these carefully selected stories will remind you why dogs hold such a sacred place in our hearts.

Don't just watch from the sidelines—be part of something extraordinary. Grab your tickets now and join a community of dog lovers for a cinema experience you'll never forget!

Get your tickets before they all sell out – you’d be barking mad to miss it.

The Top Dog Film Festival presents a 2+ hour cinematic celebration honouring the bond between dogs and their people. Filled with delightfully doggy moments of joy and celebration of our beloved canine companions.

An inclusive and family- friendly event, the Top Dog Film Tour NZ provides a welcoming space for dog lovers of all ages.
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Deaf, A woman navigates the experience of motherhood as a deaf person in a hearing world in Eva Libertad’s crowd-pleasing, feel-good drama which collected the Panaroma Audience Award at Berlin this year.

Based on the award-winning short of the same name, Spanish filmmaker Eva Libertad’s debut follows couple Ángela and Héctor as they make the transition into parenthood. Ángela is deaf. Héctor is not. When she tells them she’s pregnant, her own parents can’t hide their shock – loving but concerned that their daughter will be unable to tackle the task of motherhood. Will the baby be born deaf? Uncertainty abounds as the due date draws closer, and it’s not just Ángela’s parents who are beginning to have doubts.

The foundations for the film’s narrative derive from the personal experiences of first-time actor Miriam Garlo, Libertad’s own sister, as she began to contemplate motherhood as a deaf woman. When surrounded by her other deaf friends, Ángela is comfortable, alive, vibrant within a community that supports her. Around the local mums in the park, or her husband’s friends, isolation sets in with a painful immediacy that anyone who has ever struggled to understand the language in a foreign country will know all too well. A poignant story bound by the chemistry of its leads, deafness is woven into the film as a lived experience, not a defining label. — Matt Bloomfield
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Dreams (Sex Love), A teenage girl recounts her crush for her teacher through the pages of a memoir. The winner of the Golden Bear 2025 is a lucid and tender chronicle of the unforgettable experience of first love.

Originally intended as the second chapter in his trilogy and released in Norway as such, Dag Johan Haugerud’s Dreams ended up premiering internationally as the last. But it secured a fitting crown to the trilogy, by winning the Best Film at the 2025 Berlinale, thus inducting Haugerud among world class auteurs.

Dreams emanates from two of Haugerud’s passions: literature, as he first gained prominence in his homeland as writer, and the cinema of French master Éric Rohmer, distinguished by sentimental skirmishes brimful of finely written dialogues.

The film’s protagonist and narrator is Johanne, a 17-year-old student who falls for her new French teacher Johanna. Johanne manages to get close to her crush, who nonchalantly ignores how her student’s devotion is veering into affection. Yet, this chronicle of first love is told in a voice over reflecting the memoir that Johanne wrote on her experience – meaning that things may or may not have happened as she says. The memoir is also read by the girl’s mother and grandmother who muse on the girl’s literary talent and provide a layer of irony and melancholy to an unfathomably lucid and tender chronicle of the universal and unforgettable experience of first love. — Paolo Bertolin
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Love, What is love? Through the stories of a straight woman and a gay man, Haugerud defies conventions with humor and compassion, in an eloquent and moving masterwork on human relations in the 21st century.

What is love? The age-old question finds a contemporary and adult declination in Dag Johan Haugerud’s final chapter to his Sex Dreams Love trilogy, premiered to universal acclaim at the Venice Film Festival 2024.

Long, bright Oslo summer days form the backdrop as two medical colleagues, one straight, the other gay, follow parallel trajectories in the games of love, attraction, sex and empathy. Meeting by chance on a ferry, the two describe their searches for intimacy. Marianne is into dating and is looking for love, Tor is looking for sex – by cruising for men on dating apps as he rides to and fro on the ferries. Through Haugerud’s effortlessly unpredictable writing, the ferry turns into a magic vessel where the destinies of these two take unexpected turns…

With Love, Haugerud questions conventions with detached humor, yet he always treats his characters with profound compassion, delivering an eloquent and moving masterpiece on human relationships in the 21st century. — Paolo Bertolin
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Romeria, One of the standouts of Cannes 2025, Carla Simón’s personal exploration of the restlessness of a young woman without parents is a poignant example of the healing power of cinema.

After winning the Best Film in Berlin with Alcarràs (2022), Spanish director Carla Simón looks back into her own memories and heals pains from the past with her spellbinding third feature film Romería.

Eighteen-year-old Marina is an aspiring film student who sets out to trace the fate of her biological parents – who both died during the HIV epidemic of the late 1980s, early 1990s. Raised in Barcelona by her maternal grandparents, Marina visits her paternal family in Galicia, in order to obtain the paternity recognition documents that would allow her to apply for a scholarship. Guided on her journey by the pages of her mother's diary, Marina revisits her parents’ story of love and addiction...

Simón brushes with delicate touches the dynamics of a difficult family reconciliation and the motions of post-adolescent desire (the attraction between Marina and her cousin). While she initially draws from the tropes of summertime family dramas, Simón then turns Romería into a dreamlike fable where the past comes alive through the present thanks to the simple, yet enchanting true magic of cinema.— Paolo Bertolin
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Sentimental Value, This film may touch on the familiar theme of how artists draw from their own lives, but Renate Reinsve and Stellan Skarsgard bring incredible tenderness to a story that is ultimately about what children and parents never say to one another — and whether those lifelong silences can ever be broken.
Collaborating again with frequent co-writer Eskil Vogt (now also a successful director), Trier fashions a nuanced look at both a troubled family and a dysfunctional film industry. (Gustav’s comeback project will be distributed through Netflix, and the divisive streamer is the target of a couple of the screenplay’s better barbs.) Much of Sentimental Value takes place in the Borg family’s home, and an efficient flashback, framed as an essay Nora wrote as a girl, explains how they have lived in the house for generations… That slightly fading family home becomes an apt metaphor for the weathered bond Nora, Agnes and Gustav share, although Reinsve’s fragile performance articulates the festering resentment she feels toward her absent father.
Trier’s third picture to screen at Cannes, after 2021’s The Worst Person In The World’s breakout lead Reinsve won Best Actress, the reunion of director and star will entice arthouse crowds… and those seeking a smart, thoughtful tearjerker should be pleased with this sentimental but farfrom-mawkish film.” — Tom Grierson, Screen Daily
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: The President’s Cake, A young girl scrambles to prepare a high-stakes birthday cake for a dictator amidst the dangers and deprivations of the Gulf War in this irresistibly scrappy Caméra d'Or-winner from Iraq.

Nine-year-old Lamia (Banin Ahmad Nayef in a spectacular debut) lives with her grandmother and beloved rooster in the impoverished but tranquil Iraqi Marshes. Despite barely being able to feed themselves due to crippling food shortages caused by international sanctions, the family is randomly selected to prepare a cake as part of the forced national spectacle observing Saddam Hussein’s birthday.

From bucolic wetlands to bustling city streets, Lamia embarks on an ingredient-hunting odyssey that mixes equal parts sweet absurdity and bitter reality. Bartering with hawkers, dodging authorities, and begging the kindness of strangers, the young girl encounters the full gamut of humanity, from good to grotesque, as she approaches her ludicrous mission with innocent determination.

Director Hasan Hadi deftly evokes humour and open heartedness against a bleak background of oppression and war. Cinematographer Tudor Vladimir Panduru summons rich texture from the gorgeous locations, beautifully backed by a flowing soundtrack of traditional strings. — Adrian Hatwell
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: The Teacher Who Promised the Sea, A progressive teacher brings new methods to a village in Burgos on the eve of the Spanish Civil War, whilst in present day Catalonia a woman searches for answers as to the whereabouts of her great-grandfather’s remains.

Catalan filmmaker Patricia Font takes us to 1930s Spain by way of real-life educator Antonio Benaiges, assigned to teach in the small village of Bañuelos de Bureba. Intertwined with these flashback sequences are scenes from present day Catalonia and Burgos where Ariadna, the granddaughter of one of Antonio's pupils, seeks to locate ancestral remains at the mass graves of La Pedraja.

Antonio’s leftist leanings and critiques of the new Francoist government anger the more conservative townsfolk, particularly the town mayor. This is despite his daughter being one of the pupils benefiting most from the free expression encouraged by Antonio’s Freinet method teachings. Meanwhile, Ariadna teeters between hope and despair in her search for closure – a human vessel embodying the plight of a nation still wrestling with the consequences of a brutal conflict.

The closing credits remark that the remains of 12,000 people have been exhumed across the country. Like Ariadna, the film attempts to seek answers from the horrors of a war that took place almost a century ago – one driven by political sentiments that feel unsettlingly familiar as some of today’s most powerful nations shift towards fascism. — Matt Bloomfield
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Twinless, A grieving brother finds an unlikely connection at a support group for siblings who have lost a twin, but his burgeoning bromance threatens to turn into something darker in this uncomfortably sharp-witted comedy.

When his brother is suddenly killed in a car accident, estranged sibling Roman (Dylan O’Brien) suffers the unique pain of being permanently severed from his twin. Inseparable in childhood, the brothers drifted apart as adults, brother Rocky (also O’Brien) living out and proud in Portland while Roman lived a (decidedly hetero) tradie life in hometown Idaho. It seems he’ll never have the chance to work through his complicated feelings towards his twin until stumbling upon a bereavement group for just such a purpose.

There he meets Dennis (James Sweeney). Neurotic, sarcastic, gay, he’s the opposite that attracts as the pair bond over trauma and a deep need for attachment. They quickly become each other’s emotional support twin-surrogate, on call for late night grocery trips, afterwork bitch sessions, and road trip singalongs. But odd couple bliss can’t last, as Dennis has more than friendship in mind, Roman grapples with explosive anger issues, and dark secrets inevitably come to light.

Sweeny’s sophomore effort as writer, director, and co-star walks an entertaining balance between discomfort and hilarity. With finely calibrated performances from both leads, Twinless is witty, warped, and surprisingly warm hearted. — Adrian Hatwell
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: Went Up the Hill, An unsettling, sinister slow-burn thriller, Samuel Van Grinsven unites rising star Dacre Montgomery with Phantom Thread’s Vicky Krieps and New Zealand’s own Sarah Peirse for a supernatural chiller like no other.

In the icy, shadow-stricken world of Went Up the Hill’s Christchurch, it would seem that the death of Elizabeth, wife of Jill (Vicky Krieps), has taken with it warmth itself. The unexpected suicide of her partner has left her a hollowed-out shell – that is, until Jack (Dacre Montgomery), Elizabeth’s long-absent son, arrives at the funeral, apparently invited by Jill herself, though she does not remember doing so.

The circumstances of Jack’s long absence are unclear – all that is known is that Jack was given up for adoption at a very young age. Staying the night at Jill and Elizabeth’s oppressive, concrete-clad mountain abode, it quickly becomes clear that the spirit of Elizabeth has not yet departed – instead, she has gained the ability to possess both wife and son and is utilising this ability to linger and address the needs of either relationship. What initially seems to be a gift from beyond, however, begins to sour when long-hidden secrets of the past begin to emerge, and lines between the two begin to be crossed.

The sophomore feature of Samuel Van Grinsven, Went Up the Hill is a wintry, gothic affair, and a showcase for the untapped talents of Montgomery, who most will recognise as the golden-haired, ill-fated muscle mutt Billy from Stranger Things. Essentially a two-hander (with occasional, welcome interjection from Kiwi legend Sarah Peirse as Jack’s frosty, mystery-shrouded aunt), Van Grinsven tracks the trajectory of these two adrift people and the spirit between them – from unexpected refuge, to joy, to dread – with a purposeful, drip-fed escalation of tension. Questions of control, abuse and the lingering weight of past scars take hold, all while the usually pleasantly scenic Christchurch landscape is transformed into a suffocatingly claustrophobic ice prison. Van Grinsven’s muscular direction bears none of the flashy excesses of an emerging filmmaker – his vision emerges, stately, imposing and fully-formed. — Tom Augustine
label: Film & Media

description:
NZIFF: What Marielle Knows, Panic around a new digital Big Brother era underpins a clever, absurdist send-up of bourgeois hypocrisy, as a married couple are put on the spot by their daughter’s all-pervasive telepathy.

Germany has a thorny history with mass intelligence gathering, and a continued vigilance around data privacy – and anxiety. Director Frédéric Hambalek taps into it with satirical, ribald flair and a twist of the fantastical in a sharp domestic parable for a new era of global surveillance paranoia.

Julia (Julia Jentsch) is precariously close to a full-blown affair with the workmate she flirts with on smoking breaks. Her husband Tobias (Felix Kramer) dreams of getting even with a publishing house colleague who undercuts his authority in editorial design meetings. When their teenager Marielle (Laeni Geiseler) is slapped by a school friend over an insult, the impact leaves her with the sudden telepathic ability to see everything her parents do throughout the day – a development that spells disaster for the household, as dishonesty can no longer sustain the veneer of stable marital contentment.

As the family descends into a desperate, riotous war of manipulation, they must experiment with new moral codes. Is radical honesty and defiance the best course of action, or should they stifle egos and instincts in line with their preferred image? Better yet, can Marielle’s new powers be curbed? — Carmen Gray
label: Film & Media

description:
No One Rides Alone - Film Screening with Q and A, Special screening of No One Rides Alone the latest documentary from Silvereye Films.

Can someone with Multifocal Motor Neuropathy (MMN) ride the route of the Tour de France? That’s what Clive Phillips and four fellow veterans set out to discover during the Tour de MMN 2025. Following the 1955 Tour de France route, the team set out to see if they could ride in the wheel tracks of the first British Tour de France team

Would they overcome the challenges of the Alps, Mont Ventoux and the Pyrenees? Or would the impacts of this rare disease on Clive’s motor function and strength bring him and the team to a halt?

From Making the Most of Now and the team at Silvereye films behind the award winning “One Day Ahead”. No One Rides Alone, follows the team as they ride around France, connect with the rare disease community and learn more about MMN and the impacts it and conditions like it have.

Featuring double Paralympic gold medalist Ben Watson and Italian para-triathlete Ilaria Brugnoli, No One Rides Alone is a journey of discovery and an intimate portrait of how with team work, positivity and a willingness to be vulnerable we can achieve the seemingly impossible.

Set against the majesty of the French landscape and a remarkable historical achievement. No One Rides Alone tells an inspiring story that has lessons for us all whatever challenges we face. The film aims to raise awareness of MMN, inspire the rare disease community and raise funds for MMN Research.
label: Film & Media

description:
Reels for Meals: Prime Minister, September's Reels for Meals movie fundraiser is Prime Minister.
In August 2017, in the lead-up to national elections, Jacinda Ardern unexpectedly became New Zealand’s opposition party leader. She had just turned 37. Two frenetic months later, she was Prime Minister. Just before the final vote was in, she discovered she was pregnant. She would become only the second head of state in history to give birth while in office.
Ardern quickly became one of the most recognisable leaders in the world. She drew global attention from people craving a sensitive and compassionate approach to the critical issues of our time. In private, she struggled with being a mother and proving herself to a public skeptical of women’s leadership. A series of crises - the Christchurch massacre, pandemic lockdowns, and disinformation-fueled protests outside Parliament - would test that leadership and the feminine touch she brought to it. She resigned from office in January 2023, shocking her supporters and critics alike.
Going behind the scenes of her administration and her private life, Prime Minister follows Jacinda for seven years as she is catapulted to the top of New Zealand politics, becomes a feminist political icon, resigns suddenly from office and continues to champion the fight against isolationism, fear, and the distortion of truth. Intimate home footage shot by her husband and audio interviews that Jacinda did while in office give us unparalleled access. Along with in-depth contemporaneous interviews, these form the emotional backbone of the story, giving viewers an unfiltered window into her years in power.

All profits from this movie fundraiser go to the Lower Hutt Foodbank.
label: Film & Media

description:
Reels for Meals: Wicked: For Good, November's Reels for Meals movie fundraiser is Wicked: For Good.
Last year’s global cinematic cultural sensation, which became the most successful Broadway film adaptation of all time, now reaches its epic, electrifying, emotional conclusion in Wicked: For Good.
The final chapter of the untold story of the witches of Oz begins with Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo) and Glinda (Ariana Grande) estranged and living with the consequences of their choices.
Elphaba, now demonised as The Wicked Witch of the West, lives in exile, hidden within the Ozian forest while continuing her fight for the freedom of Oz’s silenced Animals and desperately trying to expose the truth she knows about The Wizard (Jeff Goldblum).
Glinda, meanwhile, has become the glamorous symbol of Goodness for all of Oz, living at the palace in Emerald City and revelling in the perks of fame and popularity. Under the instruction of Madame Morrible (Michelle Yeoh), Glinda is deployed to serve as an effervescent comfort to Oz, reassuring the masses that all is well under the rule of The Wizard.
As Glinda’s stardom expands and she prepares to marry Prince Fiyero (Jonathan Bailey) in a spectacular Ozian wedding, she is haunted by her separation from Elphaba. She attempts to broker a conciliation between Elphaba and The Wizard, but those efforts will fail, driving Elphaba and Glinda only further apart. The aftershocks will transform Boq (Ethan Slater) and Fiyero forever, and threaten the safety of Elphaba’s sister, Nessarose (Marissa Bode), when a girl from Kansas comes crashing into all their lives.
As an angry mob rises against the Wicked Witch, Glinda and Elphaba will need to come together one final time. With their singular friendship now the fulcrum of their futures, they will need to truly see each other, with honesty and empathy, if they are to change themselves, and all of Oz, for good.

All profits from this movie fundraiser go to the Lower Hutt Foodbank.
label: Film & Media

description:
Replica, Doc Edge Festival 2026

The perfect boyfriend doesn’t exist. Until he is coded.
Three women turn to AI lovers to fill gaps left by modern life. Qin, a factory worker in her twenties, creates the perfect boyfriend to escape isolation. Muna, a married housewife, uses AI to reclaim desire beyond the limits of her marriage. Sonya, independent and self-assured, treats AI as an experiment until it begins to unsettle her sense of control. As their relationships deepen, the film reveals the seductive pull of intimacy without friction, where affection is constant, responsive and designed to please. What happens to love when it no longer requires negotiation, and connection comes without consequence?
label: Film & Media

description:
Return to the Strange Land, Doc Edge Festival 2026

One last masterpiece for his lifelong muse.
Renowned choreographer Jiří Kylián’s craft has always reflected his own life. His final choreography made for his lifelong love and collaborator, Sabine Kupferberg, is a deeply personal performance that celebrates love, creation, and the ephemeral nature of life. Set against the raw, windswept beauty of the Dutch island of Terschelling, the shifting light and landscape mirror the fragile boundary between life and its end. Blending movement and memory with a subtle sense of the tragicomic, the film becomes an intimate meditation on longing, love and the fleeting nature of existence.

Screening Note: This film is preceded by the short film, Flashes in the Realm of Caves (11 mins).
label: Film & Media

description:
Seen The Film - Wellington, NZ. A Fundraiser for Te Aro School., We live in an age where, as parents and caregivers, there is more information than ever before. How much screen time is the right amount of screen time for our children? How best can we manage our children's daily meltdowns? Time in, time out, clear boundaries, feel all the feelings - what's best? We are hearing more and more reactive advice on how best to manage our children, yet we are missing the root cause and solution.
SEEN is a groundbreaking feature-length documentary that not only explores the transformative power of personal healing for parents, but also delves into the scientifically supported effects of such healing on parenting and its impact on child brain development.
movie trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bZPQXpw6kT0
movie website with all the beautiful info: https://seenthefilm.com/

others' and that when you leave the gig, you do so quietly to avoid disturbing our
neighbours.”
label: Film & Media

description:
Seized, Doc Edge Festival 2026

When journalism is raided, democracy is tested.
This film is a gripping, stranger-than-fiction investigative thriller that plunges audiences inside the troubling police raid on the Marion County Record. What begins as a shocking small-town incident quickly spirals into a story that reaches international headlines, exposing how corruption, politics, and decades-long tensions turned a quaint Kansas community into a microcosm of worldwide attacks on freedom of speech. Equal parts horrifying and hilarious, the film unfolds in real time through police body-cam and surveillance footage, revealing the raid’s chaos, the remarkable pettiness that led up to them, and the devastating personal toll on the reporters, including the tragic death of the paper’s 98-year-old co-publisher.
label: Film & Media

You can find more info below (including how to support if you can't attend).
NOTE: As we will be viewing and discussing potentially sensitive topics, this event will have an Open Door Policy. You may leave the venue at any time, for any reason, and will not be judged for doing so.
ABOUT THE DOCUMENTARY FILM:
"Jazz and decolonisation are entwined in this historical rollercoaster, that rewrites the Cold War episode that led musicians Abbey Lincoln and Max Roach to crash the UN Security Council, in protest against the murder of Patrice Lumumba."
WHAT IS CONGO WEEK?
Congo Week is on 19-25 October, where we commemorate the millions of lives lost in this ongoing genocide in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). It is also a time to celebrate the enormous humanity and environmental potential the beautiful country DRC has.
WHY ARE WE HOSTING THIS IN TE WHANGANUI-A-TARA, AOTEAROA (WELLINGTON, NEW ZEALAND)?
We are holding community film screenings during Congo Week to talk to each other as a community, and to help each other learn. As we support other causes/issues in Aotearoa/NZ and worldwide, we would like to increase solidarity for Congolese people.
We are buying, consuming, and benefitting from tech products/AI usage through child slavery and genocide of Congo. As long as there are customers of minerals found in the DRC, corporations will have an incentive to continue exploiting Congolese people for these minerals to be used in jewellery, batteries, e-cigarettes, and tech products like our phones and computers.
HOW MUCH IS THE TICKET?
The film screening is free but we appreciate koha for the Panzi Foundation (more info below).
WHY WOULD I WANT TO JOIN THE FILM SCREENING?
The film screening is for anyone keen to learn/watch a documentary film, wants to share their experience through optional group discussion, or wants to meet new people.
This event welcomes people from all walks of life who are willing to learn, listen, or contribute (LGBTQ+ friendly).
Between 5pm and 6pm: Set up tables and chairs
6pm-6:15pm: Karakia, health and safety, organisers' introductions, brief explanation on Congo Week
6:15pm-8:30pm: "Soundtrack to a Coup d'Etat" screening (people can come and go at any time)
8:30pm-8:45pm: Break/moment of silence
8:45pm-9:45pm: Group discussion with optional participation (each person to say their thoughts for 3 mins or less)
9:45pm-10pm: Pack down chairs and leave the room tidy
WILL THERE BE MORE IN-PERSON/VIRTUAL FILM SCREENINGS IN THE FUTURE?
Yes, will most likely be in 2026 instead of this year. We would love to collaborate with other people/groups, so we can share our skills and knowledge collectively.
I CAN'T ATTEND. HOW CAN I SUPPORT?
Please spread the word via social media stories, reposting, wheatpasting, or sharing to people who don't use social media (Instagram post here).
If you click RSVP, there is an option to donate without getting a ticket. We sincerely appreciate this.
You can RSVP to the 23 Oct 2025 film screening here.
If you click "Contact host" below, feel free to send us your email address and we can email resources after the event, e.g.:
Use refurbished tech products (instead of new ones)
Alternatives to Google/Microsoft mail/maps/calendar/forms/etc
Alternatives to Spotify/Apple Music
Reducing generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) usage at work/personal life
If using Google as your search engine, add "-ai" at the end of your searches (to stop showing AI results)
Actions and Instagram accounts to follow
WHERE WILL THE KOHA GO TOWARDS?
Koha that we receive will go to the Panzi Foundation.
The Panzi Foundation has opened hospitals, mobile clinics, and the City of Joy, a sanctuary where women learn healing, empowerment and leadership through their traumas. Rape is a weapon of war used against the Congolese people.
The Panzi Foundation is one of the largest African-led nonprofits and is committed to addressing the devastating impacts of sexual and gender based violence through a holistic, survivor-centred approach.
The Panzi Foundation was founded by Dr. Denis Mukwege, who is considered one of the leading experts in injuries of rape and was awarded a Nobel Peace Prize in 2018, 6 years after an assassination attempt on his life.
WHO ARE THE EVENT ORGANISERS?
This event is organised by ordinary community members affiliated with Te Tai-Tētēkura (an indigenous, youth-led group in Aotearoa/NZ).
Te Tai-Tētēkura is founded on the principles of revolution through education and restoration of power to the people. They hold a foundational community-based kaupapa that prioritises uplifting, connecting, and empowering our communities.
Te Tai-Tētēkura's founding is based on the socialist and revolutionary politics of the Black Panther Party, which rose to prominence during the Black Power Movement in the U.S. They combine the Black Panther Party's ideas with Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and their own landback and decolonisation principles.
Through community initiatives, Te Tai-Tētēkura shows the people that we as a community can take care of our society.
We stand in solidarity with indigenous peoples in Aotearoa/NZ, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and across the world facing injustice.
Please click "Contact host" if you have questions/feedback/concerns or if you can't attend anymore.

description:
Spin- A Multiformat Movie Marathon, What this is:
The event is a mystery movie marathon where each film plays on a different home media format over 12 hours from 10am to 10pm. There are three distinct sections, times are approximate. The event is R18, nothing is overly controversial but one film is a horror movie rated R18 for violence and nudity. The line up is subject to change but here is an indication:
Film:
Standard 8mm film - 10 minutes
Super 8mm film - 20 minutes
16mm film -90 minute urban adventure
Analog Video:
Betamax - 90 minute horror
VHS - 90 minute action
Laserdisc- 100 minute scifi action 

Digital Video:
VCD- 100 minutes comedy
DVD - 100 minutes ???
HD-DVD TBC
The film will be played on film projectors, the analog video on a CRT video projector (all going well) and the digital video on a digital video projector. All in either mono or glorious 2.0 stereo sound. Most projection is on a 2 meter wide screen.
There will be a half hour break between the analog and digital video sections. And smaller breaks during some format changeovers.
Seating provided will largely be camping chairs, if you want to bring your own chair you can- and there is a reduced ticket price option. This is intended for normal sized chairs, a camping chair, an office chair etc, not a huge armchair. There is limited space where you could bring your own beanbag up front, but you may be staring up at a sharp angle.

What this isn’t:
This is not polished professional event, it's a little bit improvised. We’re not screening in a regular cinema, we’re screening at Valhalla who are very kindly giving us a dark versatile space to work in. Technical issues may arise and we will keep on rolling, discarding formats and entire films in the line up if we can’t get them running. Some things have back ups, some don’t. No refunds, your ticket price is directly funding the event, and the event is an experiment. You can leave at any time, but please don’t yo-yo in and out every few minutes.
The presentation of the films is experimental, but the films for the most part are narrative drama films, not overly inaccessible.
Valhalla is a licensed venue so please do not bring in alcohol- If you do I will ask you to leave- with no refund! That would be awkward for both of us!

description:
The Antarctic Film Festival - Paekākāriki, An unforgettable evening of storytelling from the coldest place on Earth. The New Zealand Antarctic Society is proud to invite you to a presentation by Georgia Grant and a curated selection of captivating short films from the heart of Antarctica.

The films blend stunning documentary footage, curated by award winning filmmaker Anthony Powell, that reveals the continent’s stark beauty, unforgiving conditions, climate change, and penguin antics with stories captured by inventive and funny entries from the Winter International Film Festival of Antarctica’s 48-Hour Challenge, an annual showcase of creativity and resilience from those who winter-over on the Ice.

But before the films, we'll hear from Georgia Grant who is a sedimentologist within the Earth Sciences Surface Geoscience Department. Her research interests focus on climate variability in recent periods and past warmer climates, including Antarctic Ice Sheet and sea-level change. She analyses the statistical frequency of physical and geochemical characteristics of shallow-marine and deep-marine sediment cores. Come and join us for this informative talk and learn from Georgia's insights.

The films blend stunning documentary footage, curated by award winning filmmaker Anthony Powell, that reveals the continent’s stark beauty, unforgiving conditions, climate change, and penguin antics with stories captured by inventive and funny entries from the Winter International Film Festival of Antarctica’s 48-Hour Challenge, an annual showcase of creativity and resilience from those who winter-over on the Ice.

Before the films, hear from Ngawai Clendon, who will share her journey to the Ross Sea and the historic huts, along with the process and outcomes of that experience. Ngawai is in her third year at Victoria University of Wellington, studying New Zealand Sign Language, Te Reo Māori, Neurodiversity, and Education, with the goal of becoming a teacher who can communicate in all of Aotearoa New Zealand’s official languages while supporting children on the spectrum. Outside of study, she is a competitive marching girl with SWIS, New Zealand’s champion senior team based in Wellington.

Koha that we receive will go to the Panzi Foundation.
The Panzi Foundation has opened hospitals, mobile clinics, and the City of Joy, a sanctuary where women learn healing, empowerment and leadership through their traumas. Rape is a weapon of war used against the Congolese people.
The Panzi Foundation is one of the largest African-led nonprofits and is committed to addressing the devastating impacts of sexual and gender based violence through a holistic, survivor-centred approach.
The Panzi Foundation was founded by Dr. Denis Mukwege, who is considered one of the leading experts in injuries of rape and was awarded a Nobel Peace Prize in 2018, 6 years after an assassination attempt on his life.
WHO ARE THE EVENT ORGANISERS?
This event is organised by ordinary community members affiliated with Te Tai-Tētēkura (an indigenous, youth-led group in Aotearoa/NZ).
Te Tai-Tētēkura is founded on the principles of revolution through education and restoration of power to the people. They hold a foundational community-based kaupapa that prioritises uplifting, connecting, and empowering our communities.
Te Tai-Tētēkura's founding is based on the socialist and revolutionary politics of the Black Panther Party, which rose to prominence during the Black Power Movement in the U.S. They combine the Black Panther Party's ideas with Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and their own landback and decolonisation principles.
Through community initiatives, Te Tai-Tētēkura shows the people that we as a community can take care of our society.
We stand in solidarity with indigenous peoples in Aotearoa/NZ, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), and across the world facing injustice.
Please click "Contact host" if you have questions/feedback/concerns or if you can't attend anymore.

description:
Twin Peaks: Fire Walk With Me, "Faster and faster. And for a long time you wouldn't feel anything. And then you'd burst into fire" - Laura Palmer
TWIN PEAKS: FIRE WALK WITH ME.
DAVID LYNCH | USA & FRANCE | 1992 | 135mins | R18+| 4K DCP PROVIDED BY JANUS FILMS DISTRIBUTION
Join us for this very special community fundraiser screening of the prequel to the critically acclaimed series, "Twin Peaks".
ABC cancelled the original series after season 2 but a month later, Lynch announced he was "not yet finished with the material" and principal photography for the full length prequel film, began on September 5th 1991 at a caravan site in Snoqualmie Washington. Which became the "Fat Trout Trailer Park" where the story of the last 7 days of Laura Palmer begins.
Since its showing at the 1992 Festival De Cannes, no other Lynch film had polarized audiences to such an extent. Fans that wanted more "Cherry Pie" and "Donuts" from the TV show were served a much darker, unflinching and unforgiving work - in Lynch's own words, a movie about "the loneliness, shame, guilt, confusion and devastation of the victim". Derided by critics and many fans at the time it was a commercial box office flop.
Yet in the years since the initial reaction, a gradual wave of reappraisal and appreciation began. With time it's brilliance came into focus with growing acknowledgment, that the film is a more accurate, complex and powerful account of trauma. Combining the dramatic ferocity of Sherly Lee's tour de force and the beauty of Angelo Badalamenti's score, Lynch reclaimed full ownership of the material creating a harrowing, compassionate and enigmatic hymn to Laura Palmer.
As we approach the films 34 year anniversary and since Lynch's passing in 2025, it is now regarded by critics and fans worldwide, as a revered epilogue, essential predecessor to "The Return", and Lynch's most chilling, terrifying, and yet empathetic and humane cinematic masterpiece.
WHERE: The Roxy Cinema. 5 Park Road. Miramar. Wellington.
Cinema 1 - The big cinema upstairs with the massive screen, red italian leather sofas, and of course those red curtains!
WHEN: Wed 25th Feb 2026. Seating is unreserved so arrive early to check-in at the table upstairs, enter the raffle and get seated.
8:15pm - Doors close and the film starts. (no trailers)

COST: Tickets are $20 per person. (plus booking fee). This is a not for profit community screening put on for the pure love of Twin Peaks and the fans. All proceeds go to help pay for the cinema hire and licensing the film with any extras donated to charity. So spread the word and come celebrate "Twin Peaks Day 2026"!
TWIN PEAKS RAFFLE: Check-in at the desk upstairs and get a complimentary raffle ticket, to enter into the draw for 1 of these companion books.
The Secret Diary of Laura Palmer - By Jennifer Lynch with foreword by Mark Frost & David Lynch (paperback, 2012 edition)
Fire Walk With Me: Your Laura Disappeared - By Scott Ryan with foreword by Jeff Jensen (paperback, 2022 edition)
Laura's Ghost: Women Speak about Twin Peaks - By Courtney Stallings with foreword by Sheryl Lee (paperback, 2020 edition)
Cutoff to enter is 8:10pm and prizes drawn just before the start of the film.
RULES:
1. Tickets are per person. There will be NO door sales at the Roxy, so DO purchase it beforehand please. 
2. The film is classified R18+. All attendees MUST be 18yo + and have ID
4. The Roxy have strict no BYO food/drinks. Only Food/drinks purchased at the Roxy can be taken into the screening.
3. This is a safe, friendly, INCLUSIVE place. There is ZERO tolerance for discrimination, disrespect or creepy gross behavior of any kind. By attending you agree to the Code of Conduct.
4. Arrive early to enter the raffle before the cutoff if you want to be in it to win it. Good Luck!
Thank you and Happy Twin Peaks Day!

Widely considered the most experimental, provocative piece of art in the history of television, this cinematic masterpiece takes us on a surreal journey right back to the origin of the root of all evil.
So come join us at the Twin Peaks Townhall (aka: Newtown community centre). Bring some damn good joe, or a damn fine helmet, buckle up and strap yourself in for a stunningly beautiful and also horrendously horrific audiovisual maelstrom "through the darkness of future past that every fan longs to see."

Waifilmfest Presents Never Forgotten: the Marines of Masterton, Never Forgotten: The Marines of Masterton – Special Screening

After sold-out shows in May 2025, we’re bringing back Never Forgotten: The Marines of Masterton for one more special screening in Martinborough!

This feature-length local documentary tells the story of the United States Marine Corps’ 3rd Defense Battalion, who were stationed at Solway Showgrounds in Masterton in 1943 during World War II. Director Mark Pacey explores the Marines’ visit, the deep connections they formed with the local community, and their lasting legacy—including the journey to constructing a memorial in their honour.

Presented by Waifilmfest in partnership with Circus Cinema, Restaurant & Bar and the Wellington Historical Festival 2025, this is a unique opportunity to experience a powerful story of history, community, and remembrance.

Wairarapa Cinémathèque 2026 Presents METROPOLIS (1927), Metropolis (1927)
Sunday 5 April 2026, 7:30pm
Dir. Fritz Lang | Germany | 2h 3m | Silent | Sci-Fi | Drama

A towering achievement of early cinema, Metropolis is Fritz Lang’s visionary silent masterpiece: a film that continues to shape how we imagine the future.

Set in a vast, futuristic city sharply divided between privileged elites and oppressed workers, the story follows the ruler’s son as he meets Maria, a prophetic young woman who calls for understanding and compassion between the classes. What unfolds is an extraordinary spectacle of monumental design, groundbreaking special effects, and a deeply human moral vision.

Both epic and intimate, Metropolis is a powerful meditation on class, technology, and empathy. It is one of the most influential films ever made.

This special screening of METROPOLIS is presented in cooperation with the Goethe-Institut New Zealand.

Join the Wairarapa Cinémathèque. Memberships are available now, giving access to a curated programme of classic and significant films throughout 2026. Wairarapa Cinémathèque is dedicated to celebrating film as part of our artistic and cultural heritage. We value the communal experience of cinema, bringing people together through curated screenings, discussions, and the sharing of films of significance. description:
War on Drugs Film Screening, In remembrance of the victims of human rights violations and extrajudicial killings during the War on Drugs in the Philippines, please join us for a free/koha screening of "On the President's Orders" documentary in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

NOTE: For a list of trigger warnings, please see this document. Since we will be viewing and discussing potentially sensitive topics, the event will have an Open Door Policy, which means that you may leave the venue any time, for any reason, and will not be judged for doing so.
WHAT IS THE WAR ON DRUGS?
Spearheaded by the former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, the War on Drugs is a violent anti-drug campaign which killed nearly 30,000 Filipinos, most of which were urban poor (Karapatan, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch).
WHAT ARE EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLINGS?
"Extrajudicial killings, or extrajudicial executions, happen when someone in an official position deliberately kills a person without any legal process" (World Organisation Against Torture).
WHY IS IT IMPORTANT TO TALK ABOUT TODAY?
Human rights violations and extrajudicial killings are still on-going in the Philippines under President Bongbong Marcos, the son of the dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr. who proclaimed Martial Law in 1972, and Vice President Sara Duterte, the daughter of former President Rodrigo Duterte (Karapatan).
WHY WOULD I WANT TO JOIN THE FILM SCREENING?
The film screening is for anyone who is keen to learn about the War on Drugs, wants to share their experience during the War on Drugs (or something similar) through group discussion, wants to meet new people, wants to watch a Philippine film/documentary, or just wants to have snacks.
I WANT TO JOIN BUT I'M FROM TĀMAKI MAKAURAU / CHRISTCHURCH / THE PHILIPPINES.
We will stream the film through Zoom for viewers outside Te Whanganui-a-Tara, however, there may be internet and other technical difficulties during the event itself. Also please make sure to select the "Online" ticket option when RSVPing.
HOW MUCH IS THE TICKET?
The film screening is free but we appreciate koha for the venue/snacks/donations to Philippine non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
NOTE: This is an LGBTQ+ friendly event.

A fight for land, life, and the next generation.
Set deep in the heart of the Amazon, Indigenous chief Juma Xipaia fights to protect her people’s land from exploitation and destruction. Spanning years of activism and six assassination attempts, the film captures Juma’s historic appointment as Brazil’s first Secretary of Indigenous Rights, under President Lula. Hugo Loss, her husband and a former Special Forces ranger-turned-unwavering ally, leads dangerous operations against illegal gold miners. When Juma discovers she is pregnant, her battle takes on new urgency. Navigating impending motherhood, rising political responsibility, and Hugo’s high-risk missions, she is forced to confront the personal cost of resistance.

https://www.cordonbleu.edu/news/participating-in-the-award-winning-art-flow/en

For this special evening we welcome Lynn Blann, whose artistic journey traces back to Auckland’s vibrant creative culture of the 1960s and 1970s. During this influential period, shaped by the Peace, Anti-War, Women’s and Māori rights movements - artists, writers, poets and musicians gathered in galleries such as the renowned Barry Lett Gallery. Surrounded by the emerging works of figures including McCahon, Hanly and Twiss, Lynn developed a deep connection to the artistic energy of the time.

Today, working in acrylics, charcoal and pastels, Lynn continues to translate these influences into contemporary abstract forms on canvas. Her work reflects a lifelong engagement with New Zealand’s creative culture, recently recognised with a Merit Award at the 2025 Academy Prize for Visual Art.

The evening begins at Grazie Italian Restaurant with a welcome drink and an opportunity to meet Lynn and fellow guests. A thoughtfully curated three-course dinner follows, with dessert prepared by Chef Aman Khanna and the team at Grazie Italian Restaurant, celebrating the culinary artistry that complements the visual experience. Selected wines from Elder Pinot will accompany the entrée and main courses in tasting portions, offering guests a refined introduction to the character and craftsmanship of this distinctive New Zealand wine label.

As the evening unfolds, guests will gain insight into Lynn’s artistic journey and inspirations before continuing the experience with a guided tour through the hotel’s 'ArtFlow' exhibition spaces, where the artworks come to life within the hotel’s beautifully restored heritage interiors.

Event Programme:
• Welcome drink on arrival
• Mix & mingle - meet featured artist Lynn Blann
• Three-course dinner at Grazie Italian Restaurant **paired with a range 'Elder Pinot' wines.
• Guided ArtFlow exhibition tour with the artist

**Wine pairings will be served as tasting portions. Guests are welcome to enjoy additional wines from the Elder Pinot range, available for purchase by the glass on the evening.

'ArtFlow: Dine & Discover' offers a rare opportunity to experience art beyond the canvas bringing together artists, cuisine and conversation in an elegant and intimate setting.

We have hundreds of satisfied customers who have made some really exciting gins.

You’ll begin by foraging in the distillery gardens then we move to the gin-making room to learn about the gin making process and the ingredients involved. description: Capital of Kai, How did Wellington become a culinary paradise? Capital of Kai tells the story through 100 years of Wellington's food creatives, restaurant workers, and café culture. It's a love letter to the hospo whānau who have shaped the city. Walk through galleries of heritage treasures: the Green Parrot's working griddle, Hiakai's light-up signage, Il Casino's couch, Shanghai restaurant's 1980s menu, the Matterhorn café's cowbell. You'll see the arc from 1930s British hotel dining (roast mutton, boiled vegetables, milky tea) through European influences brought home by migrants and travellers, and the diverse cuisines - Chinese, Malaysian, Indian, Syrian, Greek, Māori - that define Wellington now. Hungry for more? Feed your curiosity at Capital of Kai.

description:

On Saturday 18 October, you can come and taste the beer in our Wild Workshop, the place where it was made. Brewers Pete and Dave will be on hand from 2pm to raise the first toast and tell you all a little about how this year’s blend came to be. We’ll also pull a couple of other goodies from the cellar to keep you and CLM company.

And, to top it off, our friends at Nomames Tacos will be here for the edible pairings.

This beer is the ultimate expression of Wild Workshop’s inner-city terroir, and the 2024 bottle is no different; a blend of five years of 100% spontaneously fermented brews, aged in French oak. The result is a complex and truly unique drop that harnesses the natural character of Pōneke.

We love this beer, and we’re so chuffed that other people do too - we’re very honoured that Chance, Luck & Magic, in its various vintages, has garnered global recognition and become one of our most prestigious creations:
Silver medals at both the 2023 and 2024 World Beer Cup (huge!)
Four consecutive gold medals at the New Zealand Beer Awards, as well as two trophies for Champion European Ale, and the Champion Beer title in 2022
Champion International Beer at the 2024 Australian International Beer Awards

The release of each new edition has become a landmark annual event for us, a chance to take a moment and appreciate the beautiful things that come from the wild workings of the environment.

Come and celebrate with us!

description:
Cheesemaking - Brie and Queso Fresco, Cheesemaking - Brie and Queso Fresco
The ultimate class in practical cheese making!   Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home.  You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.  
All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.
During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make.  You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.
A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Make Brie and Queso Fresco
- Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
- Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Begin the evening by exploring the art of fresh cheese-making — a simple yet rewarding process that will have you creating your own delicate cheese from scratch. Our experts will guide you through each step, from curdling the milk to shaping and seasoning your fresh creation.

Start your journey by making two fresh cheeses from scratch, guided by our expert cheesemongers. You and your partner will work as a team to curdle, shape, and season your own cheeses, learning the art of fresh cheese-making step by step.

Then, put your creativity to the test by building a cheese platter for two. Using a curated selection of artisan cheeses, you’ll design a board that balances textures, flavours, and perfect pairings. An array of charcuterie, fruits, nuts, and condiments will be provided, along with expert tips on plating and pairing to ensure your board is as stunning as it is delicious.

This intimate, hands-on experience is designed for anyone who loves good food, great company, and, of course, cheese!

The menu is vibrant and full of escapist flair. Start with coconut prawns and banana blossom kokoda, then dive into mains like mango glazed  pork rib rack or the tropical tofu paneer curry. Save room for dessert: pineapple upside-down pudding or a coconut rum fondue to bring the tropical fantasy to a sweet finale. A golden-age soundtrack sets the mood, featuring the smooth calypso of Harry Belafonte, beachy vibes from The Beach Boys, and sun-drenched classics by Astrud Gilberto.

description: Cognac vs Armagnac, Noble Rot sommelier Maciej Zimny has a undeniable passion for brandy, and he is yearning to share that with you. Maciej will guide you on an educational journey through this fascinating world focusing on the most prestigious French regions for brandy production: Cognac and Armagnac. He’ll provide detailed insight into the appellations, distillation and ageing processes, differences in oak maturation and why one region focuses on vintage expressions while the other ages blends for several years in barrel. But don’t worry, this isn’t a classroom affair—they'll be pouring 8 different spirits paired to a unique three-course menu to showcase Maciej’s knowledge, and he’ll even teach you the sommelier’s techniques for how to taste spirits correctly. Fall in love with brandy, find your favourite and next time you’re ordering a nightcap you can show off your new-found knowledge to your friends.

description:
Cooking class: Sri Lankan cutlets (Proceeds for disaster relief), Brought to you by Multicultural Collective and Aiyō, hosted by The Beer Engine
Sri Lanka has been hit with devastating floods, and thousands of families have lost their homes and livelihoods overnight. 100% of this events proceeds will going to disaster relief in Sri Lanka.
Come join us, learn the art of Sri Lankan cutlet-making, eat well, and make a difference at the same time. Good food. Good people. A real impact when it’s needed most.
Can You Stop at One? (We dare you!)
A Sri Lankan cutlet is history disguised as a snack. European croquettes crash-landed on the island centuries ago, and Sri Lankans didn’t just borrow the idea — they rewired it. Fish and potato for thrift, chilli and mustard seed for heat, curry leaf and lime for brightness, all sealed in breadcrumbs and fried in coconut oil. One bite tells you everything about the island: layered trade routes, colonial collisions, ingenuity in the kitchen, flavour turned into defiance. It’s super-tasty — crisp, molten, impossible to stop at one. 
Now you get to make your own and learn a bit about Sri Lankan culture.
We’re running a hands-on cutlet class where flavour is learned by instinct, not measuring spoons. You mix, taste, adjust, and chase that perfect balance of heat, comfort and citrus brightness. We bring every ingredient; you bring an appetite and the willingness to get your hands involved.
We’re being hosted by the crew at The Beer Engine — and their Yuzu Hazy is the move. Bright and citrusy, it slices through the richness and wraps around the spice in a way that makes you sit back and swear under your breath. When the frying’s done, we sit together and eat your creations with simple rice and Aiyō dhal. Big flavour, cold beer, good people. The kind of night food lovers remember.
For any questions, please email kiaora@multiculturalcollective.nz
label: Food & Drink

description:
Cooking: Homemade Chinese Egg Noodles and Pan-fried Buns, Cooking: Homemade Chinese Egg Noodles and Pan-fried Buns
Homemade egg noodles topped with your favourite sauce creates a tasty meal. Learn how to create Chinese style egg noodles that can serve as the basis for many traditional noodle dishes.  Create soft meat buns in the traditional Chinese style. Filled with succulent and juicy meat filling, these buns are perfect for a simple breakfast, lunch or snack.
Some communal ingredients will be supplied but a list of additional ingredients needed will be sent out when course numbers are confirmed. (approximate cost $35)
Please bring an apron, dish cloth, small rolling pin, sharp knife, tea towels and containers to take food home.
Note: course is not suitable for those who are vegetarian or gluten-free.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
make a selection of Chinese egg noodles and buns to take home
understand more about the Chinese egg noodle-making process
understand more about the Chinese bun-making process
feel more confident to make Chinese egg noodles and buns by hand at home
Note:  Our cooking courses are designed to provide a collaborative and immersive learning experience where learners often work in pairs and/or groups. description:
Cooking: Japanese Home-Style, Cooking: Japanese Home-Style
We will prepare simple, traditional Japanese home-style meals consisting of rice, soup, and a main dish (Ichijyu-issai). In each class, we'll make a different-flavoured miso soup along with a popular Japanese dish -- for example, teriyaki chicken or tonkatsu (crumbed pork cutlet).
  We'll introduce you to Japanese food that's easy to prepare, tasty, and made with simple fresh ingredients plus we'll show you how easy it is to incorporate tasty and healthy Japanese food into your daily diet.
All ingredients are included in the fee. You just need to bring an apron, a dish cloth, a tea towel, and a container to take your food home in. Don't forget your smartphone if you want to take photos!
By the end of the course, you’ll:
become more familiar with using Japanese ingredients
feel more confident to cook authentic Japanese-style dishes at home 
have the know-how to make delicious, well-balanced, and nourishing meals for the whole family.

description:
Crying Tiger, Charcoal smoke, sizzling meat, and you're in Nong Khai, a small northeast Thai town where families gather around the grill for Crying Tiger steak. Beef steak marinated 48 hours in coriander root, garlic, black pepper, oyster sauce, palm sugar, whiskey, and mandarin juice, char-grilled until the meat weeps with its own juices.
The chef grew up cooking this dish with family and friends. It arrives with sticky rice and a Northern Thai Isarn dipping sauce of tamarind, lime juice, ground chillies, and fresh coriander. Alongside: a sharp granny smith apple salad dressed with chilli and fish sauce, topped with prawns; and tom zapp, slow-cooked pork soft bones that melt into a soup fragrant with kaffir lime, lemongrass, and ground rice.
This is a three course set menu for $75.  Alcohol can be purchased separately.  Minimum 2 orders per table.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Curry Journey, Warm spices, layered flavours and regional traditions come together in a five-course exploration of curry across Asia. Each dish draws inspiration from a different place or technique, alongside  contemporary interpretations from the Dragonfly kitchen.

Courses are served one at a time, allowing guests to experience the range of styles, ingredients and spice profiles that define curries across the region.

The ticket includes a five-course curry menu, with accompanying sides and condiments where appropriate. Drinks are not included, but guests may purchase a specially created drinks match or other beverages on the day. Each guest also receives a curry-inspired treat to take home, created by Dragonfly’s friends at Asian Food Republic.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Daily Dose of Pies, Find Dough Bakery's wagon, wherever it appears across Wellington, guided only by word of mouth.  Each day the wagon settles in a different location (maybe even your own suburb) and serves a single pie flavour inspired by locally sourced ingredients and a spirit of experimentation. Once you've tracked the cart down, enjoy your pie on the beanbags or take it away. Location details will be seeded out carefully to pillars in the community of each suburb and shared informally. Check social media for its location, and even campaign for the wagon to visit your 'hood.
One week only, a different pie every day using local Wellington suppliers.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Dessert First, For Chef Shuchi dessert has always been the most emotional part of a meal. It's where people slow down, and where conversation softens. For this event you're encouraged to skip right to dessert for this five course dessert tasting menu each tied to a memory. Some from Shuchi's life, some shared in our collective memories, all rooted in the small, often overlooked moments that shape how we experience sweetness.

Raspberry panna cotta tastes like school lunches and summer berries. Rich brownie with hazelnut mousse is the sweet thing you crave after a long day. The lemon cake that became Le Ciel's bestseller without anyone realising. Apple crumble soufflé carries memories of Shuchi's grandmother. Passionfruit posset brings the taste of home from Tanzania. Each course is plated with technique and restraint, refined, but never losing its warmth or intent. You'll spend an evening in the warm, slow space where dessert deserves to be.

Your ticket includes five plated courses plus one palate cleanser.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Dinner With Dionysus, For this five-course degustation, Head Chef Nicolas Mentzas draws on his Greek heritage to present the flavours and textures of home through a refined, fine-dining lens. Often perceived as relaxed and informal, there is a quiet depth to Greek cuisine. It is shaped by season, coastline, mountain herbs, and generations gathered around the table.
Dinner unfolds as a carefully composed menu that honours tradition while embracing precision in one of the world’s oldest wine cultures. Rather than a shared feast, expect elevated dishes rooted in Greek culinary history, reinterpreted with elegance and detail. Each course is paired with Greek wines, highlighting distinctive indigenous grape varieties and the growing confidence of the country’s modern producers.
Throughout the evening, the Noble Rot sommelier team will introduce each pairing, exploring how Greece’s food and wine traditions complement one another in perfect harmony, at the highest level.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, an arrival wine, and seven Greek wines paired throughout the evening.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Discover Te Muna - Go Behind the Scenes in April, Join us for a full-day immersive experience in the viticulture, winemaking and wines of Te Muna Valley. Walk the vineyards, meet the producers, go behind the scenes and taste exceptional wines right where they are made.

Tickets are limited to twenty people to ensure that this is an intimate experience, taking you to places that are not normally open to the public.

Your tour begins with pickup from Martinborough Square, leading to a special start at Big Sky Wines. Kath and Jeremy will take you through a hands-on experience of their vineyard and winery. From there, visit the stunning Blue Earth Estate vineyard and olive grove. Margaret and Mike will entertain you with stories of their journey and explain how they grow their olives and grapes. You will then indulge in a long, relaxed lunch accompanied with a glass of wine. Some of the region's winemakers will join us to share their stories and answer your questions. The adventure continues with an insiders' look at the state of the art winery at Escarpment. Rowan will walk you through the process of how grapes are transformed into their wines. The day will conclude with a final tasting in Craggy Range’s private venue at their Te Muna Estate vineyard, where you will have the opportunity to revisit some of your favourite wines and chat with your hosts.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Discover the World of Chinese Milk Tea! Sip, Savor, and Explore a Cultural Icon!, Join us for a delicious journey into the world of Chinese milk tea — a beloved drink that blends flavor, tradition, and creativity. From classic black milk tea to trendy cheese foam toppings, discover what makes Chinese milk tea so irresistible!
Taste the Variety: Try popular milk tea styles from across China — including bubble tea, fruit teas, and unique toppings.
Learn the Culture: Uncover the story behind the rise of milk tea and its role in modern Chinese youth culture.
DIY Station: Mix your own milk tea creation with fun ingredients and take home your personalized blend!
Come sip with us at Mandarin Corner – where culture meets flavor!
label: Food & Drink

description:
Divine Spice Masterclass, Step into the world of chillies, spices, and bold flavours with team Apostle and craft your very own hot sauce. 

The evening begins with a short introduction to how their products are made, then you'll sample the range from Apostle alongside selected sauces from across New Zealand and Australia. From there, it gets hands-on: you'll experiment with fruits, vegetables, chillies, and spices to develop your signature blend, with guidance from the team and optional recipes for those who prefer structure. It's collaborative and fun, groups are encouraged, and there's plenty of sharing ideas and flavours. 

Your ticket includes around six bottles of your own handmade sauce, a kitchen notebook, grazing platters, drinks from Duncan's Brewery, and other treats. One alcoholic drink is included; non-alcoholic options available throughout.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Dragons Is My Uso, Chef Jessica Tang and legendary home chefs Litia Lefaoseu and Iutita Mallon are drawing on the century long fusion of Chinese and Samoan cuisine and the way food expresses love, ai, and alofa. In the late 1800s, small numbers of Chinese settled in Samoa and became part of a growing multicultural community. There they influenced local customs, made an enduring contribution to Samoan cuisine introducing contemporary favourites such as sapasui (chop suey), keke pua‘a (pork buns) and of course laisa (rice). 

Dragons celebrate this cultural and culinary fusion by showcasing these favourites and presenting new dishes highlighting the shared love of culinary staples such as taro and noodles, rice, fish, and pork, the magnificent spectrum of Chinese herbs, spices and flavours. Through cooking and sharing food together the chefs honour their culinary heritage, strengthen our connections to one another and celebrate the big and little moments in life. This is a shared-style meal, served banquet style on lazy Susan turntables. 
Dragons is My Uso was one of the sell-out hits of the 2024 festival - don't miss out!

Discounted tables for 10 available for $1000, so get the whole aiga together!
label: Food & Drink

description:
Due Isole, Join Chef Giulio Ricatti for an extraordinary evening celebrating the bond between two islands — Sardinia and New Zealand. Through a carefully curated nine-course dinner, this event offers a personal and heartfelt exploration of identity, place, and the connection between land and sea.

Raised in Sardinia and now at home in New Zealand, Chef Ricatti shares his story through a menu that bridges the wild, untouched landscapes of both countries. Each course is crafted exclusively with New Zealand ingredients, reflecting the rich bounty of our land and sea, yet inspired by the timeless traditions and bold flavours of Sardinian cuisine.

Accompanying the meal is an expertly selected pairing of wines from Sardinia and New Zealand, highlighting the unique characteristics of each region while celebrating their shared essence. The thoughtful combination of food and drink creates a dialogue between the two islands, offering diners a chance to taste the harmony of contrasts.

More than just a meal, this is an evening of storytelling. Chef Ricatti invites you to journey with him as he reflects on the places that have shaped his life and the meaning of finding a home across oceans. His philosophy of embracing the present moment is woven into every dish, making this event a sensory and emotional experience.

Whether you’re a lover of fine dining, an admirer of Sardinian culture, or simply curious about the connections between food and identity, this dinner promises a night of discovery. Step into the heart of two islands and savour their soul in one unforgettable evening.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Edible Idioms, Language and food belong together, add history and the story deepens into something altogether different. Lustre's taking the words we use every day and turning them into dishes. Cool as a cucumber becomes a palate cleanser, a piece of cake arrives as something entirely new, and every course speaks to the way culture lives in how we talk about food.

Seven courses of interpretation, each one teasing out a different idiom from around the world. There's a German one about sausage and indifference, an Indian one about something fishy in the pulses, moments where the kitchen challenges and entertains in equal measure. One surprise dish waits mid-evening, your job is to guess which idiom it is. The menu shifts with the seasons and the whims of Lustre's local farms, but the game never changes: food as language, language as history.

Your ticket covers the seven-course Lustrous banquet menu and an idiom-inspired arrival drink. Alcohol is available to purchase.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Escarpment Launch & Long Lunch, Be one of the first in the country to taste the 2023 vintage single vineyard wines from Martinborough's Pinot Noir superstars, Escarpment. From the gravels and windswept terraces of Martinborough, Escarpment has built a devoted following through word of mouth, shared by locals, championed by sommeliers, and remembered long after the last glass. 

Presented by winemaker Tim Bourne against the wild outlook of Boomrock's coastal position, you'll sample their wines paired with locally sourced wild ingredients including wild boar, Cook Strait snapper, tītī (mutton bird), venison, and Wairarapa cheese. 

The afternoon opens with Rosé on arrival and canapés of wild boar arancini and ceviche, then moves to a three-course long lunch. Expect leek, tītī, and Mānuka honey pasta with kawa kawa butter; tart cherry venison loin with purple kūmara gratin and Kikorangi Blue; and a Wairarapa cheese course with dark chocolate and blackberry jelly. Each course is matched with Escarpment's range, celebrating the magic of Wairarapa. Your ticket also includes return bus transport.
label: Food & Drink

description:
FILIPINO RESTAURANT WEEK, From October 20 to 26, 2025, Filipino cuisine will take center stage in Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch, and Dunedin for the first Filipino Restaurant Week (FRW). This week-long event introduces foodies to the rich and diverse flavors of the Philippines, with Filipino restaurants showcasing traditional and modern dishes that tell stories of heritage and community.
Participating restaurants will offer fixed-price menus featuring Filipino dishes like adobo, kare-kare, and halo-halo, giving diners a chance to experience the rich culinary traditions shaped by centuries of history. These menus highlight the unique fusion of indigenous ingredients and global influences in Filipino cooking.
Filipino Restaurant Week is a celebration of heritage, an invitation to unity, and a singular opportunity to savor Filipino cuisine. It celebrates New Zealand’s diverse cultural tapestry, deepens cross-cultural understanding, and strengthens community through the universal connection of food.
label: Food & Drink

Feast of Five Fishes, The ocean sets the tone for this five-course degustation, where fish and seafood take centre stage from first course to final bite. Drawing loosely on the spirit of the Italian Feast of Seven Fishes, this is a communal appreciation of the ocean's jewels, exploring the breadth and finesse of premium ocean produce with precision and care.

Each course reflects a thoughtful approach to seafood, drawing on seasonal catch and sustainably sourced ocean produce from around New Zealand. Expect considered technique and full use of the ingredient, treated with respect and imagination to reveal both delicacy and depth. The sommelier team has selected nine wines from around the world, fine Burgundy, savoury European whites, the occasional red, chosen to complement each expression of the sea.

description:
Field to Feast, Set on a working regenerative farm just outside Wellington, this long-table dinner brings you as close to the land that produced your meal as possible. The vegetables and pasture-raised meat will come directly from Mangaroa Farms and other local suppliers, shared in a cosy winter-dinner setting designed to spark conversation, curiosity, and connection around food. This is an interactive dinner experience that blends food, conversation, poetry, live music and inner-enquiry into one cohesive experience.
You're welcomed with whakawhanaungatanga, a warm welcome drink and canapés to acquaint your taste buds to the land. You'll gather in the yurt for a multi-course regenerative meal, with stories from the farmers and producers who grew the food. Woven through the evening will be live music from Casual Healing, poetry and reflective questions to open the table. Designed to foster a single, focused conversation, this Jeffersonian style dinner invites conversation across the table. You'll talk with strangers and leave with friends. 

Your ticket includes a snack and drink on arrival, a multi-course farm-sourced dinner complete with fresh baked bread, local sides and dessert with non-alcoholic beverages throughout the evening.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Finding Freedom: Wisdom for a Restless World, Overview


Discover a deeper meaning of freedom through practical insights from yoga wisdom and modern psychology.
Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Finding Freedom: Wisdom for a Restless World

If freedom means doing whatever we want, why do so many people still feel trapped, dissatisfied, or overwhelmed despite having so many options for pursuing pleasure?
In this interactive workshop, we'll explore timeless insights from ancient yoga wisdom alongside modern psychology to uncover a deeper understanding of real freedom—and practical ways to experience it in our everyday lives.

Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to be on time.
End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Shivananda
Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.
Read less

description:
Five Candles - A Birthday Retrospective Wine Tasting, It’s Alexia Urban Winery’s 5th birthday! Five years since we opened our doors to the public for the first time!

In that time we’ve released dozens of new wines, held scores of pop-ups, become a wine bar, and spent many hundreds of hours working towards becoming one of NZ’s few in-house Méthode Traditionnelle producers.

To celebrate we’re delving into our cellar and hosting a fun, informal tasting of some of the wines that have defined our urban winery (and us!). There’s a story behind each one.

Take a seat, hear the stories, and taste the love put into each wine as Alexia co-owners Jane (also winemaker) and Lesley spend an hour traversing five whirlwind years of a little urban winery on a Greytown back street.

Ticket includes all tasting pours.

Tasting:

Méthode Traditionnelle (an advance look at a yet to be released vintage)

2019 Chenin Blanc – that wine that showed us Wairarapa’s Chenin Blanc potential

2017 Chardonnay – 6 barrels that lit the urban winery fire

2020 Pinot Noir – the heartbreak grape from the loneliest vintage

2025 Lagrein (from the barrel) - the wine that’s been on Jane’s mind since the 1990s
