description:
Foraged Flavours : From Wild Greens to Plate, Foraged Flavours : From Wild Greens to Plate
~ Foraged Flavours: From Wild Greens to Plate ~

Step into a full-day, hands-on workshop at Mangaroa Farms, just 40 minutes from Wellington with Expert Forager Felicity Joy from Wild Botanica.

You’ll explore seasonal edible wild greens, learning to identify them, discover their properties, and turn your foraged finds into simple, delicious creations. In the farm’s fully equipped kitchen, you’ll make a range of hands-on preparations: fresh wild green spreads, infused butters, vibrant salads, and pickled or preserved treats, all designed to showcase the flavours of the season.

During the day, we’ll enjoy a shared wild feast together, tasting the seasonal dishes you’ve prepared in a relaxed, beautiful farm setting. This workshop is interactive, practical, and sensory, a chance to deepen your foraging skills, connect with nature, and celebrate the flavours of the wild. All ingredients, tools, and guidance are provided, so you can fully immerse yourself in the experience.

Perfect for those who’ve already attended Wild Botanica’s Foraging Workshops, this is the next step: taking your wild plant knowledge into the kitchen. Also suitable for total beginners, no experience needed.

When: Saturday 18th October
Time: 10 am – 3 pm (5-hour immersive experience)
Location: Mangaroa Farms, 40 minutes from Wellington

What’s included:
~ Full-day, hands-on experience: foraging, plant ID, cooking, and tasting
~ Access to a fully equipped kitchen and all tools
~ Guidance from an expert forager and cook
~ A shared wild feast using seasonal foraged ingredients prepared during the workshop
~ Educational insights into the nutritional, medicinal, and culinary properties of wild greens
~ Beautiful farm setting for a relaxed, sensory experience

Don't delay, call your friends and book your tickets now to avoid missing out:

https://www.wildbotanica.co.nz/collections/foraging-workshops/products/foragedflavours

p.s. book your tickets by 20 September to receive $20 off each ticket. Just use the code EARLYBIRD at checkout.

description:
French Cheese Escape, Step into a little corner of France without leaving Wellington.
French Cheese Escape invites you on a curated tasting journey through France’s most iconic French cheese and their regions. During this relaxed experience, you’ll enjoy a guided “fromage flight” featuring four carefully selected French cheeses - from creamy and delicate to bold and beautifully aged.
Each guest will receive a tasting passport and region guide, allowing you to travel from North to South, East to West and beyond, discovering the stories, traditions and terroir behind each cheese. Alongside your selection, you’ll enjoy artisan crackers or baguette and a perfectly matched paste to complement the flavours.
Come with friends, a date, or solo, and immerse yourself in the tastes of France at your own pace.

description:
From the Fisher's Mouth, Tom and Cole of Strait Speared have been supplying Wellington's best venues with spear-caught butterfish for four years using methods that have minimal impact on the ocean. Knowing your fisherman matters, and tonight they're coming to the table to talk you through why. 

A nine-course degustation using all the parts of the butterfish: fillets, collars, roe. Each preparation different, each one revealing something new about the fish and the selectivity it takes to harvest responsibly. You'll chat with the fishermen about their work, with the chef about different butterfish preparations, and with the people beside you as course after course unfolds. This is what transparent seafood looks like when the person who caught it is sitting across from you. 

Your ticket includes nine courses and one welcome drink on arrival. Additional alcohol can be purchased.

description:
George Motz: Burger Scholar, Calling all burger lovers. Class is in session as world-renowned smash burger expert George Motz brings a masterclass to Visa Wellington On a Plate. George has devoted his life to the humble burger, tracing its origins from 13th-century Mongolia to its current place as an American staple. He has made films, written books, and even taught university courses dedicated to the dish. In 2023, he opened Hamburger America in Manhattan, a tribute to regional burger styles and the stories behind them. Now he is bringing that knowledge to this burger loving city, at the bottom of the world, to share with all of you.

On stage, George will guide the audience through his ‘History of the Burger’. Expect a few surprises, along with the kind of detail only a ‘burger scholar’ can deliver. 

For the main event, George will cook his take on the Oklahoma onion burger live, sharing the methods that have earned him a global following. Every step is projected overhead, so you will not miss a thing. From the sizzling onions to the final stack, it is part cooking demo, part storytelling session, and a celebration of a classic. 

The evening wraps up with a Q & A, giving you the chance to ask George about his travels, techniques, and favourite burger joints. 

Whether you are a dedicated burger fan or just curious about what makes a great one, this is a chance to hear from one of the world’s leading voices on the subject.

Your ticket includes the presentation, live cooking demonstration and Q&A. No food will be served. A cash bar and merch will be available to purchase on the night.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.

description:
Hands-on Sourdough Workshop (Neil's), Sourdough for Beginners - $120 (paid via internet banking)
Come join us for a hands-on, in-person sourdough workshop at Willow Corner Collective headquarters (aka my home)! This workshop is currently the only hands-on sourdough workshop being offered in the Nelson region - I teach and demonstrate to you and then you get to mix and practice on your own dough as we go along.
Whether you're a seasoned baker or a beginner, this event is perfect for anyone looking to master the art of making sourdough bread, learning from someone who has 10+ years of experience. Perhaps you've found all the Youtube tutorials and Instagram how-to's overwhelming and are keen to learn via an in-person class. Then this is for you! I've baked hundreds of loaves in the last year alone, sold at a market, and hosted a pop-up shop. However, my passion really lies with teaching others to bake their own sourdough in their own homes, for their own families (or small businesses - one day!).You will be taught, demonstrated to, and then you get to have a go yourself; whilst learning my tips and tricks along the way. Plus we finish by sampling some delicious, fresh artisan sourdough with some favourite toppings!
You'll go home with all you need to make a good loaf of sourdough bread:
Knowledge
Student Guide, including recipes and troubleshoot guide
Bowl, liner, bowl scraper, and razor blade... all the tools you'd need to make sourdough
Dough made in class to bake the next day at home, to wow your family/friends
Confidence to continue the process yourself
Healthy, bubbling starter to continue your journey at home
Continued support and encouragement via our own private Facebook community group, for class attendees only
Note: You will have your dough to take home after the workshop that will need shaping around 6-8pm, so please ensure that will work for you that day.Also, please double check the date when booking. If for some reason you are unable to attend on the day, due to time constraints, I am unable to refund your ticket. I am happy for you to send someone in your place, though. In extenuating circumstances I may be able to hold your ticket for a future workshop; this is decided on a case-by-case basis.
*Payment to clear in bank account two days after ticket bought, after which time your ticket will be released on to someone else. Please pay immediately upon purchasing ticket.
**All workshop info you need to know ahead of time is in the confirmation email. Please ensure you read this down to the bottom.
***I recommend you already have a pair of digital scales, and a cast iron dutch oven at home to bake your loaf with as this makes the best, artisan sourdough, with great rise. Alternatively, a large, lidded casserole dish or enamel roasting pan work also. (The lids are a necessity).
"Sarah’s sour dough class is for real life! Achieve beautiful delicious bread easily in your own kitchen. Sarah teaches you how to fit sourdough into your busy life. She clearly and passionately gives the essential information, tips and tricks to make your own loaf. I loved getting to have a go at each step in the process. I love Sarah’s catchy philosophy “The goal is good bread, not perfect bread.” This took all the pressure off, for me, and I left the class empowered with all the knowledge and skills needed to give it a go at home. I appreciated the thoughtful and well prepared resources Sarah gave us. Thank you!" - Megan
"Sourdough with Sarah was a delight! From feeling overwhelmed and giving up on the idea of ever making my own loaf of sourdough, to dancing with joy as i watch a beautiful perfect sourdough loaf get nice and golden in the homewood stove!The information was packaged in bite sizes with hands on practice in between, where we all got to experience each step of the whole process, which was cleverly condensed and prepared so that despite normally having waits in between, we were able to see it all play out in a short few hours!The process was beautifully organised with attention to detail that had us fawning, came away feeling so blessed and privileged!Sarah's glowing personality made all the information feel easy and palatable, it was so fun!Such a lovely time, great environment to learn with ease." -Melody

description:
I-Sarn Thai KanTok, Join Daeng from Tuk Tuk Thai for a deeply personal culinary journey to the heart of E-Sarn, the north-eastern region of Thailand she once called home. This one-night-only event celebrates the traditional Kan-Tok style of dining – a communal meal served on handwoven bamboo trays and shared amongst family and friends. This event is made to be shared, the ticket price is for a shared menu for two. 

Growing up in the small town of Tha Bo near the Mekong Delta, Daeng’s childhood was filled with stories of rice farming, village generosity, and dishes cooked from what the garden offered. In E-Sarn, meals were acts of love, shared daily around the Kan-Tok with laughter, music, and warmth.

Now, Daeng invites you to gather at her table and experience the flavours of her upbringing. You’ll be served nine traditional dishes on a beautifully crafted bamboo tray, designed for sharing, just as they are in her village.

On the Kan-Tok:
Hor Mok Salmon – Steamed salmon in banana leaves, marinated with herbs, spices, and coconut milk
Mok Nor Mai with Pork Belly – Pork belly steamed with bamboo shoots
Larb Gai – A celebratory chicken mince salad with fresh herbs and toasted rice
E-Sarn Sausages – House-made, spiced and fermented in true north-eastern style
Nam Prik Tomato – Roasted tomato dipping sauce with chillies, garlic, and shallots
Som Tum – Green papaya salad with a sweet, sour, spicy kick
Sticky Rice – Soaked overnight and steamed in traditional bamboo baskets
Fresh and Steamed Seasonal Vegetables – To enjoy with sauces and mains

Dessert:
Kanom Chan – Thai layered jelly cake
Kanom Mun – Tapioca and coconut pudding

Pull up a seat at Daeng’s table and discover the stories, flavours, and traditions that shaped her childhood.
Single tickets or odd numbers unable to be catered to.

description:
Introduction to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Workshop - August 2026, Overview




A 2-day introductory, experiential ACT workshop for clinicians.
Over 1000 randomised control trials have clearly demonstrated ACT’s efficacy for a wide range of diagnoses and life problems. ACT helps people make space for their thoughts and feelings while moving towards the life they value. At this experiential workshop you will establish a foundational understanding of Psychological Flexibility, develop skills for using ACT and learn about Relational Frame Theory (RFT).
Over the two days you will learn how to:
meet clients where they are and foster their willingness to change
help clients hold their painful thoughts and emotions gently; identify and actively move towards their values; and develop awareness of the present moment and their capacity to notice it
develop a therapeutic relationship in which support can be provided compassionately and flexibly
formulate life struggles from an ACT perspective
practice ACT exercises and relate the concepts back to your own life and clinical experiences.
This workshop is fully catered with vegetarian food.
Giselle Bahr and Ben Sedley are clinical psychologists and co-founders of ACT Wellington. Since being trained and supervised by many of the world’s leading ACT therapists and researchers, ACT has been the foundation of their practices for many years. Giselle and Ben have both worked at Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, in Private Practice with adults and adolescents, and trained clinical psychology students at Victoria University of Wellington. Giselle has developed and facilitated groups introducing ACT to parents and adults, and served on the Board of ANZ ACBS. Ben wrote Stuff That Sucks: Accepting what you can’t change and committing to what you can, Holding the Heavy Stuff: making space for critical thoughts and painful emotions, and Stuff That’s Loud: A teen’s guide to unspiralling when OCD gets noisy (with Lisa Coyne). He is also an ACBS Peer Reviewed ACT Trainer.

description:
Keiko Kuwakino + Joe McLeod, For one night only, two forager-chefs from opposite ends of the Pacific will bring you - Kai meets Shoku - as they cook together at Pipitea Marae, for an all inclusive six course dinner that could only happen in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

Pipitea Marae has always been a place of gathering and welcome. For generations, Te Āti Awa ki Te Whanganui-a-Tara has offered manaakitanga to those who arrive by sea, by land, and now, from across the Pacific.

On 29 August, that tradition continues with a dinner bringing together two chefs whose life's work is rooted in the same conviction: that honouring culture and history is best done via the puku.

The story of this harbour is one of guardians, pathways, and the meeting of worlds. Te Āti Awa have long understood that the sea connects rather than separates. What began as a relationship across the Pacific between Te Āti Awa and Japan finds its expression at the table, where two Indigenous cultures share their stories through food.

Chef Joe McLeod (Ngāi Tūhoe) brings more than 40 years' experience as an international chef, alongside six decades spent researching, recording, and reconnecting Mātauranga Kai Māori, returning traditional food knowledge to marae across Aotearoa. One of the foremost authorities on traditional Māori cuisine, Chef Joe's kaupapa is grounded in the belief that food carries whakapapa, and that restoring a people's relationship to their kai is an act of cultural survival.

Chef Keiko Kuwakino travels from Satoyama Jujo in Niigata, Japan, where her Michelin-starred restaurant reflects a practice rooted in wild mountain vegetables, fermentation, and the rhythms of Japan's snow country. Her cooking begins with the land she forages. For Keiko, cuisine starts with the land itself, her role simply to listen carefully to nature and translate its story through food.

Hosted by Te Āti Awa at Pipitea Marae, Kai Meets Shoku is a partnership between Wellington Culinary Events Trust, Te Rūnanganui o Te Āti Awa, and E Kai Māori, supported by MBIE.

Your ticket includes five courses, matched beverages for all courses, and Māori and Japanese entertainment

description:
Lunch Speaker Series, Noble Rot invites you to enjoy a relaxed lunch in style. While away your afternoon with a leisurely three-course menu as they keep the wine flowing amongst you and your friends. They've lined up two incredible guest speakers at the forefront of the wine industry to entertain you with their stories, knowledge and insights into current trends in a relaxed but intimate atmosphere. You'll wish all learning was done this way. It’s the perfect excuse to treat your friends, your mum or your date.
 
Guest Speakers & Dates:

Saturday 9th — ‘Small Region, Big Sky’
Katherine Jacobs and her husband Jeremy embarked on a dream to produce some of Martinborough’s finest wines from their special vineyard in Te Muna, and they’ve achieved great success! Katherine will speak about upcoming trends, big dreams and hidden secrets in our favourite region’s wine scene.
 
Saturday 23rd — ‘A Rosie Afternoon’ 
Enjoy the company of Rosie Finn of Neudorf Vineyards, second generation of one of New Zealand's most prestigious wineries in Nelson. You’ll have the opportunity to ask Rosie all about current trends as she combines the story of her family winery’s historic roots and its impact on the landscape of New Zealand fine wines.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Madeira My Dear, Madeira has been too often overlooked. It sits in grandmother's cabinet waiting for cooking or forgotten entirely. But Madeira is built to last, it's a quietly complex wine that deserves discovery. Noble Rot will spend an afternoon proving it to you.
The afternoon begins with a welcome cocktail before settling into a three-course long lunch served sharing style at the table, in the traditional Mediterranean spirit. Generous plates are designed to encourage conversation and a slower pace. Across the meal, guests will taste six Madeiras, exploring the spectrum from dry and saline expressions through to richer, caramel-toned styles, with insight into grape varieties, ageing methods, and the oxidative character that gives Madeira its unique flavour profiles and remarkable longevity.
Your ticket covers a themed arrival cocktail, three generous sharing courses, and six Madeira wines paired throughout the afternoon.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Maille Sunday Kai, Escape the winter chill and head along to Cuba St Tavern for some Sunday Kai with Maille Mustard, running every Sunday of August. Each week features a different delectable roast, served with either a Maille Dijon Bloody Mary or warming mulled wine, and finished with a house-made dessert. Sunday has never tasted so good! Bookings available from 1pm.

$50 for 2 courses
$65 for 2 courses inc a Maille Bloody Mary or House made Mulled wine

Menu
Every Maille Sunday Kai event will offer a vegetarian option of eggplant parmigiana with buffalo mozzarella, Maille Dijon mustard, tomato ragù, garlic potato and broccolini.

3 August
Free-range roast porchetta served with garlic potato, creamed spinach, broccolini, Yorkshire pudding, Maille wholegrain mustard jus and apple sauce.
Dessert: Sticky toffee pudding with custard.

10 August
Roast duck breast served with duck fat roast potatoes, Chinese broccoli, mushrooms, Yorkshire pudding, and Maille Dijon mustard and onion cream.
Dessert: Dark chocolate torte with orange mascarpone.

17 August
Conscious Valley roast lamb shoulder with garlic roast potatoes, honey-glazed carrots, minted peas, Yorkshire pudding, Maille wholegrain mustard jus and mint sauce.
Dessert: Bread and butter pudding with ginger gelato and crème anglaise.

24 August
Half a roast chicken with duck fat roast potatoes, garlic green beans, cavolo nero, Yorkshire pudding, chicken schmaltz and Maille mustard gravy.
Dessert: Steamed honey pudding with custard and honey gelato.

31 August
First Light roast sirloin served with honey-glazed carrots, duck fat roast potatoes, cabbage and bacon, Yorkshire pudding, horseradish, Maille Dijon mustard and jus.
Dessert: Chocolate fondant with vanilla bean gelato.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Maille à Maille, Since 1747, Maille has been synonymous with French gastronomy. The supplier to the court of King Louis XV, it remains one of the most recognised French condiment brands in the world. This August, Maille teams up with Le Bouillon Bel Air for Menu du Jour: a special collaborative bistro series served every Sunday throughout the month.

Step into a classic Parisian-inspired dining experience and enjoy a three-course menu where Maille's signature mustards feature throughout each dish. Begin with a leek terrine dressed in a Dijon and wholegrain Maille mustard vinaigrette, followed by Poulet Gaston Gérard—chicken in a rich Maille mustard and cream sauce. Finish with a dark chocolate mousse accompanied by brown butter crumble, poached pear, and a mustard-sesame-honey tuile. This exclusive three-course menu is available for $85 per person, every Sunday in August.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Mastering Paella Workshop, Learn to authentically create Paella by Spanish Embassy Special guest chef, Edrick Corban-Banks, from Casa Paella.
In collaboration with the Embassy of Spain in New Zealand and Casa Paella, we are proud to offer a one-day workshop taught by the award-winning chef, Edrick Corban-Banks.
Chef Edrick is the owner of Casa Paella, Casa Paella holds the official ICEX “Restaurants from Spain” quality seal, recognising its place within Spain’s international network of restaurants committed to authenticity, quality, and the promotion of Spanish gastronomy. This is rare opportunity to learn the culture and traditional Valencian techniques of Paella from a master artisan.
You will spend the day in Teams of 2 as Chef Edrick guides you through the creation of the award winning Arroz con Salmón.
Date: 25th July
Time: 9:30am – 3pm (light lunch is included with a glass of Albarino white wine)
Location: Level 2, 52 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington
Allergies: Ingredients in this class contain the following allergens: Fish, Shellfish/Crustaceans, Molluscs, and Sulphates. This dish will be Gluten Free.
You Will Create:
Arroz con Salmón (Salmon Paella featuring Ōra King Salmon)
First developed in Tasmania using Petuna ocean-grown salmon and awarded the
Tetsuya Wakuda “Best Plate” prize at Taste of Tasmania, this paella is designed as a
technique-led masterclass in stock construction, rice absorption, and heat
management. A concentrated seafood fumet—prepared from shellfish and fish
frames—builds depth and structure, allowing the character of premium local salmon
to remain the centre of the dish.
Course Details: During the workshop, you will learn the following skills:
Prepare a fresh seafood stock using fish and shellfish frames
Build flavour through sofrito, saffron, paprika, and olive oil
Cook Valencian paella rice correctly so each grain remains separate
and full of flavour
Manage heat, evaporation, timing, and liquid levels
Understand the difference between cooking “rice with seafood”
and creating a true Mediterranean rice dish
Develop the prized socarrat — the golden crust at the base of the paella
Finish and serve your paella in the traditional shared style
Course Includes: All ingredients and equipment supplied, at the end of the class, participants will sit down together and enjoy the paella they have created with a glass of Albarino white wine.

What is a Le Cordon Bleu Workshop? A Le Cordon Bleu Workshop is a hands-on culinary training session delivered in our professional teaching kitchens. Be personally guided by world class chefs and taught key techniques step-by-step, with chef feedback throughout. This workshop includes a light lunch, and is designed to give you skills you can repeat confidently at home or in a professional setting.
Contact Details: +64 4 472 9800 | nz@cordonbleu.edu
label: Food & Drink

description:
Mediterranea, At Cicio Cacio Osteria, the Mediterranean comes to the table in an intimate dinner shaped by memory and place. Inspired by the owner's childhood on a Mediterranean island, this dinner traces a path from Italy to Spain, across Greece and into the Middle East, with dishes from each region reflecting the shared spirit of the Mediterranean: the sun, the sea, the music, the nostalgia, the being in the moment. The food is uncomplicated and entirely enjoyable, simple, fare focused on freshness and simplicity, letting the ingredients speak for themselves. Expect the most perfect hummus with grilled pita, the best Spanish tortilla, uncommon seafood like octopus and sardines, couscous, lamb, and goat, pastas, and colourful salads, a true insight into the Mediterranean spirit. 

You'll be seated at a long communal table in front of a real fire for a progressive nine-course menu, each plate paired with a matched wine selected to reflect its origin and character. Throughout the evening, the chef shares stories behind the dishes, offering insight into flavours, traditions, and personal history. You're invited to come into the kitchen and share the secrets of each recipe, cooking alongside the chef. A final musical touch ends an evening dedicated to the beauty, spontaneity, and simplicity of the Mediterranean. 

Your ticket includes nine courses, nine matched wines, storytelling, hands-on cooking, and recipe sharing.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Michelin Star to Martinborough, Join celebrated Chef and Union Square owner Adam Newell for a once-in-a-lifetime culinary experience. Take a journey through four decades of his exceptional career, including his Michelin-starred tenure at the renowned Fulham Road Restaurant in London. This exclusive event will offer an intimate exploration of Chef Newell's evolution as a chef and restaurateur, showcasing iconic dishes from four pivotal periods in his career.

Set in the elegant Napoleon dining room inside the historic Martinborough Hotel, each course represents a defining moment in Chef Newell’s career. Paired with fine wines selected by in-house Sommelier Carl Fraser, this evening is designed to be a feast for both the palate and the mind.

Course 1: 1980s – Claridge’s Hotel, London
A taste of the refined sophistication from one of London’s most prestigious hotels.
Course 2: 1990s – Le Gavroche, London
A nod to the classic French techniques that helped shape Chef Newell's early career.
Course 3: 2000s – Zibibbo, Wellington
A celebration of New Zealand’s finest ingredients and a significant step in his culinary journey.
Course 4: 2010s – Union Square Bistro, Martinborough
Reflecting his achievements at Union Square, the course that represents his current culinary vision.

This evening offers guests a unique chance to experience the evolution of one chef's journey through extraordinary dishes paired with wines that elevate each moment.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar, Alexia Urban Winery x Greytown Distilling Company present: Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar

Aperitivo – it’s the Italian pre-dinner beverage ritual designed to open the palate, open the stomach, and open the conversation.

Wander past any Italian bar as the sun goes down, and you’ll see the locals sipping martinis and negronis, while engaged in animated discussion!

The common ingredient in these cocktails…and conversations is vermouth – a delicious, aromatic, botanical-loaded, fortified wine. Wine, you say? That’s where we come in. Alexia has been working with Greytown Distilling to create a vermouth for them right here in Greytown, and they’ve asked us to host something fun to celebrate its release for the Greytown International Cocktail Festival!

We’re channelling vermouths Italian roots and transforming into a little pop-up Italian neighbourhood vermouth bar!

We’ll be serving the most intriguing (and cutest) cocktail flight in town to showcase the beauty and versatility of vermouth… the ‘vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray’ - a cocktail broken into three micro parts: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni.

All the Alexia wines will be available too, of course, and it’s Italian all the way in the kitchen, with guest chef Caleb Kloeg turning out crispy arancini and gelato soft-serves so delicious you’ll be transported to Italy.

Cocktail inspired? You’re in luck. Greytown Distilling will have a little pop-up shop on the night, selling all the essential cocktail-making accessories too.

It’s neighbourhood Italian bar vibes on a Greytown backstreet, and we can’t wait… so get on your vespas, pump up the tyres on your Bianchi, rev those Fiats and get to Alexia!

Vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray

The most intriguing cocktail in town…a single cocktail broken into a micro-flight showcasing the beauty and versatility of vermouth: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni. Shrunken, not stirred…

Essential details: 4pm – 8pm, Friday 27 March, Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown. No bookings required, just turn up. GF? Yes. Vegan? Yes. Leashed dogs ok. This is a rain or shine event, so don’t miss out!

The Greytown International Cocktail Festival is proudly sponsored by Greytown Distilling Co and The White Swan.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Mystery Feast on Mischief Night! Halloween dinner with Chef Max Gordy
Supporting Kaibosh., Step inside, if you dare... on the eve of Halloween. It's a Mischief Night!
A chilling murder mystery unfolds over a hauntingly good three-course Halloween dinner by Chef Max Gordy!
On 30 October, gather your cleverest friends and find your darkest ghoulish attire
Who will crack the case first: the Detectives or the Villains?

Expect twists, laughter, and a touch of fright
with spot prizes through the night — plus a reward for the best-dressed.
Award-winning chef Max Gordy ( @grazewinebar ) will conjure up a frightfully delicious Halloween-themed feast.
Your ticket includes one complimentary alcoholic beverage (with more available to purchase on the night).
Every ticket sold helps Kaibosh ensure that no good food is left to die.
TICKET TYPES
Bring a team of six to solve the mystery and devour a fiendishly good feast for $666.
Have a frightening four-some? Book a table for $444.
Spooky single seats available for $111... we will seat you at a mystery table...
VENUE
60 Dixon Street is up a flight of steep steps – with only one way in.
What is Mischief Night?
In parts of Pennsylvania and New Jersey in the eastern USA, 30 October is called “Mischief Night.” The tradition refers to the eve of Halloween in which children and teenagers celebrate the holiday one night early with pranks, tricks and more. While in New England, some call it Cabbage Night...
label: Food & Drink

description:
Netherfield Ball, Step into the enchanting world of Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice at Homewood, where the timeless elegance of a Regency-era ball comes to life. This evening of romance, music, and culinary delight invites you to relive the iconic moments of Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy’s fateful meeting.

Guests will be greeted with crafted cocktails inspired by love potions, showcasing ingredients from some of the finest distilleries in New Zealand and the United Kingdom. As the evening unfolds, indulge in a carefully curated selection of canapés, created with fresh ingredients sourced from Homewood’s own garden, evoking the flavours and charm of the Regency period.

The grand setting of Homewood, the esteemed residence of the British High Commissioner, will transport you to a bygone era. With the glow of garden lighting, live music filling the air, and an atmosphere brimming with romance, you’ll feel as if you’ve stepped into Austen’s world. Dancing will play a central role in the evening, allowing guests to immerse themselves in the grace and grandeur of the Regency social scene.

Whether you’re an Austen devotee, a fan of Bridgerton, or simply drawn to the allure of historical elegance, this event promises to captivate your imagination and senses. Don’t miss this rare opportunity to be part of a night filled with charm, sophistication, and timeless romance.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Nyumbani: A Taste of Tanzania, Journey through the heart of Tanzania with dishes that feel like home - comforting, bold, and full of love. This special five-course degustation is created by Chef Shuchi Bhardwaj, a baker who grew up in Tanzania and carries its flavours, traditions, and warmth in her heart. 
Whether it’s the warm embrace of coconut-infused stews, smoky grilled meats, or fragrant spiced rice, each course is a reminder of how food connects us. This menu brings authentic East African flavours to the table, reimagined in a modern way that feels like home. Each course is matched with a carefully selected wine to enhance the flavours of the dish. Expect generous hospitality and a setting that feels like stepping into a Tanzanian family gathering.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Once Upon a Time in Wellington, We are hosting some very special guest chefs over a 2 week period, with each chef joining us for a 2 night collaboration. Their identities won't be reveiled until the day before via Instagram. Speculate, believe the rumours, start the rumours for all we care! Three local legends, one from outside Wellington, and a roster that reads like the highlight reel of modern cooking in this country. It will be a small a la carte format during our usual trading hours.  Walk ins are encouraged but bookings for groups of 4 or more it is highly recommended. The menus will be small and à la carte throughout. 
Guest #1 (4-5 Aug) The Taipan
Our first guest is a previous collaborator, you know him, you love him, we love him. If you've eaten his food before, you know subtlety isn't on the menu. Expect bold and aggressive flavours, and probably some offal. 
Guest #2 (7-8 Aug) The Kodiak Bear
Lover of restaurants and a wizard with words on paper. We are very excited to introduce this guy and give him a creative platform to show Wellington something special from a unique perspective. 
Guest #3 (12-13) The Suzumebachi
Joining us from the Hawkes Bay, This man brings a tempered approach to cooking from his time cooking in Japan. Now an established award winning chef in New Zealand, and someone we consider at the pinnacle of modern cookery in this country. Expect Japanese flavours and techniques utilizing the some of the best produce NZ has to offer.
Guest #4 (14-15) The Bighorn Ram
With many curls in his horns, this guy has been pivotal and arguably one of the most important chefs Wellington has ever known, setting the stage for many of us who followed. An award winning chef who pioneered modern cuisine in this City, you wont want to miss this. Expect a measured and wise approach to fun flavour combinations with precision.
label: Food & Drink

description:
Paint and Wine Night - Flowers Say It All, Looking for a creative night out in Wellington? Join us for a fun beginner-friendly adults painting class in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. It’s the perfect excuse to switch off, get creative, and try something a little different.

Whether you’re coming along solo, planning a date night, or organising a catch-up with friends, Paintvine is all about good vibes, creativity, and having fun while you paint – you might even surprise yourself with what you can create!

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit! Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

description:
Paritua, The Botanist & Sea Shepherd!, We've teamed up with Paritua Vineyard and Sea Shepherd NZ to bring you a fantastic evening of dining and drinking excellent wine! We'll be serving a four course plant based dinner, matched with Paritua wines, in support of Sea Shepherd New Zealand.
⁠
Each dish draws its inspiration from the sea with a kiwi twist, designed by our head chef Stephanie Hinton. Stephanie has recently moved back to New Zealand after 16 years cheffing in London, and running acclaimed vegan businesses there. Each course is paired with organic and vegan wines presented by Ollie Kettle and Josh Pointon of Paritua Wines. Proceeds from tickets sold will be donated directly to Sea Shepherd to help protect our oceans.
Numbers are limited, so gather your friends and book early for an unforgettable night of food, wine and ocean conservation.

description:
Summer Sessions I Under the Stars I An Evening at Ata Rangi, Join us at Ata Rangi for a long-table dinner amongst the vines - an evening brimming with beautiful food, exceptional wine, and lively company.

Savour seasonal, locally inspired cuisine by Ant North, celebrated for dishes that bring the best of the Wairarapa to the table. Served family-style, each course is paired with a hand-picked selection of Ata Rangi wines, while Sam Auger’s warm, intimate evening sets create the perfect soundtrack for the night.

- Welcome drinks at sunset

description:
Taste and Create, Join pastry chef Maxine Scheckter of Sugar Flour for an art class like no other. While being tutored by Inverlochy’s talented artists in a medium of your choice, you’ll enjoy a range of sweet treats that have been inspired by the artists and their food memories. Pastries will be paired with refined teas and non alcoholic bubbles.

You can choose from four workshops: pottery, screen printing, life drawing, or printmaking.  Your ticket includes two hours of tutored art instruction in your chosen medium (materials included), three pastry courses, non-alcoholic bubbles and tea, and access to explore the historic building.

description:
Urban Wine Walk | Pōneke Wellington (NZ), ON SALE TIMES
Presale Access - Thursday 11 September, 12pm NZT - Register Here
General Access - Thursday 11 September, 2pm NZT
----
The streets and laneways of Pōneke Wellington are set to come alive this Spring as a line-up of eight venues each play host to an incredible winemaker, who'll be there ready to pour and chat you through an unforgettable afternoon.
HOW IT WORKS
Kick things off at your chosen starting spot with something to eat, and then let the adventure unfold. Wander at your own pace, glass in hand, discovering incredible wines and venues along the way.
With a stellar line-up of winemakers, good vibes at every stop, and a guaranteed sell-out crowd, the Urban Wine Walk is the ultimate self-guided tasting experience you and your crew won’t want to miss!
PARTICIPATING VENUES & WINEMAKERS
1 - Choice Bros Ft. Coney Wines (NZ)
2 - Glou Glou Ft. Halite (NZ)
3 - Little Beer Quarter Ft. Hopes Grove & Aard (NZ)
4 - Lulu Bar Ft. Margrain Vineyard (NZ)
5 - Noble Rot Ft. VALLI (NZ)
6 - Panhead Tory St Ft. The Good Way (NZ)
7 - The Arborist Rooftop Bar Ft. Matawhero (NZ)
8 - The Tasting Room Ft. Tettonica Wines (NZ)
*Please note that traditional venue menus may vary due to the nature of the event.
TICKETS
Vino Lover Pass – $79 + Booking Fee (Limited Availability)
WHAT’S INCLUDED
Wine Tastings – Up to 3 wines per winemaker along the trail
$10 Food Voucher – Redeem at your nominated starting venue (before 1pm)
$25 Wine Voucher – Put towards event-day wine orders (six-pack minimum, participating producers only)
Event Essentials – Your official wristband & keepsake tasting glass
EVENT REGISTRATION & COLLECTION
Before heading to your nominated starting venue, swing by the official registration point to collect your wristband, tasting glass & vouchers.
📍 Where: Panhead Tory St (1 Tory St)
🗓️ When: Saturday 18th October | 11am – 1pm
Please note: The Urban Wine Walk officially runs from 12-4pm. Arrive early to grab your event pack and avoid the rush!
REFUND POLICY
Tickets are non-refundable (we’re all in for good times rain, hail or shine!). The only exception is if the event is cancelled or postponed by the organisers – then we’ve got you covered.
GETTING AROUND
One of the best parts about the Urban Wine Walk...? It’s totally self-guided! After checking in at your nominated starting venue, the day is yours! Wander at your own pace, discover new spots and sip your way through the trail however you like.

description:
50yrs Misuse of Drugs Act: What impact & what next?, The 1975 Misuse of Drugs Act (MoDA) has failed to deliver. Data from the United Nations Office for Drugs and Crime indicates the demand for drugs is greater than ever, while the supply of drugs knows no bounds. The failure and harm caused by the so called 'War on Drugs' is acknowledged globally and witnessed first hand here in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Back in 2011 a comprehensive review of the MoDA conducted by New Zealand Law Commission recommended the MoDA “should be repealed and replaced by a new Act …administered by the Ministry of Health”. HRCA wants to see that recommendation enacted.

New Zealand has a history for bold world leading policy reform: Woman’s Right to Vote; Decriminalisation of Sex Work; National Needle Exchange, Same Sex Marriage and most recently Drug Checking.

This half day Symposium will provide clear evidence why major law reform is necessary and detail the foundations upon which Aotearoa NZ can once again be innovative and lead the way with new drug laws based on evidence, research and experience -providing a safer environment for future generation.

Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa are delighted to have assembled a group of respected independent thinkers with vast experience of drug policy in Aotearoa and beyond, to reflect on the impact of the MoDA and to identify the principles and values needed to underpin new drug laws.

Warren Young: Prof. of Law & Former Deputy President New Zealand Law Commission.
Kirsten Gibson: Chair of Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa and Qualitative Researcher.
Fiona Hutton: Associate Prof. Institute of Criminology, Victoria University of Wellington.
Adam Dorsett: 40 yrs Living/Lived Experience of Prohibited Drug Use, 25yrs in Prison.
Julian Buchanan: Former UNODC Advisor and Criminology Professor.

description:
A Place of Firsts, Globally, citizens assemblies are widely used as an effective way to involve local people in deciding how to address complex issues such as climate change. Despite the repeated failure of standard policy processes, citizens assemblies have only recently made it to New Zealand. Register for this event to find out more about the Porirua Assembly on Climate and its innovations. 
Porirua is known for community-led innovations in governance and delivery, and the Porirua Assembly on Climate continued this tradition by being:
the first climate assembly in New Zealand,  
the first assembly co-designed and organised by an iwi authority and a community group, 
the first assembly process designed to honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi by using a tricameral design,  
the first New Zealand assembly to include children and young people, and 
by creating a new local governance body - the Porirua Community Leaders Forum - that sponsored the Assembly, holds its recommendations and can instigate ongoing community dialogue on local issues. 
Panellists will share learning on the Porirua Assembly’s innovations, talk about why the standard citizens assembly model was modified, dig into what enabled so many firsts and how these worked out in practice. They will reflect on this legacy and possible future impacts. Might these democratic innovations strengthen local democracy elsewhere in Aotearoa New Zealand? 
About the Host and Speakers
Jodi Watene is a Systems Change Lead at Te Rūnanga o Toa Rangatira Incorporated, was the project manager for the Porirua Assembly and is helping to establish a New Zealand Community of Practice on Indigenous Citizens’ Assemblies.
Makerita Makapelu is a Team Leader for Wesley Community Action in Porirua with a background in performing arts and youth work. She specialises in community-led development and grassroots systems change, and was one of the Porirua Assembly facilitators.  
Cally O'Neill was a participatory designer of community spaces until 2019 when she shifted her focus towards advocating for Te Tiriti-based deliberative democracy to address the climate and other contemporary crises. She is a founding member of Te Reo O Ngā Tāngata/The People Speak and was one of the Porirua Assembly facilitators. 
Future Unity, a youth climate group formed during the Assembly process will be represented by Orini Rokx-Taratu and Santino Morehu, who were participants in the Assembly’s youth and community streams.  
Emily Beausoleil is an Associate Professor at Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of Wellington. Her research as a political theorist centres on the dynamics, conditions and challenges of democratic engagement in diverse societies. She is conducting an independent evaluation of the Porirua Assembly process.

description:
AI in Education: Part 1, Sovereign AI in NZ Education is a two part series that invites educators, AI developers, wh`ānau, students, and other interested people to consider how we - in Aotearoa - can design, build, and use AI tools. The goal of these sessions is to spark and support the creation of AI tools and practices that best serve the aspirations of our students and whānau, and blend well with the skills and insights of New Zealand's educators.
Part 1:
Generative AI is already in Aotearoa’s primary classrooms.  It is used by many teachers for planning and by ākonga both in and out of school.  However, policy, training, and culturally safe practice haven’t always kept pace.
In this talk, David Coblentz will provide research-based insights into:
teacher adoption patterns,
what students say they’re doing (and worrying about), and
where schools are missing guidance.
We'll also discuss what AI sovereignty could mean in education in Aotearoa New Zealand.
Then we can close with some practical steps for boards, leaders, kaiako, and whānau to support constructive and equitable AI use in Years 5–8.
*While the formal (and online) event will finish at 5pm, those attending in person are encouraged to stay on for snacks and drinks to share. Stay till 6pm or later, and get into the ideas more deeply, in a room full of good people.
David Coblentz is a Senior Statistician at NZCER. In addition to an undergraduate degree in Mathematics and Physics, David holds advanced degrees in Biostatistics (MS), History (PhD), and International Studies (MA) from the University of Washington in Seattle. Prior to coming to NZCER and transitioning into an educational research career in 2021, David worked as a biostatistician, data analytics director, and statistical consultant. David also has university teaching experience in history. His areas of interest include data analysis and data science, history education, evaluation, and AI in education.
Part 2 will follow within two weeks of David Coblentz's presentation. It will be an online event that features two or three local AI in education developers, talking about their current development projects.
We intend to record both parts and make them available via our community site - https://community.sovereignai.nz/

Accountability in War: International Justice and Accountability for Ukraine, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has posed an unprecedented challenge to the international legal order — raising fundamental questions about accountability, reparations, and the enforcement of international law.
This expert roundtable brings together three visiting Ukrainian legal and civil-society practitioners for a focused discussion on the international justice mechanisms being developed in response to Russia’s aggression, and the role that partners such as New Zealand can play in supporting them.
The discussion will explore recent progress on:
the international compensation mechanism for Ukraine, including the Register of Damage and the newly established International Claims Commission;
ongoing efforts to ensure individual accountability for the crime of aggression, including the establishment of a Special Tribunal;
the broader international response grounded in the rules-based international order.
The roundtable forms part of the Oceania Fora on International Justice and Accountability, and is organised in collaboration with the Embassy of Ukraine in Australia, during the Ukrainian delegation’s visit to Australia and New Zealand in February 2026.

description:
Activists, Allies & Beyond: 40 Years Since Homosexual Law Reform, Join us at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library for a free event celebrating the 40th anniversary of the Homosexual Law Reform Act 1986. We’ll be joined by Trevor Mallard, Linda Evans, Bill Logan, Onjei Bond, and host Gareth Watkins for a panel discussion exploring the social and political climate, and the long history of community activism that contributed to the landmark 1986 reform passing through Parliament.

The panel will discuss the political processes behind the bill and the community campaigns that emerged during a deeply divisive period in New Zealand’s history. We’ll hear about the personal impacts this had on members of the rainbow community, the resulting legacies of the reform, and the ways it continues to shape the lives and rights of queer people in Aotearoa today.

About the Speakers:
Trevor Mallard:
Trevor Mallard was an MP for 35 years and served as a Minister and Speaker. More recently he was our Ambassador to Ireland, is now retired and spends his time gardening, walking his dog and helping with grandchildren.
Trevor acted as “whip” for the Homosexual Law Reform Bill. His role was to keep a day by day count to help ensure the numbers were there to make sure it became law.

Linda Evans:
Linda Evans has been an activist in lesbian, feminist and gay politics in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since the 1970s. She was involved in the ongoing campaigns for homosexual law reform and anti-discrimination laws in the 1970s and 1980s.
Linda is a trustee and voluntary curator for Kawe Mahara Queer Archives Aotearoa.

Bill Logan:
In 1985 Bill Logan was a radical Wellington bookseller and involved in the Gay Switchboard and the response to the Aids pandemic. He became one of the organisers of the Homosexual Law Reform campaign to decriminalise sex between men. He remains engaged in socialist and community activism, and now works as a counsellor and marriage and funeral celebrant.

Onjei Bond:
Onjei Bond is a recent Master’s graduate in Museum and Heritage studies, interested in the queer history of Aotearoa.
He has recently finished a six-month research project focused on documenting and preserving the queer history of the Taranaki region – in collaboration with Pride Taranaki and Puke Ariki.

Gareth Watkins:
Gareth Watkins (he/him) founded the non-profit community website PrideNZ.com in 2009. It has grown into the largest online audio repository of local LGBTQIA+ Rainbow histories, with more than 1,000 recordings of events and life histories, alongside thousands of related news items dating back to the early 1900s. The material is freely available to a global audience. Gareth is also a co-founder of Walk Tours NZ, a volunteer group sharing Wellington’s queer history through free walking tours and digital storytelling. He is currently writing an AI-assisted musical marking 40 years since homosexual law reform in New Zealand, combining human storytelling with AI-generated production elements. Across his work, Gareth is interested in how archives, technology and creative practice can help keep community histories alive and bring them to new audiences.

description:
Are Prisons Obsolete? A future we make for ourselves., People Against Prisons Aotearoa is an organisation that calls for a transformation in our approach: not just towards what we'd call criminalised behaviour and people, but towards organising the whole of society to support human flourishing.
The carceral system is an industry that does not produce a product, but a world of limited potential. While in the immediate future the cessation of harmful practices such as solitary confinement or abusive 'boot camps' for youth might not require alternatives, abolitionists like Ruth Wilson Gilmore argue that abolition is brought about by building something new. Some alternatives have already been attempted, such as restorative justice, but these programs are routinely discontinued even when they show signs of success. Other alternatives, such as Turuki! Turuki! https://www.beehive.govt.nz/.../2019-12/Turuki%20Turuki.pdf or #CareNotCages, are an imagined future, where education and community involvement transform lives for the better, in contrast to the so-called 'Justice System' limiting them far beyond reason.

Join us for the next Café des Idées - Sealife stories from the subantarctic: links between France and New Zealand

About this Event

The next Café des Idées, organised by and , is honoured to host Wendy Nelson and Kevin Hackwell for a captivating discussion on the shared scientific and environmental connections between France and New Zealand in the subantarctic marine world.

Wendy will be talking about important marine collections made on French expeditions of discovery to the NZ subantarctic in the early 1800s that are housed in the Herbarium of the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle in Paris.
Wendy has been collaborating with Professor Line Le Gall (Departement Origines et Evolution) and for two weeks in October they worked to locate and document these important specimens - uncovering answers to some long held questions about the identity of species described over 180 years ago and not found subsequently.
In this talk she will take you into the Herbarium of the Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle, Paris - and highlight some of the remarkable treasures housed there.
(This work was supported by funding from the French Embassy in Wellington and the Royal Society of New Zealand Te Apārangi.)
Kevin will talk about the importance of the marine protected areas in the subantarctic and initiatives that have been taken to protect critical habitat for southern seabirds and connections between French and NZ in this critical work.

Wendy Nelson is a botanist and marine biologist, currently Senior Research Fellow Auckland Museum Tāmaki Paenga Hira
Kevin Hackwell is an ecologist, formerly Chief Conservation Advisor for Forest & Bird, a sister organisation to LPO (Ligue pour la Protection des Oiseaux)

description:
China and the Media Landscape in the Pacific, Over the last decade, the People’s Republic of China has sought to deepen its ties with Pacific Island countries. Beijing’s efforts to cultivate influence in the region have included expanding economic, diplomatic, and security ties with Pacific Island nations, as well as expanding China’s footprint in the region’s media landscape. This talk will present the findings of recent research on China’s efforts to shape reporting, media coverage and narratives in the Pacific Islands and put Beijing’s efforts within the context of the region’s rapidly evolving information landscape.
 About the speakers:
Heidi Holz is a Senior Research Scientist at CNA. For close to two decades, her work has focused on PRC strategic communications, propaganda, and influence efforts. She is a graduate of Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service, where she received a master’s degree in security studies and a bachelor’s degree in Chinese and East Asian history.
Genevieve Collins is a research specialist in the China Studies program at CNA, where her research focuses on the behaviour of China’s state-run media and its reactions to US military operations and activities.
 Barbara Dreaver (Discussant) has been the Pacific Reporter for TVNZ 1 News since 2002, breaking stories uncovering social and economic issues affecting Pacific people living in New Zealand and the Pacific Islands. In 2020, she created a two-year training programme through Pacific Cooperation Broadcasting Ltd to support new Pacific journalists across the Pacific region. In the 2024 New Years Honours she was awarded an ONZM for services to investigative journalism and Pacific communities.
 About CNA: CNA is a non-profit, non-governmental research and analysis organization dedicated to providing independent and objective analyses to the U.S. government and the public. This talk will build on previous CNA research on China and the Pacific Islands media landscape which you can find at www.cna.org.

description:
Connected Theatres or Fractured World? Emerging Threats and Collective Responses Across the Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific, Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 it has become clear that threats in the Euro-Atlantic region and the Indo-Pacific are profoundly inter-connected. North Korean troops and weapons have helped Russia’s war effort and Chinese technologies have sustained its military industrial base. Ships registered in the Pacific have been part of Russia’s sanctions-busting ‘shadow fleet’ and implicated in cable-cutting activities in the Baltic Sea. Conversely, Russia has transferred advanced weapons technologies to North Korea, and lessons from the war in Ukraine have implications for Indo-Pacific flashpoints, including across the Taiwan Strait. But if cross-theatre links are clear, forging collective responses has become much more complicated. The recent US National Defence Strategy points to a more limited US role in Europe and expectations that in the Indo-Pacific allies and partners will have to do more. International order is in flux. What does all this mean for New Zealand, for our region, for partners, and for global security? 
Confirmed speakers:

This talk will spotlight unique Pacific experiences—building federated data ecosystems, navigating data sovereignty, and fostering cross-regional collaboration—while drawing connections and insights that may be relevant to New Zealand’s own data governance community.
Our speakers for this event are:
Malcolm Fraser - Malcolm is a data governance and digital innovation specialist focused on unlocking the value of data across public, private, and social sectors. Currently leading the Pacific Data Hub Team at Pacific Community (SPC), based in New Caledonia, he is committed to advancing ethical data practices and building integrated data ecosystems that benefit society, the environment, and the economy.
Kevin Sweeney - Kevin is the Data Governance Advisor for SPC – Pacific Community, the preeminent international development organisation for the Pacific. He is currently leading an initiative to implement and improve Data Governance within SPC, across its Pacific Island nation members, and amongst its international partners. Prior to joining SPC, Kevin served as the Principal Advisor for the Data System Leadership branch of Stats NZ, advising the Government Chief Data Steward, helping strengthen data capability across the government data system, while serving as the New Zealand delegate on international data forums. With several decades of experience scoping and implementing data and information strategies and systems, Kevin has worked in numerous capacities in New Zealand and the United States, including as Director of the New Zealand Geospatial Office, founding partner of a strategic consulting firm, and independently through his own management consulting practice.

Hosted by the Embassy of Italy in Wellington in collaboration with the United Nations Association of New Zealand – Wellington Branch, this event offers a platform for dialogue and exchange between the diplomatic community, academia, and the public.
Thursday, 20 November 2025
5:30 – 7:00 pm (5 pm arrival for 5:30 start) (followed by Italian refreshments)
RHLT3, Rutherford House, Victoria University, Wellington
Why Attend:
Celebrate 75 years of Italy–New Zealand friendship and cooperation.
Engage directly with the Ambassador of Italy in an open, insightful discussion.
Explore how both nations are working together to promote peace, sustainability, and shared prosperity.
Network with diplomats, students, academics, and community leaders.
Ambassdors Bio:-
Cristiano MAGGIPINTO
Born in Noci, Bari (Italy) on 20/12/1962.
1987: graduates from the University of Florence, degree in political science.
1989: joins the Italian Diplomatic Service and is assigned to the Directorate General
for Economic Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Appointed Second Secretary.
1993: First Secretary (Economy and Trade) in Tel Aviv (Israel).
1997: First Secretary for Social Affairs in Bonn (Germany).
1999: confirmed in Bonn and subsequently in Berlin (Germany) as Counselor for
Emigration and Social affairs.
2001: returns to Rome and serve as Chief of Staff of the Director General for Italians
Abroad and Migration Policies.
2004: promoted First Counselor.
2006: Consul General in Huston (USA).
2009: First Counselor for Emigration and Social Affairs in Washington (USA).
2011: appointed Minister Plenipotentiary.
2013: returns to Rome and serves as Head of the Communication and Evaluation
Office of the Directorate-General for Development Cooperation.
2017: Ambassador of Italy to Malaysia.
2021: Diplomatic Advisor to the Mayor of Florence (Italy).
2024: back to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Protocol Department.
In 2006 receives the Knighthood of the Order of Merit of the Republic.
Languages: Italian, English, French.
Married, no children.

This evening promises inspiration, meaningful conversation, and a celebration of two nations’ shared journey from Rome to Wellington.

description:
HRCA 50yrs Misuse of Drugs Act: What impact? What next?, Rutherford House (by the train station)
Room RHLT2
Bunny Street
Wellington
1.30-4.30pm
Free Admission
Light refreshments afterward
The NZ Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 (MoDA) has failed to deliver. Data from the United Nations Office for Drugs and Crime indicated the demand for drugs is greater than ever, while the supply of drugs knows no bounds.
A failure acknowledged globally and one we witness first hand here in Aotearoa NZ.
Back in 2011 a comprehensive review of the MoDA conducted by New Zealand Law Commission had already concluded the MoDA “should be repealed and replaced by a new Act …administered by the Ministry of Health”.
The Harm Reduction Coalition of Aotearoa wants to see that recommendation enacted.
We are delighted to have assembled a group of respected independent thinkers in the field, with vast experience of drug policy in Aotearoa and beyond, to reflect on the impact of the MoDA and to identify the principles and values needed to underpin new drug laws.
Warren Young
Professor of Law & Former Deputy President New Zealand Law Commission
Kirsten Gibson
Chair of Harm Reduction Coalition Aotearoa and Qualitative Researcher
Fiona Hutton
Associate Professor, Institute of Criminology, Victoria University of Wellington
Adam Dorsett
40 Years Living Experience of Prohibited Drug Use, in Prison for 25 years
Julian Buchanan
Former UNODC Advisor and Criminology Professor
New Zealand has a history for world leading innovative policy reform: Woman’s Right to Vote; Decriminalisation of Sex Work; National Needle Exchange, Same Sex Marriage and most recently Drug Checking.
This half day symposium will provide clear evidence why major law reform is necessary and detail the foundations upon which Aotearoa NZ can once again lead the way with new drug laws based on evidence, research and experience.
We look forward to seeing there!
Do pass on to anyone who might be interested.

Juggernaut: Live!, Join Toby Manhire and guests for a special one-night-only event to launch season two of last years most talked-about podcast – Juggernaut 2: The Story of the Fourth National Government.
After the tempestuous 80s, New Zealand wanted that cup of tea and a lie down. Instead, the Juggernaut was reborn for the 1990s with fresh crisis, brutal cuts and blizzard of reforms, including an historic new chapter in Crown-Māori relations, a Beehive coup and the gravity-defying advent of an entirely new electoral system. 
In the second season of the Spinoff’s award-winning podcast we bring that story to life with the people who were in the room. 
Get an exclusive look at what is to come and discussion around the legacy of a whiplash chapter in political history at Juggernaut: Live! 
-
Toby Manhire is editor-at-large at the Spinoff and writer/host/foley-artist for Juggernaut. He also presents the Gone By Lunchtime politics podcast.

description:
Kazakhstan and Central Asia: Leveraging International Partnerships in an Uncertain World, Kazakhstan’s strategic location between Europe and Asia, combined with the sweeping political and economic reforms, substantial energy, critical minerals, transit, and sustainable agriculture potential, increasing AI and digital profile, makes it a hotspot for international investors and pundits alike.
Meanwhile, amid the shift towards an increasingly multipolar order, Kazakhstan has also been emerging as an important middle power contributing to regional and global governance, stability, inter-faith dialogue, and sustainable development. But bold ambitions and increasing global fragmentation raise big questions:
How will Kazakhstan and the region of Central Asia, as a whole, navigate a world increasingly shaped by great-power rivalry and competing alignments, while sustaining regional cohesion and driving growth and innovation? What new opportunities might global decision-makers and investors uncover as
Kazakhstan develops its strategic sectors and promotes a well-balanced and pragmatic foreign policy?
Kazakhstan's regional Ambassador His Excellency Askar Kuttykadam based in Singapore will be in Wellington on 4 November and is a great opportunity for members, students and guests to learn about a region we don't hear too much about in New Zealand!
Event details
Date: Tuesday 4 November, 12:30-1:30pm
Venue: RHMZ03, Mezzanine Floor, Rutherford House, Pipitea Campus
Doors Open: 12:10pm
Event commences: 12:30pm
Event concludes: 1:30pm
Terms and Conditions
-One ticket per person. Each ticket must contain your full first and surname, email address and phone number that matches your ID. This event is for registered members of the NZIIA or non-members who pay the registration fee. We reserve the right to cancel any tickets registered as a NZIIA Member if you are not a 2025 NZIIA member. Walk ups are not allowed- you must be registered in advance.
-In keeping with NZIIA practice, unauthorised recording of this event (either audio or video) is not permitted.
-As a courtesy to others given limited availability of seats please only book if you can definitely attend.
Biography - HE Askar Kuttykadam
Ambassador of the Republic of Kazakhstan to the Singapore, Australia and New Zealand
General information, education
1998 - Graduated from Al-Farabi Kazakh State National University, Almaty, Kazakhstan.
Career
He began his diplomatic service in 1998 as the Referent (Assistant Attache) at the Europe and America Division of the Department of Bilateral Cooperation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
From 1999 to 2001 – Attache, Third Secretary of the Department of Bilateral Cooperation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan. In 2001- 2004, he was the Attache, Third Secretary at the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Lithuania.
In 2004-2005, he worked as the First Secretary in the Department of Europe and America and the Department of Information and Analytical Work and Forecast Assessments.
In 2005, he was the head of the Department of Information and Analytical Work and Forecast Assessments of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
From 2005 to 2007, he was the Counsellor of the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Malaysia, and in 2007-2009 – Counsellor of the Embassy of Kazakhstan in China.
In 2010-2011, he worked as the Head of Division, Deputy Director of the OSCE Department, in 2011-2012, Deputy Director of the Department of Pan-European Cooperation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
From 2012 to 2013 he held the position of Minister-Counsellor of the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Canada, in 2014-2015 – Counsellor of the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Malaysia.
From 2016 to 2018, he worked as the Deputy Director of the Department of Foreign Policy Analysis and Forecasting of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan. In 2018-2019 – Counsellor to the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Poland.
Prior to his appointment as Kazakhstan's Ambassador to Singapore, Australia and New Zealand concurrently, he was Deputy Head of the Department of Foreign Policy and International Relations of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The Ambassador presented his credentials to the Governor General in Wellington on 8 August 2023.
Askar Kuttykadam has the diplomatic rank of Envoy Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the I class.

description:
Minilateralism: a new page in the Indo-Pacific IR lexicon, Minilateralism has emerged as a defining feature of contemporary international relations, particularly in the Indo-Pacific. Yet, despite its growing prominence, the conceptual boundaries of this form of cooperation remain underdeveloped. This seminar addresses this gap by proposing a comparative framework that distinguishes minilateralism from other established modes of cooperation—not only bilateralism and multilateralism, but also plurilateralism and regionalism. Through this analytical distinction, the study clarifies the conceptual contours of minilateralism and illuminates its purposive and exclusive character. By advancing a sharper theoretical understanding, this research contributes to the conceptual lexicon of international relations and enhances our grasp of cooperation dynamics in the Indo-Pacific.
 Mr Ryosuke Hanada is a PhD candidate and Sessional Teaching Staff at the School of International Studies, Macquarie University. He was a Research Fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs (JIIA), researching Japan’s foreign policy in the Indo-Pacific region from 2016 to 2020. He experienced several fellowship programs, including the Japan-US Partnership Program of the Research Institute of Peace and Security (RIPS), Young Strategist Forum of the German Marshall Fund (GMF), Strategic Japan Program of the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), Indo-Pacific Fellow of the Perth USAsia Centre, and Raisina Young Fellow of Observer Research Foundation (ORF) in India. He holds Master of Research from Macquarie University, MA from the University of Warwick and BA in Law from Waseda University.

Navigating the turbulent transition: an international perspective, Navigating the turbulent transition: an international perspective
The world is facing what the head of the IEA has called "the biggest energy security threat in history".

About this Event

The conflict in the Gulf is causing shortages of oil, gas and fertilisers around the world, and the situation could worsen dramatically as countries burn through their reserves. At the same time, we have seen the ending of ever-freer trade, a splintering of international consensus on climate action, and the promotion of geopolitical fragility by the second Trump Administration. Set against this backdrop, however, we are living through explosive growth and plummeting costs in renewable energy, batteries and EVs, and the dawn of a new era of artificial intelligence. What does all this mean for New Zealand? Does the new security and geopolitical environment necessitate a policy U-turn? Or can the needs of climate, economics and energy security be reconciled?
Global energy thought leader Michael Liebreich will share his international insights in Wellington on the morning of Friday 5 June. Michael is the founder of BloombergNEF and Chairman and CEO of Liebreich Associates, as well as being a prolific writer and broadcaster, and host of YouTube channel Cleaning Up. The event is being facilitated by ERGANZ and will be hosted at the Wellington offices of MinterEllisonRuddWatts.

worldwide, yet, despite this, the nuclear issue remains relevant to New Zealand. As long as

Zealand’s role as a disarmament leader.

description:
Preferences on the design and financing of the New Zealand government’s retirement income schemes, This lecture reports the results of a multi-criteria decision-making survey investigating the preferences of a sample of New Zealanders on the design and financing of the New Zealand government’s retirement income schemes.
The survey, conducted in 2022, is almost identical to a 2014 survey. It is designed so that respondents make trade-offs between seven features of retirement income schemes, including taxes. The results are similar in both years.
Five results stand out:
There is noticeably more support in 2022 for keeping the age of eligibility at 65 years rather than 67 years, although opinion remains divided.
In both years, support for universality and opposition to means-testing is the most important criterion overall, although it is less important in 2022 than in 2014.
Opposition to a small compulsory saving scheme is higher now than in 2014, but it remains small. Most people would not oppose a compulsory saving scheme.
Opposition to an increase in current taxes has increased, but a majority of people would still be willing to pay higher taxes now to reduce the need to raise taxes on future generations.
Overall, the 2022 respondents were less confident than the 2014 respondents that they will be comfortable in retirement.
The survey shows that New Zealanders have diverse views on the relative importance of different aspects of retirement schemes. The results can be used to make inferences about the relative popularity of different potential policy reforms.
As was the case in 2014, raising the age of eligibility to 67 years attracts much less support and much more opposition than raising taxes to keep the age at 65 years. If taxes were raised, there is a preference to raise taxes sooner rather than later, to avoid significant increases in taxes on future generations.
This event is supported by voluntary donations. Please consider making a donation when reserving your ticket.
Biography
Andrew Coleman is a research economist at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and a visiting professor at the Asia School of Business, Kuala Lumpur.
His research interests include intergenerational economics, tax policy and social security; transport and housing economics; and international monetary economics. He has written widely about the New Zealand economy and was a member of the 2010 Saving Working Group.
Andrew holds a Ph.D. in Economics from Princeton University and has taught at the University of Michigan and the University of Otago.

description:
Putin’s Russia and Southeast Asia: The Kremlin’s Pivot to Asia and the Impact of the Russia-Ukraine War, Dr Ian Storey will discuss his new book on Russia’s relations with Southeast Asia. The first major study of Russia and Southeast Asia since the end of the Cold War, it traces the dramatic shifts in Moscow’s relations with the region since President Vladimir Putin took power in 2000. Dr Storey assesses the legacy of the Soviet Union, charts the evolution of Putin’s foreign policy and identifies the drivers behind the Kremlin’s ‘Turn to the East’ or Asia pivot. His book also examines Russia’s dialogue partnership with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the development of Moscow’s political, economic and military ties with each of the 11 regional states over the past 25 years. A large part of the book is devoted to Southeast Asia’s responses to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. At the end of the talk Dr Storey will also provide an update of Russia-Southeast Asia relations in 2025 and how the region views the on-going Russia-Ukraine War.
Dr Ian Storey is a Senior Fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute, Singapore. He specializes in regional security issues, focusing on Southeast Asia’s relations with the major powers and maritime security, especially the South China Sea dispute. Since joining ISEAS in 2007 he has been the editor of the ISEAS academic journal Contemporary Southeast Asia. Prior to ISEAS, Ian held academic positions at the Asia-Pacific Center for Security Studies, Hawaii and at Deakin University, Australia. Ian received his PhD from the City University of Hong Kong, his Master’s degree from the International University of Japan and his BA (Hons) from the University of Hull, England. He is the author of Putin’s Russia and Southeast Asia: The Kremlin’s Pivot to Asia and the Impact of the Russia-Ukraine War (2025) and Southeast Asia and the Rise of China: The Search for Security (2011)

Israel Randell (Tainui, Ngāti Kahungunu, Rarotonga, Mangaia)
Israel is a multidisciplinary artist, curator, and educator whose practice is grounded in Indigenous futurisms, spatial storytelling, and whakapapa. Her work often takes the form of installation, writing, and performance — exploring the relationships between time, place, and identity through a distinctly Māori lens.
Lisa Reihana (Ngāpuhi - Ngāti Hine, Ngāi Tū-Te Auru)
Lisa's extraordinary multidisciplinary practice – encompassing film, photography, sculpture, costume, body adornment, and written text – examines the many ways in which identity and history are constructed and represented, and the complex conceptualisation of place and community.
Matt Tini (Waikato, Ngaati Tiipa, Ngaati Mahuta, Ngāti Rākaipaaka, Ngāti Kahungunu)
Matt Tini is an artist and educator who works with photography, moving image, and native fibres. Deeply grounded in whakapapa, Māori cosmologies and contemporary lived experiences, Matt’s practice considers what it means to be tangata whenua in relation with te taiao. These ever shifting reflections influence Matt’s material and conceptual curiosities.
Louise Pōtiki Bryant (Kāi Tahu, Kāti Mamoe, Waitaha)
Louise is a New Zealand Arts Laureate, and an award-winning multi-media artist. She weaves Māori contemporary dance, video art, animation and film to create immersive multi-layered performances, video artworks and video design. Guided by Kaitiakitaka, and Mātauraka Māori, she aims to embody these values into every creative expression to inspire the care, protection, and regeneration of the whenua, moana, and awa.
