description:
Minarets journal at the Rita Angus Cottage, Join Enjoy at the Rita Angus Cottage for an event to celebrate the latest issue of Minarets journal, in conjunction with Tarika Sabherwal's summer residency. 
Minarets issue 15 is edited by Nirvana Haldar and connects the poetry and poetics of Aotearoa New Zealand with South Asia and its diaspora. Contributors to the issue will give readings of their work in Rita Angus' famous garden. Readings by Anisha Sankar, Faisal Al-Assad Liam Jacobson, and Ya-Wen Ho.
This event is free to attend. Light refreshments provided.
Minarets is a semi-annual journal of contemporary literature. With over a decade of issues featuring prominent and emerging writers and artists with a range of guest editors, the journal has sought to connect the poetry and poetics of Aotearoa New Zealand with international ideas.
Editor's note:
This one remains to be an ode for those who cannot sleep, for those who can and cannot grieve, and for those that live in interrupted durée.
In pursuit of generating a critical dialogue on borders, colonial nations and settler states, we have invited artists and writers to record their relation to these interrogations.
The fragmentation of the “South Asian” identity and its diaspora through the nation state’s homogeneity, has led to the erasure of spaces and its people. We have invited these interventions to ground themselves in Aotearoa, and in writing from this place, to understand borders, homogeneity, and the erasure of these spaces and people from “South Asia”.
We hope that this issue helps us arrive to the
memory of a place,
memory of a martyr,
memory of fleeing,
memory of reaching,
memory of a scent,
memory of a loved one,
memory of a home or many.
We hope that this issue holds space for all the grief that may come through this fragmentation, and together, creates an archive of spacio- temporal interventions by these poets.
—Nirvana Haldar

description:
Astronomy vs. the Billionaire Space Race - Dr Samantha Lawler, University of Regina, RASNZ, WAS and the University of Victoria Wellington are co-hosting this year's Beatrice Hill-Tinsley Lecture.
Time: 6:00 pm, Date: Friday 13 May 2026
Venue: RHLT1, Victoria University Pipitea Campus
Available online via Zoom https://vuw.zoom.us/j/97988322365 if you can’t make it in person, but we strongly encourage in-person attendance for the best experience!
In February 2024, hundreds of pounds of potentially lethal debris from a SpaceX Crew Dragon trunk from a private astronaut mission fell on farmland near Regina, Saskatchewan. Later in the year, a piece of a SpaceX Starlink satellite was found in a lentil field in another part of the province. In September 2025, one of the handful of Starlink satellites reentering every week was witnessed burning up across the entire western half of Canada, with the reentry ending over Saskatchewan.
Dr. Samantha Lawler of the University of Regina has been studying the proliferation of satellites in orbit over the past few years, and has been stunned to learn how often space debris falls so close to her home. Come learn why Saskatchewan is the best place in the world to find space debris, and what happens when you find space debris on your farm and silent SpaceX employees show up in a rented truck to be greeted by an astronomer and a dozen of Saskatchewan's finest local journalists. The billionaire space race is well underway, and this has important implications for international law, the continued operation of satellites in Low Earth Orbit, atmospheric pollution, and the future of astronomy.
Samantha Lawler is a professor of astronomy at the University of Regina in Saskatchewan, Canada. She completed degrees at the California Institute of Technology, Wesleyan University, and the University of British Columbia, followed by postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Victoria (Canada) and NRC-Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre. Her discoveries in the Kuiper Belt and predictions for satellite pollution have been featured by BBC, CBC, CNN, NPR, BBC, Scientific American, The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, Wired Magazine, Nature, and many other international news outlets. She lives on a farm outside Regina and deeply appreciates the beautiful prairie skies.

description:
Autumn Sandcasting Day, Join us for this wonderful intro to sand casting - it is a great opportunity to make some gorgeous lasting jewellery gifts for yourself or your loved ones!

The class runs from 10am - 4pm and there will be a lunch break.

Students are shown the ancient technique of sand casting, using a wax to make a simple hard model or found objects such as buttons or simple small forms - create your simple 2-part mould and melt and pour sterling silver or shibuichi (a mix of silver and copper) to cast into the sand.

The model you have made or found enables you to make multiple pours possible to create multiple pieces. Best suited to smaller scale items, both to keep the budget down and the amount of weight in a piece this technique can be used to create rings, pendants or small earrings. This is a fun process for those who just want to try their hand at it, or a very useful low-tech process for those who are making jewellery into a career or creative activity. Each student will be given opportunity to cast one or two items, and then time will be included in the day to finish up the pieces so you can wear them away.

This class uses a combination of tutor supervision and also a peer-buddy system so that students are also given opportunity to watch and learn from each other's casts and pours.

The class has a practical health and safety aspect to it as students are introduced to working with an oxy-lpg torch and molten metal.

Course cost does not include silver costs but students can expect to use around $60 - $120 worth of silver or shibuichi.

Friday 3rd April
10.30am Pole Flow, Leg Rotations & Flexible Hips (Ana)
Leg rotations can create different shapes, lines and feeling to our movement. They can elevate our pole flow and are foundational to many transitions and moves. Leg rotations start from the hips. We can make them more comfortable and access more dramatic shapes by conditioning our hip flexors and increasing our range of motion. In this workshop we will learn:
•Conditioning exercises for our hip flexors that you can add to your regular practice
•The foundational movement of leg rotations and how they can elevate and create variety in our pole moves
•A variety of dance elements that use leg rotations, that you can add to your pole flow or routines
(All levels)
12 noon Belly Dance: Making It Slinky (Pip E-Lysaah)
The magic isn’t in the big tricks. It’s in the pause before them.
In Making It Slinky, we’ll dive into the slow moments that define a performance, the entrance, the exit, and every delicious transition in between. This workshop is all about how you arrive, how you linger, and how you leave them slightly unwell. We’ll explore controlled undulations, weighted steps, breath-led movement, and the art of stretching time so the audience forgets to blink. Less rushing. More reigning.
This is signature muscle isolation and control, the kind that makes a simple belly roll wave feel scandalous. We’ll break down my structured approach to belly rolls, arm waves, and wraps ... not just how to execute them, but how to layer and thread them so nothing ever “stops.” Everything melts, coils, and unwraps with intention. You’ll learn how to build tension through transitions, turning the space between movements into something almost indecent. If you’ve ever been told to “do more,” this workshop is about doing less… slower… and making it hit harder.
(All levels)
1.30pm Sensual Awakening: Unleash your Inner Siren (Vixen Temple)
Get out of your head and into your body with Vixen Temple! In this empowering workshop, you'll explore techniques to tap into your inner sensuality and trust your body. Harness your erotic energy to move with seductive fluidity and hypnotic flow.
(All levels)
3.00pm Nail Your Inverts (Elisa Puccioni)

Whether it's refining your form, building strength, or gaining more aerial control, we've got you covered! This workshop is ideal for beginners who are starting with their inverts up to intermediate students that want to polish their inverting techniques. Don't forget to BYH (bring your heels!) for an extra challenge and added flair!
(All levels)
4.30pm Feeling the Floor (Karina Shann)
In this workshop Karina will utilize fundamental floorwork moves such as shoulder stands, rolls, duck dives and body lines to guide you through ways that you can accentuate parts of your body, move with intention and captivate the audience. She’ll teach transitions and combos incorporating the fundamentals that you can take away to elevate your floor game. Heels optional but recommended. Socks, leg warmers optional, knee pads necessary.
(Prerequisite – Backwards & forwards roll)
6.00pm Choreography Kickstarter (Maree & Giada)
This workshop is perfect to get you started on your performance journey.
• Practical exercises to unlock your creativity, start building combos for your routines, and practice transitions between moves.
• Talk through how to structure a routine, performance tips and tricks, how to deal with nerves and much, much more!
This workshop is suitable for students of all levels. If you are currently working on a dance for a show, we can help with that. But you don't have to have a performance in mind to get heaps out of this session!

A burlesque classic – Express! Let’s get our groove on to this banger. We will learn some cute chair tricks and transitions to sass our way through this choreography. Beginner friendly, this dance is suitable for all levels! Plus, progressions for those who want to get upside down.
Wear comfortable clothes, socks or dance heels.
(All levels)
12 noon Creative Practices for Freestyle (Rachael)
Freestyling is a fantastic way to develop your movement style. This workshop will cover various concepts like tempo, sensation, texture, intention. You’ll learn new approaches for practicing freestyling and have fun while gaining a new appreciation for the practice.
(All levels)
1.30pm Stripper Flow (Maddie May)
Learn how to slink around the pole in your own authentic way, focusing on embellishing movements, fluid transitions and musicality!

We are excited to be welcoming Suzanne Paul as our Guest Speaker for 2026.
Inspirational speaker Suzanne Paul arrived in New Zealand from the working-class streets of Wolverhampton in 1991 with just $18 in her pocket and a fierce determination to succeed.
Despite the challenges of a learning disability that brought anxiety and low self-esteem, Suzanne channelled her boundless optimism and natural gift for sales into building one of the country’s most successful direct marketing empires. Her iconic products, such as Natural Glow and the Suzanne Clip, became household names, and within five years, she had transformed herself into a multimillionaire and one of New Zealand’s most beloved public figures, complete with her own TV shows. In 2007, she further captured the nation’s heart by winning Dancing with the Stars.
Life took a dramatic turn at 50 when Suzanne lost everything and was declared bankrupt. Though tempted to give up, she instead drew on the same resilience and skills that had built her earlier success. Starting over from nothing, she rebuilt her life step by step, launching new ventures and embracing fresh challenges.
Among her many accomplishments since then, Suzanne developed a clothing line for petite women, opened a boutique in Remuera, and spearheaded the success of Thin Lizzy Makeup in both New Zealand and Australia. She also became a bestselling author with But Wait, There’s More, a book that shares her journey and practical wisdom on making dreams come true. A second edition is currently in the works, focusing on resilience and turning intention into action.
Now living her dream life once again, Suzanne Paul continues to prove that even in the face of adversity, reinvention is always possible—and that success is never out of reach.
Join us for a delicious lunch by Party Perfect, network and have a great time!

Jewellery-making in 8 weeks: Monday nights, Level 2+, This course is for level 2+ and advanced students; it is not open to beginners. This more advanced class is ideal for those who are already competent at soldering simple joins, annealing, and basic tool use on their own.

Students must have completed an 8-week block with ring-making and bezel settings or equivalent. If you have not done one of our 8-week beginner’s classes or are unsure of your level because you may have done a few different shorter classes, please contact us and we can advise you.

A more advanced set of students means that your tutor can support you and the group to take on more exciting and complex challenges. They will work with the group to find appropriate projects for you and for the class as a whole. Each 8-week block may focus on a particular skill topic, rather than doing loads of different topics with each student over the block. This means the students will benefit from a more in-depth learning experience, supported practice, and peer support from fellow students.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chain-making as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something familiar to hone their skills on, as well as take on a new skill. Their silver project could be a pendant on a handmade chain, a charm bracelet, or a more complex bezel setting.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class—more chains or simple bezel settings are ideal to help them strengthen their soldering skills—alongside a challenge project that might be a shelf setting (an adaptation of a bezel setting that can take faceted stones), a tube setting, or a larger bezel setting for a box or brooch.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student. All metals and stones, as well as quality findings and chains, are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

description:

Mana Taiohi is a principle based framework that informs the way people who work with young people work in Aotearoa. Mana Taiohi has evolved from the principles of youth development previously expressed in the Youth Development Strategy of Aotearoa (2002). It is informed by the voice of young people and people who work with young people, Aotearoa based literature into positive youth development, and a Te Ao Māori worldview.
Matt was born and raised in Te Awakairangi, Wellington and his ancestors are Ngāti Porou - Tikapa, Ngāti Kahungunu - Wairoa, Ngāti Ruapani - Waikaremoana, Āti Haunui-a-Pāpārangi - Pungarehu and Gujurat. He has been married to his wife Rachel since 2016 - she’s Ngā Puhi, Japanese, and English and their son, Mana Tuku Iho, was born in April 2024 after a 7-year fertility journey.
Matt has been involved in youth and community work since 2005 and co-founded the 'Te Awakairangi Youth Development Network' with a team of superstars. Matt is currently the Pouwhakamana for Zeal Youth Aotearoa, Āpiha Kaiwhakahaere for Ngā Kaihoe, and the Kaiāwhina of World Vision New Zealand.
In 2019, the whānau moved to Tāmaki Makaurau to study a Bachelor's in Indigenous Theology (Māori/Pasifika), a Diploma in Māori Leadership and a Diploma in Te Reo Māori, completing these qualifications in 2022. These studies have been transformational for both their personal growth and their work in youth and community development, changing the way they engage with the world. Through storytelling, making connections, and wānanga, they share these insights with the people they meet.
Now, with the arrival of Mana, they are back in Wellington, closer to friends and whānau. They are excited to continue their mission to see Aotearoa lifted up and our people thriving to their full potential.

You may choose to add the 'Enriched Air' and/or the 'Dive Against Debris' specialty qualifications to your weekend experience. Simply ask to: include these dives as part of your five dives, complete the on-line study and a short practical, pay a small fee – and go diving. These Specialties count towards the prestigious PADI Master Scuba Diver rating.

Pay your deposit and you can begin the AOW theory. Make sure your dive medical is current, then join us for a weekend's fun diving. After everything is completed, you will qualify as a PADI AOW Diver. This is the minimum requirement for our dive adventures and a prerequisite for the PADI Rescue Diver course.

description:
Silk Aquatint Printmaking, Discover the silk aquatint, an accessible, non-toxic alternative print technique similar to collagraph printing whereby the texture of woven silk on the plate provides a ground to start building a design with varying tonal qualities. The outcome can be wonderfully detailed and painterly.

In this workshop you will learn -

- To identify appropriate silk to create an aquatint plate
- The importance of preparing an appropriate matrix for the silk
- About the different effects created by different types of media applied to the print matrix
- To make an aquatint plate
- To print an aquatint plate
- This workshop is open to beginners as well as seasoned printers.

Basic materials included. Bring drawings or designs to help you get started and wear clothes you are not precious about.

Half hour break for lunch. Bring your own packed lunch to have in the historic Inverlochy house or explore the local Te Aro cafes.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course.

description:
Women's Krav Maga Self Defence - Intro Night, We believe every woman should feel strong, fearless and confident for life. Krav Maga has proven to be highly empowering for women all around the world. We offer this course to women to learn to deal with women-related challenges, encouraging every woman to overcome anxiety or fear, with confidence, skills, strength.
In an ideal world, women would not need to learn to protect themselves. However, until some deeply ingrained societal problems are resolved, it is smart and necessary to have some skills to be able to look after yourself and loved ones with. In the meantime, we encourage every women to approach this training with personal development, personal growth, enjoyment and empowerment being the motivating purpose.
We understand women often prefer to train in a women's class. This is our Women's (13+) class called ROAR.
Beginning in 2018, this program was created to provide a safe, holistic and supportive class where women can experience empowerment through training. You will learn to find your voice, inner strength and resolve, while learning physical skills such as how to escape and overpower an assailant, counter grabs, abduction attempts, chokes, hair grabs, pushing and shoving, being hit, being pinned to the ground and sexual assault attempts. We will help you unleash your protective feminine fighting spirit.
The Intro Night is the ideal time for women interested in the Women's Class to try a class first, see how we train, who we are, and gain some valuable basic skills, before deciding to join the full course. (Note: School Term 1, 2025 is 10 weeks long). No cost to attend the Intro Night.
Please email contact@tacticalsurvival.co.nz to enquire or book your spot.
More Info: www.tacticalsurvival.co.nz/womens
After Intro, classes run every Wednesday night 7:00pm - 8:00pm (Thistle Hall Cuba St)

All about our ancient bats, A creature of the forest floor and the night sky, the New Zealand short-tailed bat is found nowhere else on Earth and is clinging on to survival in a handful of scattered sites.
Join Dave Hunt as he explores the current conservation status of these extraordinary ancient bats, and the work underway to protect and manage their fragile populations.

Ōtari 100: Celebrating 100 years of native plants, conservation, and community. 1926-2026.

description:
Awa After Dark: Spotlighting at Kumutoto Forest, Kelburn, Awa After Dark: Spotlighting at Kumutoto Forest, Kelburn
Explore your local awa with freshwater experts from our Wai Connection team at this spotlighting event at Kumutoto Forest, Kelburn. With your gumboots and a torch, head off on an evening hīkoi to your local waterway to ‘spotlight’ and observe freshwater species in their natural habitat. Learn about the health of our waterways, freshwater conservation efforts in your neighbourhood, and some of the ways that you could become a kaitiaki of your local awa. Due to the delicate nature of this awa the observations will be stream-side as we walk along the banks and bridges of the stream.

This event is in collaboration with the Kumutoto Restoration Project, a restoration group that has been working on restoring and enhancing the biodiversity within and around the ngahere and awa at Kumutoto.

Book here: https://events.humanitix.com/awa-after-dark-spotlighting-at-kumutoto

Awa After Dark events take place in the early evening, they’re perfect for the whole whānau.

This event is free, but bookings are essential. These events are very popular, please let us know if you have booked and can no longer make it so we can reallocate your spot.

Outdoor event:
This event is outdoors, please dress appropriately (gumboots and warm clothing recommended). If the weather is really bad, we'll let you know we’re cancelling via the email you've provided us.

Location:
The streams we spotlight often don't have an 'address'. On the day before the event, we'll email you all the details you need to find our exact meeting location on the night.

What is spotlighting?
Ever played spotlight with a fish? Heaps of our native freshwater critters are nocturnal. Scientists often visit freshwater areas at nighttime with a torch, it’s the best time to see exactly who’s living in our awa!

What is Wai Connection?
Wai Connection is a national programme delivered by Mountains to Sea Wellington aimed at connecting local communities to their waterways to improve them. We support communities and mana whenua with the knowledge, tools and expertise to monitor and care for their local freshwater places.

description:
Cult & Classics: Ferris Bueller's Day Off, Our CULT & CLASSICS series is back from March 1, bringing iconic films and unforgettable favourites back where they belong - on the big screen.
Whether you’re revisiting a favourite or seeing it for the first time, this is your chance to experience cinema the way it was meant to be seen: with a crowd, in the dark, on Brooklyn’s biggest screen. & only for $15 per ticket!
We’re kicking things off with the ultimate feel-good favourite: Ferris Bueller's Day Off.
Released in 1986 and directed by John Hughes, the film follows smooth-talking high school rule-breaker Ferris Bueller as he takes one perfectly planned day off school. Alongside his best friend Cameron and girlfriend Sloane, Ferris embarks on an unforgettable adventure through Chicago - complete with a vintage Ferrari, a parade performance, and one very determined principal on his trail.
Sharp, endlessly quotable, and pure ’80s energy from start to finish, Ferris Bueller’s Day Off is the perfect way to relaunch our CULT & CLASSICS season.
Join us from March 1 at 7:30 pm. Tickets on sale now.

description:
French Film Festival - Leave One Day, Making waves in 2025 as the first-ever debut feature selected to open the Cannes Film Festival, Amélie Bonnin’s joyously entertaining musical romance stars break-out singer/songwriter Juliette Armanet as a talented Parisian chef forced to reconnect with her small-town upbringing during an unexpected trip home.
Cécile (Armanet) – a fan-favourite Top Chef winner – is about to finally realise her dream and open her own restaurant when her father, the cook at a small rural truck stop, falls unwell.

Cécile must deal with a return to her roots that is more complicated than she imagined; when she runs into her teenage first love (César Award-winner Bastien Bouillon), old memories and sensations resurface... and then her fiancé, who senses something’s wrong, shows up.
Evocatively depicting regional France and the complications of family life with tenderness and wit, Leave One Day interweaves music naturally into the story, blending several classics with more recent hits by artists such as Stromae and Céline Dion.

Armanet, herself one of France’s most popular contemporary artists, performed John Lennon’s “Imagine” during the Paris Olympic Games’ opening ceremony and proves to be a shining discovery, in this warm-hearted and completely endearing gem.

description:
TWIN PEAKS: FIRE WALK WITH ME, UPDATE 11/2/26: There are about 150 tickets sold so we are down to the last 15 or so seats.
___________________________________________________________________
"Faster and faster. And for a long time you wouldn't feel anything. And then you'd burst into fire" - Laura Palmer

TWIN PEAKS: FIRE WALK WITH ME.
DAVID LYNCH | USA & FRANCE | 1992 | 135mins | R18+| 4K DCP PROVIDED BY JANUS FILMS DISTRIBUTION

Join us for this very special community fundraiser screening of the prequel to the critically acclaimed series, "Twin Peaks".

ABC cancelled the original series after season 2 but a month later, Lynch announced he was "not yet finished with the material" and principal photography for the full length prequel film, began on September 5th 1991 at a caravan site in Snoqualmie Washington. Which became the "Fat Trout Trailer Park" where the story of the last 7 days of Laura Palmer begins.

Since its showing at the 1992 Festival De Cannes, no other Lynch film had polarized audiences to such an extent. Fans that wanted more "Cherry Pie" and "Donuts" from the TV show were served a much darker, unflinching and unforgiving work - in Lynch's own words, a movie about "the loneliness, shame, guilt, confusion and devastation of the victim". Derided by critics and many fans at the time it was a commercial box office flop.

Yet in the years since the initial reaction, a gradual wave of reappraisal and appreciation began. With time it's brilliance came into focus with growing acknowledgment, that the film is a more accurate, complex and powerful account of trauma. Combining the dramatic ferocity of Sherly Lee's tour de force and the beauty of Angelo Badalamenti's score, Lynch reclaimed full ownership of the material creating a harrowing, compassionate and enigmatic hymn to Laura Palmer.

As we approach the films 34 year anniversary and since Lynch's passing in 2025, it is now regarded by critics and fans worldwide, as a revered epilogue, essential predecessor to "The Return", and Lynch's most chilling, terrifying, and yet empathetic and humane cinematic masterpiece.

WHERE: The Roxy Cinema. 5 Park Road. Miramar. Wellington.
Cinema 1 - The big cinema upstairs with the massive screen, red italian leather sofas, and of course those red curtains!

WHEN: Seating is unreserved so arrive early to check-in at the table upstairs, enter the raffle and get seated.
8:15pm - Doors close and the film starts. (no trailers)

COST: Tickets are $20 per person. (plus booking fee). This is a not for profit community screening put on for the pure love of Twin Peaks and the fans. All proceeds go to help pay for the cinema hire and licensing the film with any extras donated to charity. So spread the word and come celebrate "Twin Peaks Day 2026"!

TWIN PEAKS RAFFLE: Check-in at the desk upstairs and get a complimentary raffle ticket, to enter into the draw for 1 of these companion books.
1.The Secret Diary of Laura Palmer - By Jennifer Lynch with foreword by Mark Frost & David Lynch (paperback, 2012 edition)
2.Fire Walk With Me: Your Laura Disappeared - By Scott Ryan with foreword by Jeff Jensen (paperback, 2022 edition)
3.Laura's Ghost: Women Speak about Twin Peaks - By Courtney Stallings with foreword by Sheryl Lee (paperback, 2020 edition)
Cutoff to enter is 8:10pm and prizes drawn just before the start of the film.

RULES:
1. Tickets are per person. There will be NO door sales at the Roxy, so DO purchase it beforehand please.
2. The film is classified R18+. All attendees MUST be 18yo + and have ID
4. The Roxy have strict no BYO food/drinks. Only Food/drinks purchased at the Roxy can be taken into the screening.
3. This is a safe, friendly, INCLUSIVE place. There is ZERO tolerance for discrimination, disrespect or creepy gross behavior of any kind. By attending you agree to the Code of Conduct.
4. Arrive early to enter the raffle before the cutoff if you want to be in it to win it. Good Luck!

Thank you and Happy Twin Peaks Day!

description:
Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness, Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness
Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness

Develop the tools you need for navigating stress, anxiety, and overwhelm.

Mary Rose Dias - Positive Psychology Practitioner (MSc), Yoga Therapist, and Certified iRest®️ Meditation Teacher - will be leading a nourishing and practical evening exploring how mindfulness and positive psychology can help us cultivate greater calm, resilience, and inner steadiness.

Life can be demanding, and when stress builds in our system, it can become difficult to access clarity, ease, and perspective. While we can’t always remove life’s challenges, we can learn to shift our relationship with stress and develop tools that help us meet it with greater awareness and self-compassion.

Through guided meditation, reflection, and experiential practices, you’ll be introduced to accessible tools to help you:
•⁠ ⁠Regulate stress and settle anxiety
•⁠ ⁠Connect with a deeper sense of inner safety and steadiness
•⁠ ⁠Clarify intentions and reconnect with what matters most
•⁠ ⁠Access practical resources for greater calm and wellbeing in everyday life

Together, we’ll explore grounding practices drawn from mindfulness, meditation, and positive psychology, beginning and ending with guided meditation to support integration and deep rest.

This is more than just developing a mindset, you’ll be leaving with something practical to draw upon long after the evening ends.

Open to all - no prior meditation experience needed.

Plus - there is an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert included in your ticket! Stay back for the good food & great company.

Meet Mary Rose
Mary is a Wellington-based holistic therapist, meditation teacher and yoga practitioner whose work gently weaves together evidence-based psychology, ancient yogic wisdom, meditation practices and a whole lot of unconditional love and respect for each person’s unique journey. With over 15 years of experience in wellbeing, counselling, coaching, yoga and meditation, she is deeply passionate about creating nurturing spaces that support healing, self-discovery and inner calm.

Her heart-felt calling is to support others in accessing greater health, healing and happiness. While based in her birthplace of Aotearoa New Zealand, Mary’s dedication to wellness has taken her around the world, including Hawaii, Australia, Ireland, the Czech Republic and the UK, where she has trained with internationally recognised teachers in yoga, meditation and positive psychology. Through private sessions, workshops, courses and retreats, she offers a grounded, compassionate and holistic approach that honours both modern psychology and timeless wisdom traditions.

Men's Group Tuesday 28 Oct, To join this community, and book your Tuesdays - please sign up here first, and we will email you the event access code. (our venue address will be emailed with your ticket).

This is a space for men to talk honestly, listen deeply, and figure some things out together. It’s not about having it all sorted. You don’t need to be a certain type of guy. Just show up as you are, with no pressure to speak or share.
Open group: new faces are welcome
Flexible: book to come when it suits you. Each Tuesday is a new event. Most will try for fortnightly.
Small groups: 8 men + 2 experienced hosts
Inclusive: all ages, backgrounds and identities (18+)
It's about connection and showing up, instead of going it alone. It makes time for meeting our various challenges, while learning and growing us into better friends, partners, dads, sons and humans. 
It isn’t a boys or bros club, therapy or a self-help seminar, religious or new-age. No fixing, preaching, or pressure. It’s not a crisis service or a substitute for professional care. The sign-up form explains this in more detail.
You can expect to:
Practice listening and learn communication skills for life
Discover greater integrity and self-accountability
Be supported in building your emotional intelligence
Become a part of a hearty and diverse community
Have a good time - it’s often uplifting and inspiring.
Joseph and your team of hosts have all been in regular men's groups for many years. The group sometimes offers simple and proven inquiries that draw on NVC, MBSR, active listening, gratitude and more.

description:
🧠 The Starving Brain | A Yogic Perspective on Nourishment, Energy & Focus, 🧠 The Starving Brain | A Yogic Perspective on Nourishment, Energy & Focus
We often talk about eating less — but not about what happens when we don’t eat enough.
When the body is under-fuelled, the brain takes priority — quietly redirecting energy away from digestion, hormones, and even mood regulation.

From a yogic lens, this is more than biology.
When energy stops flowing freely (prana), we lose clarity, intuition, and the natural rhythm that keeps body and mind in harmony.

In this 2-hour workshop, we’ll explore:
• Why the brain “steals” energy when under stress or depletion
• The emotional energy of food — and what your cravings might be teaching you
• The science of fasting — when it supports healing and when it harms
• The gut–brain connection and how awareness restores balance
• How nourishment, breath, and rhythm support neuroplasticity and vitality

We’ll finish with Q&A and discussion to help you integrate the insights into your own life.

💰 $40 per person
📍 Yoga Studio, Raumati South
🔗 Book here:

https://35daydetox.simplybook.net/v2/

“In yoga, nourishment isn’t indulgence — it’s how energy becomes consciousness.”

A rare cosmic event where six of the seven planets are in dawn sky during this final Planetary Parade for 2025. Matariki is also visible at this time close to the line of planets.
Come down to the Wellington waterfront at dawn and see the planets Pareārau (Saturn), Kōpū/Tāwera (Venus), Hine-i-tīweka (Jupiter), Whiro (Mercury), and Matariki (Pleiades) in our skies. Rangipō (Uranus) and Tangaroa (Neptune) are also in the sky but they will be too faint to see. Matawhero (Mars) follows after Te Rā (the Sun) rises so it won't be seen in the sky.
If you want to gaze in wonder at Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, look through our amazing telescopes! We can show you where to find Matariki, but binoculars at better so if you have a pair bring them along. The event is child friendly and free!
If you want to support our Society by becoming a member, please go to https://www.was.org.nz/join-us/

Parent to Parent hosts regular Parent Support Groups in Lower Hutt to support carers and parents just like you. These groups are a safe space for family and whānau to share their experiences, their challenges, their triumphs, and to learn from each other in an open and 100% judgement- free environment. No topic is too ‘weird’, no question too ‘out there’. We get it, and we are here to help.

description:
Whānau Chine Colle - Creative arts holiday programme for teens & adult, Welcome to mixed media collage the printmakers way. Chine Colle is a printing process in which a thin sheet of paper is printed on and at the same time, mounted on a sturdier sheet, creating a subtle delicate backdrop to the printed image. Expanded on, this can include contrasting papers, graphic images, select colour shapes and fabric.

This is a workshop whereby teens (minimum age 13) are encouraged to learn collectively with one of their favourite adults. Art can be created as a joint or individual project. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

In this one day workshop people will:

- Practice traditional and individual chine colle techniques
- Explore the use of delicate papers more responsive to ink and hand printing
- Test and practice mixed media chine colle with images, papers and fabric
- How effective chine colle is as a method of adding colour to prints
- Making and using a damp pack
- Recipes for traditional glues

This is a workshop whereby tweens/teens (minimum age 11) are encouraged to learn collectively with one of their favourite adults. Art can be created as a joint or individual project. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

description:
Ceramicus 2025, Now in its 67th year, Ceramicus returns to the Wellington Botanic Garden’s Begonia House from 5–15 November!
Presented by the Wellington Potters’ Association in partnership with Wellington City Council, this much-loved annual exhibition celebrates the creativity and diversity of contemporary ceramics in the Wellington region.
This year we’re thrilled to welcome Aaron Scythe as our Guest Selector and Featured Artist. Known for blending Japanese and New Zealand ceramic traditions, Aaron brings both mastery of technique and a spirit of experimentation to his work. His curatorial eye promises an exhibition that’s thoughtful, dynamic, and full of surprises.
Don’t miss our Pop-Up Pottery Market!
Alongside the exhibition, join us on 8 & 9 November and 15 & 16 November for the Ceramicus Pop-Up Pottery Market, held just outside the Begonia House. Browse and buy directly from local potters, explore a range of handcrafted ceramics—from elegant tableware to unique statement pieces—and take home something special. Synthesizer isn’t just the title of their seventh album; it’s also a custom-built instrument created specifically for it. “It’s pretty messed up, chaotic… but it feels really human,” says frontman Oliver Ackermann. The album celebrates spontaneity, collaboration, and the kind of raw noise that can only come from a band locked in together.

Written in the band’s Queens studio after a refreshed lineup — Ackermann with John and Sandra Fedowitz — Synthesizer cracks open and reimagines the signature APTBS sound in vivid new ways. Bear’s Den New Zealand 2026 | Wellington, British country and indie-folk band Bear’s Den are coming to play their first ever headline shows in Aotearoa. They’ll perform at Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Tuesday 12 May and San Fran Wellington on Wednesday 13 May. Tickets go on sale this Thursday 26 March at midday

Formed in London 2012, Bear’s Den have carved out a global reputation and devoted following for over a decade. Their debut album Islands was certified gold, with the hit single ‘Above The Clouds of Pompeii’ nominated for the Ivor Novello Award for Best Song musically and lyrically. Since then, they’ve created four critically acclaimed studio albums, a collaborative project with screenwriter Paul Frith and a soundtrack album to Season 3 of Apple TV Series Trying. 
Their emotive story telling and cinematic sound has made up a catalogue that translates into film and onto live stages, taking them to some of the world’s biggest arenas and festivals, including Reading and Leeds, Glastonbury Festival, Pukkelpop, Lowlands and Bonnaroo. 

Consisting of founding member Andrew Davie on vocals and guitar, Christof van der Ven (banjo, guitar, vocals), Marcus Hamblett (synths, horns), and Jools Owen (drums, horns), the band have been on the road celebrating the 10 year anniversary of Islands for the past year and they’re now set to bring it all to New Zealand for the first time.

description:
Bic Runga & The NZSO, More than 60 classical musicians will collaborate with Bic Runga and her band for a special concert in Wellington. Bic Runga & the NZSO is a concert of songs from Bic’s much-anticipated new album ‘Red Sunset’. The performance will also feature a selection of hits and best-loved songs spanning the artist’s extraordinary 31-year career.   
This is the only leg of the ‘Red Sunset’ tour featuring orchestra, so expect the songs to be transformed by the powerful accompaniment. Also involved in the show is Bic’s partner, multi-instrumentalist Kody Nielson of The Mint Chicks and Unknown Mortal Orchestra fame.   
Bic Runga (Ngāti Kahungunu) is a multi-award-winning singer-songwriter. The youngest inductee into the New Zealand Music Hall of Fame, she shot to fame in 1996 with the single ‘Drive’. Her 1997 debut album ‘Drive’, including the hit ‘Sway’, won the Tūī for Album of the Year. Over her career, she has won 20 Tūī awards — the most for an Aotearoa solo artist, including Best Female Vocalist four times. 
A New Zealand Order of Merit recipient for services to music. Bic is also acclaimed for her collaborations and live performances with other music icons, such as Tim and Neil Finn, Sir Dave Dobbyn and Anika Moa. She’s also inspired and influenced a new generation of New Zealand musicians. Lorde described her as “New Zealand music royalty” when she performed on stage with Bic in 2019.

Bob McNeill & Emily Roughton in concert, Bob McNeill & Emily Roughton in concert
DATE: Saturday Sept 27
TIME: 7pm
LOCATION: The Offering – 65 Main St, Greytown
AGES:
COST: $25 pp at the door or booking link below

Bob McNeill & Emily Roughton are two of New Zealand’s best-known folk musicians. They bring their deep musical connection to festivals across New Zealand, playing their favourite songs and tunes collected over years of playing together at festivals, stages and late into the night at kitchen tables. Based in Wellington, Bob is one of NZ’s best-known folk songwriters and a favourite with Greytown audiences. His songs have been covered by artists in NZ, Australia, the UK and the USA. New Zealand Musician magazine compared his songwriting to Bruce Springsteen and Mark Knopfler; the Dominion Post likened him to Jackson Brown, James Taylor, Luka Bloom and Dougie Ma¬cLean. A guitarist, he is known for his distinctive open-tuned acoustic fingerstyle and electric guitar playing. He has toured widely in NZ, Australia, Canada, Ireland, the UK and the USA. His latest album, released in June 2024, is Lost Stars, an extended release on CD and download featuring new recordings and rarities, with Emily on violin and piano.

From Whangarei, Emily is a virtuoso violinist inspired by the Scottish tradition and the modern trad movement. Classically trained, she is infinitely adaptable with her gorgeous stylings and fiery tune playing, making her the perfect foil for Bob’s lyrical songs.

Don’t miss a chance to see these two consummate musicians share their foot-stomping collection of banging tunes, favourite songs and stolen moments from the last 20 years.

Book your tickets here:
https://greytownarttown.com/bob-mcneill-and-emily-roughton-in-concert/

description:
Concert Pianist Nikolai Saratovsky returns to Paekakariki - JUNE 14, A VERY SPECIAL PIANIST RETURNS TO NEW ZEALAND:
MULLED WINE CONCERTS PRESENTS NIKOLAI SARATOVSKY
Nikolai Saratovsky is an internationally acclaimed Russian concert pianist with an extraordinary repertoire. Mary Gow, organiser of the Paekakariki-based Mulled Wine Concerts discovered Saratovsky in 2018 when he played in Brussels as a young pianist after succeeding in several important piano competitions in Europe. "I was amazed by his virtuosity" says Gow, a concert pianist herself, "He not only had a love for the music, he had all the technical skill-set you need to express yourself fully on the piano". She told him she came from New Zealand and he then told her that he and his Japanese-born wife had always dreamed of visiting New Zealand! As Gow notes, "from there, it was a short step to discussing possibilities..."
His effect on audiences here was remarkable - everyone who heard him knew that they were seeing and hearing something special. Since then, audiences around the world have come to the same conclusion. Saratovsky is now a professor of piano at the huge music school of Taiwan University where he combines teaching and academic research with his performing career, appearing in major concert venues worldwide. He also gives master-classes for aspiring international concert pianists.
Nikolai himself says this of his visits here: "This will be already the fifth time I am coming to NZ, and every time I feel extremely happy to come. I have lived and worked in Taiwan for more than 6 years. I have many memories from NZ. New Zealand is very different from Taiwan, and for me it's very important to "charge my inner spiritual battery". Coming to New Zealand is the ideal choice. Combination of meeting my lovely friends, conversations beside the fire place, fantastic sunsets, and music making makes this trip truly remarkable" He has chosen a wonderful set of music for his recital: "I chose this program by myself, because at this moment of life I prefer to play something that gives me a positive energy. I feel very compassionate with these music works, and they help me to recover during difficult times. I am happy to share this beautiful music with the audience, and I am looking forward for this fascinating musical journey". The concert will start with Western European romantic composers and conclude with pieces by Tchaikovsky and Rachmaninoff.
Mary Gow feels that his visit to New Zealand represents a wonderful opportunity for Kapiti audiences to catch a star already well known in Europe, Russia and the Far East. "This concert I regard as one of the most important and for the North Island, not-to-be-missed!" Mulled Wine Concerts will sponsor his appearance at the Paekakariki Memorial Hall on Sunday, June 14.
==============================
Mulled Wine Concerts presents a piano recital by Nikolai Saratovsky at 2:30 PM on Sunday 14 June, 2026 at the Paekakariki Memorial Hall, The Parade, Paekakariki.
Tickets: $35 adults ($15 students under 14).

description:
Elegance - Wellington, Elegance - Wellington
Dynamic British Isata Kanneh-Mason make her NZSO debut in a concert featuring Mozart, Brahms and Andrée.

Programme:
Andrée Andante Recitative
WA Mozart Piano Concerto No. 27
Brahms Serenade No. 1

Isata Kanneh-Mason, the eldest sibling in a dynasty of extraordinary musicians, is being lauded as a pianist who is “the real deal” (classical-scene.com). What a treat to hear her bring such intelligent elegance to Mozart’s last piano concerto. Praised by BBC Music Magazine as capable of making “lines sing beautifully and virtuosic passages dance, finding intimacy and eloquence at telling moments”, Kanneh-Mason is the perfect performer to bring this mature, serenely lovely concerto to Aotearoa New Zealand audiences.

To round out this programme, the NZSO performs two works that deserve a wider audience. Brahms’ Serenade harks back to Mozart’s own delightful serenades, while Elfrida Andrée’s Andante Recitative, written in 1878, was only rediscovered in the 1980s, and “open[s] in broody darkness, but quickly blossom[s] into optimistic, songful melody” (Michael Clive).

description:
Handel's Messiah, Celebrate the festive season with a magnificent performance of Handel’s Messiah on Saturday, 13 December, at 7:30 pm in the Michael Fowler Centre. Presented by Orpheus Choir Wellington in collaboration with Orchestra Wellington, this timeless masterpiece has been a beacon of holiday joy for centuries, blending grandeur, beauty, and drama in equal measure.

Under the direction of Brent Stewart, Music Director of Orpheus Choir Wellington and one of New Zealand’s leading conductors, this performance promises to capture the full brilliance of Handel’s most beloved work. From the exuberance of Worthy is the Lamb to the powerful The Trumpet Shall Sound and the transcendent Hallelujah Chorus, Messiah is a musical journey that inspires and uplifts like no other.

Joining Brent is a stellar lineup of soloists. Emma Pearson, recognised for her captivating performances on international stages, brings brilliance and artistry. Mezzo-soprano Maaike Christie-Beekman adds depth and warmth with her rich, expressive voice. Rising tenor Lila LJ Crichton contributes freshness and flair, while Lexus Song Quest winner Joel Amosa grounds the quartet with his commanding bass.

The Michael Fowler Centre, renowned for its superb acoustics and stunning architecture, provides the perfect setting for this extraordinary concert. With its sweeping choruses, unforgettable arias, and sheer emotional power, Messiah is the ultimate way to mark the festive season.

Come and join us for an evening of musical brilliance that will have you saying, Hallelujah!

description:
Jazz Orchestra Composer Series Presents Callum Allardice, The eleventh concert in our series of Aotearoa jazz composers features award winning composer and performer Callum Allardice, with a new suite of music for rhythm section and strings; Ode to Sadness.

A collection of songs, old and new, presented alongside some of the works that inspired them. From intimate improvisations and poignant melodies to soaring strings, the music moves through moments of reverence, reflection, and quiet triumph. Sometimes solemn, sometimes radiant, but always beautiful, Ode To Sadness is a celebration of the beauty found in sorrow.

Callum is an award-winning composer and guitarist based in New Zealand. He is a three-time recipient of the APRA Best Jazz Composition award for his works ‘Sons of Thunder’ (2016), ‘Deep Thought’ (2017), and ‘Chungin’ (2019). In 2020 he and his group The Jac, received the Recorded Music NZ Best Jazz Artist award for their album ‘A Gathering’, and in 2022 he was the inaugural Te Kōkī - New Zealand School of Music jazz composer-in-residence.

The Jazz Orchestra Composer Series showcases original music for large jazz ensemble by New Zealand composers. Concerts take place every 1st and 3rd Friday of the month, from May to October, from 7pm. Tickets are $15, door sales $20.

Thanks to Creative New Zealand for their generous support.

description:

International jazz supergroup LVDF bring their genre-bending, globally informed sound to New Zealand for an exclusive appearance at the Wellington Jazz Festival.
All acclaimed bandleaders in their own right, LVDF is a cross-cultural quartet featuring Myele Manzanza (NZ/UK) on drums, Alex Hitchcock (USA/UK) on saxophone, Michelangelo Scandroglio (ITALY) on double bass and special guest Daniel Hayles (NZ) on piano and synths (stepping in for Maria Chiara Argirò). Their fresh sound fuses jazz with electronic textures, global rhythms and raw improvisation.
With Wellington-raised Myele Manzanza returning from London for this special hometown performance, LVDF will perform his groundbreaking Festival commission Music for a Multi-Polar World. This bold new work explores shifting global narratives through sound and draws on events from Brexit to the conflicts in Gaza, Sudan and Congo. Manzanza reflects “I’ve noticed how much the geopolitical shifts have unsettled and angered me, as well as shifting and widening my views on the world, and giving me some things to be hopeful for amidst change.” The work channels both the uncertainty and hope of a rapidly changing world.
The set will also feature tracks from LVDF’s upcoming self-titled EP - a bold and electric statement from a group as diverse in experience as it is unified in vision.
Only in Wellington - don’t miss the debut of one of modern jazz’s most exciting new ensembles, live at Meow Nui.
Commissioned by Wellington Jazz Festival
This LVDF performance is supported by Help Musicians UK, Embassy of Italy, Wellington & Comites Nuova Zelanda

description:
Ludovico Einaudi | Wellington - Michael Fowler Centre, Ludovico Einaudi
Sunday 1 February 2026
Michael Fowler Centre
The world’s most popular classical music composer, Italian pianist, Ludovico Einaudi, returns to Australia and New Zealand this January with his new album The Summer Portraits.
He has performed on an Arctic ice-floe for Greenpeace and has seen his music become the soundtrack for Oscar and Golden Globe winning films ('Les Intouchables', 'Nomadland', 'The Father') and TikTok phenomena (his 2012 track 'Experience' exploded on the app) alike. From his earliest work composing for theatre and ballet in the 1980s to his multi-million-selling albums like 'In a Time Lapse' and his popular soundtracks across film and television, Einaudi has drawn upon neo-classical, pop, ambient, rock and experimental styles to create a sound that crosses boundaries and generations, becoming the world’s best known – and most streamed – classical music artist in the process.
In January 2025, Einaudi released 'The Summer Portraits'. The record is a lush return to full-band textures and is the result of a cascade of personal memories triggered by sun, summer and family holidays. On his last Australian tour, before a gig at the Sydney Opera House, Einaudi sat down and started composing the single 'Rose Bay', based on his sense impressions of the bay his grandfather made home.
Don’t miss your chance to experience the world’s most popular contemporary classical artist.

description:
NZTrio presents Hypnotique, Described as a “national treasure” and “New Zealand’s most indispensable ensemble”, NZTrio He Taonga Wairere is renowned for its eclectic repertoire, outstanding talent and warm kiwi stage presence. Bringing together three incredibly accomplished artists, every NZTrio performance powerfully reaffirms the importance and cathartic nature of a live musical experience in today’s digital world.

Hypnotique presents a diverse array of works that challenges expectations of traditional chamber music. A whirlwind of motion typifies NZ composer Lyell Cresswell's virtuosic Moto Perpetuo, ahead of Fauré's Piano Trio in D minor with lyrical elegance and lush harmonic textures, contrasting with the percussive and electronic influences in Le Boeuf's jazz-adjacent Obliquely Wrecked. Australian composer Elena Kats-Chernin pays homage to Haydn, blending classical and contemporary styles in Calliope Dreaming, then finally, the full Romantic immersion of Schönberg's Verklärte Nacht is structured around the five stanzas of a poem; deeply transcendent and utterly beautiful.

The Programme (2 hours including 20min interval)

Lyell Cresswell (NZ) - Moto perpetuo
Gabriel Fauré - Piano Trio in D minor, Op. 120
Pascal Le Boeuf - Obliquely Wrecked
Elena Kats-Chernin - Calliope Dreaming
Arnold Schönberg - Verklärte Nacht arr. for piano trio

Poems and Songs from the Road

After seasons of wandering through foreign cities, sharing songs with strangers, and capturing stories from the road. PEBBLE has spent the past few years on an open-ended journey: traveling across continents in search of the deepest stories, the wildest love, the purest expression of what it means to be human. From late-night train stations to hidden cafés, from sunlit rooftops to candlelit stages—PEBBLE has been gathering moments and melodies from everywhere he goes, transforming them into songs and poems that reflect a life lived wide open.

“Love in Every City” is the next chapter in that journey—a stripped-back, soul-forward performance that brings those stories home.

Backed by a vision to build a global movement of traveling artists who choose authenticity over perfection, connection over isolation, and creative ownership over compromise, PEBBLE’s work invites us to remember what we’re really here for: to live, to feel, to share.

This show is a moment of reflection and reconnection—
Join us for an intimate night of music, poetry, and storytelling at Moon in Newtown, Pōneke. A suitcase full of songs. A guitar by the table. A heart full of cities.

Born in West Virginia and raised on the Canadian prairies, Scott Cook quit a job teaching kindergarten in Taiwan in 2007 to embark on the life of a full-time troubadour. He’s toured nearly nonstop across Canada, the US, Europe, Asia, Australia, New Zealand and elsewhere ever since, living out of backpacks and campervans, averaging over a hundred shows and a dozen summer festivals a year, and distilling his experiences into empathetic, keenly observant verse. Since 2022 he’s been joined full-time by his sweetheart Pamela Mae on upright bass and vocals, crisscrossing 45 US States and 8 Canadian provinces in their campervan Roadetta, and covering a fair bit of Australia in their HiAce Hector. In 2026 they’re bringing the duo project to New Zealand for the first time with an extensive tour of the North and South Islands in support of Cook's eighth album Troubadourly Yours. Fresh from the open road, these are sturdy, straight-talking songs that see the good in you.

“Whip-smart, bone-achingly lovely, socially committed songs presented with a bold, elegant directness evoking the very best of the folk music tradition. Last night's performance in Notional Space was a thing of rare beauty.” —Mark Jacobs, presenter, Notional Space

“He sings his heart and soul, and in doing so lets light flood into your own... He has a good eye for imagery, a gentle human touch, a wry sense of humour, a whole lot of integrity, a warm, rugged voice and a bunch of memorable lines... Truly one of Woody Guthrie's children.” –RnR Magazine

description:
The Wooden Box Band at Greytown Upclose and Personal, The Wooden Box Band in concert 4pm 19 October in Cobblestones Museum new gallery.
The Wooden Box Band has some of Wellington’s best known musicians getting together and having fun playing the kind of music they love.


Songster Jessie Moss came from Jessie James and the Outlaws which was a staple of the Newtown scene a few years back. Newtown Rocksteady musician Jeremy Desmond has been in the Wooden Box band for many years bringing an array of guitar tones on his bright red Gibson 335 and effects pedals. On bass is the busiest bassist in town, Murray Costello, who cut his musical teeth in the Mockers during the eighties and has been playing hard ever since.

He plays an electric upright to bring bottom end to the urban folk sound. Together with Jessie Moss the other main songwriter in the band is local luthier Paddy Burgin, who’ s also busy with the Zimmermans and other acoustic and electric groups around the capital. He features on acoustic guitar, slide guitar and keyboards. The front row of singers is completed with Emily Clemmett who also brings her trumpet and fiddle to the party, and together with Jessie and Paddy these three produce thrilling harmonies reminiscent of the Mamas and the Papas.

On drums we have Search for Yeti man Sean Barker who keeps a very lively beat going behind the rest of the musicians. He’s also on quips and humour.
Their music has a sixties vibe with the tones and harmonies. They believe in adventurous tuneful songs with universal themes that people can relate to. And they perform them in a very engaging manner. Expect to be toe- tapping and even singing along!
The Wooden Box Band’s latest album, Broken River, was released over the winter. You can find them on Spotify for a preview.

description:
Tom Callwood | Ant Donaldson | Lucien Johnson | Jonny Marks | Dayle Jellyman, Five of Pōneke's finest improvisors converge on the Pyramid Club to channel "electronic space jazz"!
-
Tom Callwood (double bass) is an improvisor and collaborator who has performed throughout NZ and the UK. He’s a regular in the local experimental and popular music scenes with bands including The Phoenix Foundation, Teeth & Devils Gate Outfit.
-
Anthony Donaldson is one of this country's great drummers and a pioneer of improvised music in Aotearoa. He has been a creative force in Wellington music for over four decades and continues to push the boundaries of accepted musical norms.
-
Lucien Johnson is a New Zealand saxophonist, composer, and theatre maker. In recent years he has focussed on creating his own unique jazz sound, shrouded in wonder and mystique. His last album, “Wax///Wane” received rave reviews internationally, with France Musique calling it “Bewitching and Astonishing” and London Jazz News describing it as “Mystical, a touch retro and increasingly spellbinding”.
-
Dayle Jellyman is a keyboardist, guitarist, composer and man of many bands - from regular jazz sessions to the positive punk of Love Party and the apocalyptic metal of Fvkvshima.
-
Vocalist and electronic musician Jonny Marks has been a key figure in the creative music scene in Wellington since the early 2000s. Modulating his vocal chords like a synthesizer, Jonny moves between sub-bass drones to ring modulated whistle tones with his voice alone - and now in a spellbinding combination with a beloved Synthi AKS.

description:
Violet Hirst Summer Tour: Hataitai Bowling Club Wellington, Contemporary singer-songwriter Violet Hirst tours small Aotearoa venues this summer. An evening of layered vocals, familiar melodies and unique songwriting supported by Madeleine Dove.
Born and raised in Tāhuna Queenstown, Violet's musical journey began the day she was born: opening night of her mother's musical Kitchens. Her songs and live performance embody the theatrics and ballads that surrounded her childhood. Gaining comparisons to Aldous Harding and Julia Jacklin, Hirst’s songs combine hypnotic vocal melodies with meditative rhythms and poignant lyrics from a young woman. After touring the USA as a support musician for Flying Nun rockers Office Dog, Hirst is back on the road to share her own new works.
Her debut album Donegal was recorded in Central Otago with De Stevens (Roundhead Studios, Marlin's Dreaming) and Reuben Scott (Saltwater Criminals, Molly Payton). The album received a Student Radio nomination for Best Album, charting on both SRN and Radioscope charts. Followed with a nationwide tour and sold-out shows, Hirst is excited to return to the road for the first time since then. Joined by Madeleine Dove (vocals, keys) the duo will perform new contemporary meditations and vocal experiments.
“(Donegal) is brimming with the confidence of an artist fully inhabiting their own sound; wistful and slightly heartbroken, but unencumbered by expectation." - RNZ
“Evident to everyone present was how special that rainy night was, how flawless, nuanced and emotive Hirst’s singing and songwriting. The real deal, with the crowd standing in the rain outside afterwards, not ready to leave, raving.” - NZ Musician
https://violethirst.bandcamp.com/

description:
Vorn and his Prog Consort / Thagomizer, Vorn and his Prog Consort / Thagomizer
Wellington legend Vorn Colgan has been writing and releasing extraordinary and odd popular music from bedrooms across Aotearoa and the world since 1999, a career which was scheduled to be cut short in 2019 by a terminal cancer diagnosis. 2023 saw him release his surprisingly non-posthumous hit The Late Album, and given his demonstrated inability to die he was left with maybe the world's most wonderful problem: what to record for his 10th album?

The answer is The Aeronaut, a 60ish minute meditation on Wellington, the universe, and everything, hewn from purest regionally-sourced prog rock and presented in a single baffling and hopefully pleasant serving. The Aeronaut is currently still a work in progress; this evening offers keen punters a chance to watch Vorn and his frighteningly good band (Nick Brown - Drums; Charley Davenport - Bass, Thomas Liggett - Violin) iron out the final kinks on a future Kiwi classic. Be there so you can say you were!

https://vornpowertool.bandcamp.com/

Thagomizer is the dino synth project (dinosaur themed dungeon synth) of Caspar Kneale (yes, he is related, in fact mr Birchville Cat Motel is Caspar's Dad). Inspired by the vibe of retro dinosaur media, Thagomizer aims to summon a Mesozoic mood to transport you back in time. As far as we know, Thagomizer is the only dino synth project in the country.

An evening with David Sedaris, He’s been referred to as the God of the comic essay. Author David Sedaris is a savant of sardonic wit. Wellington gets to experience his razor-sharp sense of humour when he visits to promote his latest book - ‘The Land and Its People’. David will take to the stage to read from the collection of essays and freshly minted diary entries. This will be followed by a candid audience Q&A session and an extended book signing that — true to form — will run as long as it needs to.   
In ‘The Land and Its People’ he reflects on what it means to be a foreigner, a brother, and a lifelong friend — trying on the role of caretaker after his partner Hugh’s hip-replacement surgery. Equal parts tender and devastating, it’s classic Sedaris: the kind of writing that makes you laugh until you feel guilty, then laugh again anyway. It has been said that listening to him read is an affirming, joyful experience that leaves a person feeling as if their cup has been filled right to the brim.

description:
Myths & Legends - Wellington, Myths & Legends - Wellington
Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works with conductor Pietari Inkinen and NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen.

Programme:
Sibelius Pohjola’s Daughter
Magnus Lindberg Violin Concerto No. 2 (NZ Premiere)
Sibelius Lemminkäinen Suite

Aotearoa New Zealand’s dramatic landscapes chime in kind with a country half a world away: Finland. In this concert, Arctic North meets Pacific South in a programme of heart-stirring Finnish works that resonate with audiences here.

Pietari Inkinen leads the Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Finnish composer Magnus Lindberg’s Second Violin Concerto, with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen as soloist. This duo of Finnish talent are the perfect team to evoke the work’s “massive, expansive ... panoramic vista ... of dark clouds over forests and lakes, of repressed passions and baleful desires” (Financial Times).

We pair this contemporary Finnish masterpiece with a past master. Sibelius’ Pohjola’s Daughter and Lemminkäinen Suite were both inspired by the ancient epic the Kalevala. The latter describes the mythological adventures of the wizard Väinämöinen, the hero Lemminkäinen and their entanglement with the primordial forces of nature, death and magic.

description:
Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time | Wellington, Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time | Wellington
Aotearoa Music Award-winning and Taite Award-winning artist Vera Ellen releases her new album Heaven Knows What Time. on May 1 via Flying Nun Records. Alongside the album release, Vera Ellen returns to Aotearoa in July for a six-date national tour in celebration of Heaven Knows What Time.

The title Heaven Knows What Time. arrived while Vera was lying on the top bunk of a house truck in Buenos Aires, nearly two years after writing the record and almost a year after completing the mix. After multiple working titles, it surfaced with clarity and immediacy - less a decision than a moment of recognition. It reflects the album’s central tension: frustration and surrender to forces outside of control. As Vera describes it, creativity cannot be demanded - it can be nurtured, but ultimately arrives in its own time, “like a baby”.

The album was written during a two-week songwriting residency in Greytown, awarded through the NZ Pacific Studio Artist Residency Programme. The residency provided space and solitude away from touring and performance, culminating in a performance at Studio 73 for fellow residents and members of the local community.
‍

In her residency application, Vera wrote: “After the heaviness of Ideal Home Noise, I feel it is pressing that I now create an uplifting record that has a guiding message of hope, but from a matured perspective.” While that intention is present, Heaven Knows What Time. resists neat resolution, moving through themes of love, joy, self-assurance, humour, moodiness, and heartbreak - positioning Vera as an observer of both inner and outer worlds.

Alongside extensive touring in Aotearoa — including the 2025 Laneway Festival — Vera has performed internationally with her band, including a 14-date tour of China, a sold-out run in Australia supporting Crowded House, appearances at New Colossus Festival and SXSW (Austin and Sydney), and a full UK/EU support tour with Yumi Zouma. She is set to support Aldous Harding on her full UK/EU tour and perform at The Great Escape in Brighton. The Guardian described her performance as: “Arising New Zealand empress Vera Ellen and band were a revelation, a shimmering reminder that pop’n’roll can still nudge one’s soul.”

Kiwi rock fans are in for the ultimate celebration of grunge history as The Pearl Jam Experience crosses the Tasman to deliver a definitive, career-spanning greatest hits set. This special tour will honour the massive catalog of the Seattle icons, delivering a full-throttle, high-energy performance packed to the brim with Pearl Jam’s biggest anthems and fan favourites.
Widely regarded as the premier tribute to Pearl Jam, the band is renowned for recreating the atmosphere, the madness, and most importantly, the sonically accurate music that defined a generation.
Their commitment to the music’s authenticity goes beyond the stage. In a remarkable nod to Pearl Jam’s golden era, the band recently recorded a collaborative cover of the hit song Go with former Pearl Jam drummer Dave Abbruzzese. Abbruzzese, who drove the rhythm section during the band's peak explosive years, lent his signature powerful drumming to the track and mixed it for the group.
The Pearl Jam Experience also maintains a deep connection to the band's philanthropic legacy. They are proud supporters of the EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the largest nonprofit funding research for a cure for Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), co-founded by Jill and Eddie Vedder.
For New Zealand fans, this is the ultimate chance to experience a high-octane concert that embodies the true sound and spirit of Pearl Jam, delivered with the energy, precision, and respect this legendary rock catalog deserves.

description:
Cacao & Connection, Cacao & Connection
This evening is about real connection - the kind that happens when guards soften, and we don’t have to perform or impress.

We will all share cacao, and have conversations that feel a little more meaningful than everyday small talk.

How the evening unfolds:

We’ll begin with a short grounding exercise to help everyone arrive and settle. Life is hectic, and this is a moment to pause and land before moving into connection.

We’ll then share a cacao ceremony in a circle. Cacao is known for gently opening the heart space and supporting presence and openness. It’s subtle and grounding rather than dramatic.

From there, the circle opens for a heartshare experience. A reflective question will be offered as a prompt, and each person is invited (but never expected) to share from their own experience. This is not about fixing or advising - it’s about speaking honestly, listening deeply, and being witnessed.

The evening ends with a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket. Conversations can continue!

What heartsharing can offer

A sense of true connection
Being seen and heard as you are can soften feelings of loneliness and remind you that you’re not alone in what you carry.

Honest, meaningful conversation
Heartsharing moves beyond small talk, creating space for authenticity, vulnerability, and real presence.

Deeper self-understanding
Listening and sharing with others often brings clarity around your own feelings, needs, and experiences.

Gentle personal growth
There’s something quietly powerful about speaking from the heart and listening without judgement - it often opens new perspectives in unexpected ways.

Emotional support and wellbeing
Sharing in a respectful, non-judgemental space can feel grounding, relieving, and deeply human.

A few things worth knowing

You’re very welcome to come alone - many people do. There’s no expectation to know anyone, and no pressure to speak if you don’t want to.

You don’t need to be experienced with cacao ceremonies or heartsharing, or “good at talking.” Curiosity, openness, and presence are more than enough.

The evening concludes with a plant-based dinner & dessert - all included in your ticket.

Meet Andre, your host
Andre has been exploring the art of authentic connection since his teens, when a rite of passage in Golden Bay first sparked his passion for circle work. Since then, he has been creating spaces that invite honesty, vulnerability, and depth — guiding people into experiences of being truly seen and heard. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and breathwork facilitator, Andre brings creativity and presence to all his offerings, inspired by the question of what it really means to be human.

description:
A Day in the Heart - One Day Silent Yoga and Meditation Retreat, A Day in the Heart - One Day Silent Yoga and Meditation Retreat
An invitation to press "pause" for a day, and just Be.

To drop from the busy mind into the silence of the Heart.

And to remember the freedom of who you are, when you're not in a role.


This lovingly crafted offering is a day immersion into practice, providing a glimpse of what the experience of silence can offer.

Suitable for complete beginners in meditation and yoga, as well as for advanced practitioners who'd like to unplug and enjoy retreat-time.


The schedule will include:

- Multiple seated meditation sessions with guidance

- Walking meditation

- Mindful Hatha Yoga and Restorative Yoga sessions

- Yoga Nidra

- Cacao to open the Heart

- Time to journal, walk in nature, or just be


Cost for a whole day program + 2 meals: $195


Food:

breakfast and lunch - nutritious vegan meals prepared with love + tea and cacao


Location:

the Lotus Yoga Centre in Paraparaumu


Date: 22nd August 2026 Saturday

Duration: 7.30am - 5.30pm

please arrive at 7.15am to settle in and start on time


To book, please purchase your ticket below or email Radha for more info at


*WHY IS THIS A SILENT RETREAT? A silent retreat means that everyone participating observes mauna, noble silence (apart from the teacher/ the guide). This means no casual chats and conversations, but also no use of phone or any devices during the day. The practice of silence allows the the mind to quieten down significantly, it is a very unique, deeply purifying and enlightening experience. It creates space for a deep insight and a proper reset, even in the short span of one day.


*WHY MEDITATION? Meditation is known for thousands of years as one of the most powerful practices, within and outside of spiritual context. It is good not only for creating a state of calm or relaxation, but also is the best known path to self-knowledge and self-love. When we retreat into silence beyond mind, there is an unmistakable feeling of being back home, in the heart of being, a sense of connection and purpose.


*WHY "A DAY IN THE HEART"? The Heart/ Hridaya in Sanskrit is a synonym of awareness or presence. According to the great yogis and the non-dual philosophy, the Heart is a place to centre in our meditations, but also an organ of knowledge and the seat of our true Self. When the mind is quiet and we centre within, the Heart can awaken - bringing a sense of being back home, back to what truly matters, back to our Self.

As Rumi said, "Close your eyes, fall in love, stay there"

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life.

There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.
Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999.
