description:
Hands-on Sourdough Workshop, Sourdough for Beginners - $120 (paid via internet banking)
Come join us for a hands-on, in-person sourdough workshop at Willow Corner Collective headquarters (aka my home)! This workshop is currently the only hands-on sourdough workshop being offered in the Nelson region - I teach and demonstrate to you and then you get to mix and practice on your own dough as we go along.
Whether you're a seasoned baker or a beginner, this event is perfect for anyone looking to master the art of making sourdough bread, learning from someone who has 10+ years of experience. Perhaps you've found all the Youtube tutorials and Instagram how-to's overwhelming and are keen to learn via an in-person class. Then this is for you! I've baked hundreds of loaves in the last year alone, sold at a market, and hosted a pop-up shop. However, my passion really lies with teaching others to bake their own sourdough in their own homes, for their own families (or small businesses - one day!).You will be taught, demonstrated to, and then you get to have a go yourself; whilst learning my tips and tricks along the way. Plus we finish by sampling some delicious, fresh artisan sourdough with some favourite toppings!
You'll go home with all you need to make a good loaf of sourdough bread:
Knowledge
Student Guide, including recipes and troubleshoot guide
Bowl, liner, bowl scraper, and razor blade... all the tools you'd need to make sourdough
Dough made in class to bake the next day at home, to wow your family/friends
Confidence to continue the process yourself
Healthy, bubbling starter to continue your journey at home
Continued support and encouragement via our own private Facebook community group, for class attendees only
Note: You will have your dough to take home after the workshop that will need shaping around 6-8pm, so please ensure that will work for you that day.Also, please double check the date when booking. If for some reason you are unable to attend on the day, due to time constraints, I am unable to refund your ticket. I am happy for you to send someone in your place, though. In extenuating circumstances I may be able to hold your ticket for a future workshop; this is decided on a case-by-case basis.
*Payment to clear in bank account two days after ticket bought, after which time your ticket will be released on to someone else. Please pay immediately upon purchasing ticket.
**All workshop info you need to know ahead of time is in the confirmation email. Please ensure you read this down to the bottom.
***I recommend you already have a pair of digital scales, and a cast iron dutch oven at home to bake your loaf with as this makes the best, artisan sourdough, with great rise. Alternatively, a large, lidded casserole dish or enamel roasting pan work also. (The lids are a necessity).

"Sarah’s sour dough class is for real life! Achieve beautiful delicious bread easily in your own kitchen. Sarah teaches you how to fit sourdough into your busy life. She clearly and passionately gives the essential information, tips and tricks to make your own loaf. I loved getting to have a go at each step in the process. I love Sarah’s catchy philosophy “The goal is good bread, not perfect bread.” This took all the pressure off, for me, and I left the class empowered with all the knowledge and skills needed to give it a go at home. I appreciated the thoughtful and well prepared resources Sarah gave us. Thank you!" - Megan

"Sourdough with Sarah was a delight! From feeling overwhelmed and giving up on the idea of ever making my own loaf of sourdough, to dancing with joy as i watch a beautiful perfect sourdough loaf get nice and golden in the homewood stove!The information was packaged in bite sizes with hands on practice in between, where we all got to experience each step of the whole process, which was cleverly condensed and prepared so that despite normally having waits in between, we were able to see it all play out in a short few hours!The process was beautifully organised with attention to detail that had us fawning, came away feeling so blessed and privileged!Sarah's glowing personality made all the information feel easy and palatable, it was so fun!Such a lovely time, great environment to learn with ease." -Melody

description:
Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar, Alexia Urban Winery x Greytown Distilling Company present: Micro Aperitivo - Neighbourhood Vermouth Bar

Aperitivo – it’s the Italian pre-dinner beverage ritual designed to open the palate, open the stomach, and open the conversation.

Wander past any Italian bar as the sun goes down, and you’ll see the locals sipping martinis and negronis, while engaged in animated discussion!

The common ingredient in these cocktails…and conversations is vermouth – a delicious, aromatic, botanical-loaded, fortified wine. Wine, you say? That’s where we come in. Alexia has been working with Greytown Distilling to create a vermouth for them right here in Greytown, and they’ve asked us to host something fun to celebrate its release for the Greytown International Cocktail Festival!

We’re channelling vermouths Italian roots and transforming into a little pop-up Italian neighbourhood vermouth bar!

We’ll be serving the most intriguing (and cutest) cocktail flight in town to showcase the beauty and versatility of vermouth… the ‘vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray’ - a cocktail broken into three micro parts: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni.

All the Alexia wines will be available too, of course, and it’s Italian all the way in the kitchen, with guest chef Caleb Kloeg turning out crispy arancini and gelato soft-serves so delicious you’ll be transported to Italy.

Cocktail inspired? You’re in luck. Greytown Distilling will have a little pop-up shop on the night, selling all the essential cocktail-making accessories too.

It’s neighbourhood Italian bar vibes on a Greytown backstreet, and we can’t wait… so get on your vespas, pump up the tyres on your Bianchi, rev those Fiats and get to Alexia!

Vermouth micro-trio cocktail tray

The most intriguing cocktail in town…a single cocktail broken into a micro-flight showcasing the beauty and versatility of vermouth: micro vermouth on the rocks, micro gin martini, and micro negroni. Shrunken, not stirred…

Essential details: 4pm – 8pm, Friday 27 March, Alexia Urban Winery, 197 West Street, Greytown. No bookings required, just turn up. GF? Yes. Vegan? Yes. Leashed dogs ok. This is a rain or shine event, so don’t miss out!

This beer is the ultimate expression of Wild Workshop’s inner-city terroir, and the 2024 bottle is no different; a blend of five years of 100% spontaneously fermented brews, aged in French oak. The result is a complex and truly unique drop that harnesses the natural character of Pōneke.
We love this beer, and we’re so chuffed that other people do too - we’re very honoured that Chance, Luck & Magic, in its various vintages, has garnered global recognition and become one of our most prestigious creations:
Silver medals at both the 2023 and 2024 World Beer Cup (huge!)
Four consecutive gold medals at the New Zealand Beer Awards, as well as two trophies for Champion European Ale, and the Champion Beer title in 2022
Champion International Beer at the 2024 Australian International Beer Awards
The release of each new edition has become a landmark annual event for us, a chance to take a moment and appreciate the beautiful things that come from the wild workings of the environment.

description:
The wines of the South, An Evening of French Terroir
A Wine Dinner Featuring Provence & Bordeaux Thursday 5th of March 6.30pm
Join us for a refined culinary journey through two of France’s most celebrated wine regions. This exclusive wine dinner pairs a thoughtfully curated four course menu with exceptional selections from Domaine Peyrassol in Provence and Château Malescasse in Bordeaux.
Domaine Peyrassol – Provence

Nestled in the sun-drenched hills of Provence, Domaine Peyrassol crafts elegant wines that capture the essence of the Mediterranean landscape. Known for their refined rosés and expressive whites, these wines offer vibrant freshness, delicate fruit, and a whisper of coastal minerality.


Château Malescasse – Bordeaux

From the prestigious Haut-Médoc appellation of Bordeaux, Château Malescasse produces structured, expressive reds rooted in gravelly soils and generations of expertise. Expect layered aromas of dark berries, subtle spice, and velvety tannins that speak to classic Bordeaux character.


The Evening
Aperitif on Arrival;
4 course seasonal tasting menu
Guided wine pairings and tasting notes
Insight into the history and philosophy of both estates
This is more than a dinner—it is a celebration of craftsmanship, terroir, and the timeless harmony between food and wine.
Reserve your seat and savour the flavours of Provence and Bordeaux.
$150pp

description:
Mediterranea, At Cicio Cacio Osteria, the Mediterranean comes to the table in an intimate dinner shaped by memory and place. Inspired by the owner's childhood on a Mediterranean island, this dinner traces a path from Italy to Spain, across Greece and into the Middle East, with dishes from each region reflecting the shared spirit of the Mediterranean: the sun, the sea, the music, the nostalgia, the being in the moment. The food is uncomplicated and entirely enjoyable, simple, fare focused on freshness and simplicity, letting the ingredients speak for themselves. Expect the most perfect hummus with grilled pita, the best Spanish tortilla, uncommon seafood like octopus and sardines, couscous, lamb, and goat, pastas, and colourful salads, a true insight into the Mediterranean spirit. 

You'll be seated at a long communal table in front of a real fire for a progressive nine-course menu, each plate paired with a matched wine selected to reflect its origin and character. Throughout the evening, the chef shares stories behind the dishes, offering insight into flavours, traditions, and personal history. You're invited to come into the kitchen and share the secrets of each recipe, cooking alongside the chef. A final musical touch ends an evening dedicated to the beauty, spontaneity, and simplicity of the Mediterranean. 

Your ticket includes nine courses, nine matched wines, storytelling, hands-on cooking, and recipe sharing.

description:
Découvrez Orléans - Workshop & Tasting, Overview



Join us and learn more about this beautiful town!
🌿 In the heart of the Centre-Val de Loire, along the banks of the Loire river, lies Orléans. A historic city of medieval streets, grand cathedrals and a legacy that helped shape the destiny of France.
This is the France of Jeanne d'Arc: the young heroine who, in 1429, freed the city from siege and helped turn the tide of the Hundred Years' War so decisively at the Battle of Patay that the French expression "mettre la pâtée" (to thrash someone) is said to trace back to it. Wander through the medieval old town, admire the soaring Cathédrale Sainte-Croix, the statues honouring Jeanne d'Arc, the lively place du Martroi and its historic carousel.
Join Lou for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and step into the history, traditions and art de vivre of Orléans from the famous Fêtes de Jeanne d'Arc to the Festival de Loire, and the region's culinary treasures: the wines of the Centre-Val de Loire, Orléans mustard, and the beloved Pithiviers.
And of course, we'll wrap up with a tasting of delicious traditional treats from the region!
🗯️ French A2/B1 level required
🗓️ Saturday, 8 August 2026, 11.30pm-1pm
📍 Alliance Française Wellington (78 Victoria Street, Wellington)
🎟️ $30 for AF members & $35 for non-members

Crying Tiger, Charcoal smoke, sizzling meat, and you're in Nong Khai, a small northeast Thai town where families gather around the grill for Crying Tiger steak. Beef steak marinated 48 hours in coriander root, garlic, black pepper, oyster sauce, palm sugar, whiskey, and mandarin juice, char-grilled until the meat weeps with its own juices.
The chef grew up cooking this dish with family and friends. It arrives with sticky rice and a Northern Thai Isarn dipping sauce of tamarind, lime juice, ground chillies, and fresh coriander. Alongside: a sharp granny smith apple salad dressed with chilli and fish sauce, topped with prawns; and tom zapp, slow-cooked pork soft bones that melt into a soup fragrant with kaffir lime, lemongrass, and ground rice.
This is a three course set menu for $75.  Alcohol can be purchased separately.  Minimum 2 orders per table.

Join us for full-day immersive experience in the viticulture, winemaking and wines of Te Muna Valley. Walk the vineyards, meet the producers, go behind the scenes and taste exceptional wines right where they are made.

description:
Daffodil Express 2025, Daffodil Express 2025
Carterton’s Daffodil Festival in the early Spring creates a great day out for the whole family. Why not travel there in style by a heritage train, let Steam Incorporated take the stress out of travel as you take the train to the Wairarapa. This year, our train has reduced capacity, so be sure to book in quickly!

Hauled by our heritage locomotives, take a glimpse into the bygone era of train travel as we clear the rush of Wellington, racing through the suburbs of Petone, Lower Hutt & Upper Hutt. After picking up the last of our passengers at Upper Hutt, we will race through the 8.8km long Rimutaka tunnel. This tunnel remains the longest in New Zealand with scheduled passenger trains, and has just been subjected to a full track relay for the first time since it was opened in 1955.

Passing through Featherston, we head east and navigate the rolling hills towards Carterton.

Arriving into Carterton, you'll have a few hours to disembark and go and explore Carterton's annual Daffodil Festival , before jumping on the train for the return journey home.

The Daffodil Fields and Festival
Located in the heart of the Wairarapa, Carterton’s popular Daffodil Festival offers an abundance of activities ranging from the famous Daffodil picking at Middlerun Farm, markets along High and Holloway Streets, the Big Wai Art sale in the events Centre, live music, and loads more family fun.

The festival features two major international acts making exclusive New Zealand debuts. Wellington will see two-time Grammy Award-winning jazz vocalist and bandleader, Gregory Porter and five-time Grammy Award-winning jazz singer, Samara Joy. Gregory Porter’s unique and timeless sound blends jazz, soul, and gospel. His influences include Bakersfield Southern Gospel and jazz legend Nat King Cole. At just 25 years old, Samara Joy has become a breakout jazz sensation. She’s redefining 21st-century jazz with a rich, mature tone and refined phrasing. 
The treats in the programme continue with Australian First Nations soul singer Bumpy, and a commissioned work by New Zealand/Congolese drummer, composer, and rhythm master  Myele Manzanza. He’ll be performing with international supergroup, lvdf. SUNDAY 28TH SEPTEMBER @ FUTUNA CHAPEL - KARORI
Three joyful houses, three families and three client stories about the commissioning, designing, building and living in homes designed by Ian Athfield.
SPENCER and DIANE LOGAN
1974 - 1978
WINDY POINT – EASTBOURNE
Photographer unknown
Spencer Logan and his wife Diane will talk about the commissioning of their first new home, its design, construction, the cleaning of thousands of bricks, and living in this unique collection of a pair of recycled brick towers with timber clad ‘saddlebags’. 
ROSS, CUSHLA and TESS JAMIESON
1974 - 1978
MAHINA BAY
Ross and Cushla have lived in their home on the Eastern hills above Mahina Bay for 48 years. They will, along with their youngest daughter, recount their experiences of working with Ian Athfield in the commissioning of the design of their home, the construction process and then living in this hillside hugging collection of building, and how this home may have influenced their living and the raising of a family of four children.
JONATHAN CUSTANCE   - THE CUSTANCE HOUSE 1981 – 1982
HAVELOCK NORTH
“The Custance House replaced an early modern home that burnt to the ground in 1981 leaving only the swimming pool unscathed.  Ray and Ann Custance, who were friends of the Athfields, sought a bold replacement.  With their son, industrial and interior designer Jonathan Custance, they prepared a four page brief for a new building….. “
Text taken from Athfield Architects by Julia Gatley 2012 AUP.
The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend this event and support the Trust in its work.
The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all funds raised from the Futuna Lecture Series go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust.

BVRBWYRE
BVRBWYRE is a Newtown-based DJ known for bass-driven sets that balance groove, variety, and pure dancefloor joy. Her selections are bouncy, rhythmic, and designed to pull people in and blow them away. With a playful approach to mixing and an ear for unexpected flips, she weaves together warm low-end, cheeky rhythms, and upbeat energy that moves with intention. She creates easy momentum that keeps crowds smiling, booty shaking, and 100% locked in. For this resonant rave expect her love of garage, breaks, and bass house at the forefront.

XL: 40th Anniversary Concert, Come celebrate out very special 40th anniversary!

The Tudor Consort celebrates its 40th birthday in 2026 and we have an incredible season planned to celebrate. Collaborations with five different ensembles, a debut in Auckland, three premiere performances, and of course a performance of Thomas Tallis’ 40 part masterpiece Spem in alium. Make sure you visit our website to get all the details and secure your tickets!
We will be taking part in our third Aotearoa Festival of the Arts with SoundCathedral on Sunday March 1, an incredible re-composition of Orlande de Lassus’ Prophetiae Sibyllarum by Michael Norris, written especially for our anniversary and the 25th birthday of Stroma contemporary music ensemble. We celebrate going ‘over the hill’ in style in our May 2 concert XL, featuring two 40 part works by Tallis and Mäntyjärvi. We have two concerts with our friends Orchestra Wellington - Leonard Bernstein’s energetic Chichester Psalms as part of W:Ellington on 30 May, and Victoria Kelly’s brand new opera Ocean on 28 November. A debut in Auckland with NZ Barok sees us performing Lotti and Handel, and we finish the year with Messiah with Australian virtuoso harpsichordist and director Erin Helyard. 

This is one of the most exciting seasons in our history, and I hope very much you can join us as we celebrate!

Coven: Wet - Pride Party, Follow the siren song to Ivy Bar this Pride Festival and get pool ready for a night that will leave you dripping. This is a pride dance party for sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people, so let's get wet with pride.
You don’t want to miss the tantalising surprises we have planned… Follow us on Instagram for more teasers.

Coven is pay as you wish or koha on the door.
More info about Coven:
Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.
Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.
For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.
This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

FRUIT LOOP FESTIVAL, Fruit Loop Festival
Marlborough’s freshest music festival!
About the Festival
Fruit Loop Festival is Marlborough’s juiciest new summer gig! A full-blown celebration of music and dance, kicking off under the sun and well into the night. Think open-air energy - blending Marlborough's summer magic with a full-scale music festival. An insane line-up of DJs and live performers with production to match! From the first drop to the final track, it's where the beat hits harder and the drinks taste sweeter.
Fresh, wild, fierce - Fruit Loop is the party Marlborough has been waiting for.
The Line-Up
DICK JOHNSON: The heart of NZ’s electronic scene, Dick Johnson is a true house music heavyweight. With remixes for global icons like Fatboy Slim and Claude VonStroke, plus Kiwi favourites L.A.B and Tiki Taane, he’s spent over two decades electrifying dancefloors worldwide. A relentless force behind the decks - and music director for Synthony - Dick brings the fire every time.
SIN: Co-host of George FM Drive, Sin is plugged into the pulse of the dance scene and has quickly become a revered authority on all things electronica. She’s torn up stages at Rhythm & Vines, Homegrown, Hidden Valley, and international festivals from Fiji to the UK. With supports for legends like Fatboy Slim, Groove Armada, and Netsky, Sin brings high-energy house, techno, and ravey curveballs to every set.
KITA MEAN: Kita Mean is New Zealand’s award-winning drag superstar, known for her infectious charm, razor-sharp wit, and high-camp aesthetic. With a career spanning 15+ years across stages and screens worldwide, she’s wowed audiences from Aotearoa and Australia to London, Canada, the USA, and beyond. Winner of the very first RuPaul’s Drag Race Down Under and co-owner of the iconic Caluzzi Cabaret, Kita continues to dazzle with colourful looks, flawless mug, and hilarious timing. Quirky, kooky, kitsch, and quick - Kita Mean isn’t just a queen, she’s an experience.
PETE GREEN: Originally from the UK, Pete is part of the vinyl-digging collective Rare Specimens. His love for deep, worldly electronic sounds brings low-end warmth and an infectious energy to the dancefloor. Along the way, he’s supported artists such as Crazy P, Psychemagik, Audio Jack, and Christopher Tubbs, playing festivals and parties from Creamfields and Rhythm & Alps to Tempo Schmempo. Expect a set seasoned with Italo, ambient, and deep house flavours, dusted with disco, and finished with a splash of techno.

description:
Over the Rainbow, Over the Rainbow
There’s no place like Pōneke.

Queer historian Will Hansen and legendary barman Malcolm Vaughan kōrero the capital’s vibrant LGBTQIA+ nightlife for Wellington Heritage Festival.


About Will

Will Hansen (he/him) is a transgender historian based in Pōneke. He is the recipient of a Judith Binney Trust Writing Award and is currently working on turning his PhD thesis – ‘Queer Activism in Aotearoa, 1961-2013’ into a book. Will is also a trustee of Kawe Mahara Queer Archives Aotearoa.


About Mal

Malcolm Vaughan is a Wellington gay icon. Before the Homosexual Law Reform Act of 1986, Mal worked at a series of bars and late-night haunts in the capital. More than just places to drink, venues like The Dominion, Bamboo Bar, Casper’s, The Dome (to name a few) provided a safe place in the capital for the city’s rainbow community to meet without prejudice. Today, Malcolm alongside husband, Scotty Kennedy ow and run the iconic Cuba Street establishment Scotty & Mal’s Cocktail and Lounge Bar.

Advocates for many LGBTQIA+ causes, they have supported many community initiatives over the years. In 2000 they co-founded the After Life Memorial Trust, now called the Chrissy Wītoko Memorial Trust, which originally provided financial support for AIDS patients of the rainbow community. The Trust continues to provide a wide range of support for the Wellington rainbow community.

description:
The Epic Life of Kahe Te Rau-o-te-Rangi, Te Waka Huia Wellington Museum is excited to have Miria Pōmare share the beautiful tāonga of her family’s story for Wellington Heritage Festival.

Miria comes from a long line of influential wāhine Māori. Her namesake, Lady Mīria Pōmare (1877-1971), was a community leader who spent much of her life advocating for the benefits of both Māori and Pākeha. In 1918, Lady Mīria was appointed an OBE for her service to the Māori Soldiers’ Fund which was established to help provide soldiers with comfort (food, knitted garments, letters) while they were away from home. Lady Mīria Pōmare’s story is shared in a display in the Attic of Te Waka Huia.

Hear the life story of modern-day Miria’s tupuna and great Rangatira Kahe who was one of five women who signed Te Tiriti in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Nau mai, haere mai to hear more about this Mana Wāhine and her truly epic life.

description:
Public History Talk: Writing Mr Ward’s Map, In the last Public History Talk for 2025, historian Elizabeth Cox will speak about her new book Mr Ward’s Map: Victorian Wellington Street by Street.
Wednesday 3 December 2025, 12:10pm to 1pm
Auditorium (Taiwhanga Kauhau), lower ground floor, National Library Building, corner Molesworth + Aitken Streets, Thorndon, Wellington and online.
A fascinating journey through Wellington’s past
In 1891, a remarkable map of Wellington was made by surveyor Thomas Ward. It recorded the footprint of every building, from Thorndon in the north, across the teeming, inner-city slums of Te Aro, to Berhampore in the south.
Updated regularly over the next 10 years, it detailed hotels, theatres, oyster saloons, brothels, shops, stables, Parliament, Māori kāinga, the Town Belt, the prisons, the ‘lunatic asylum’, and the hospital. The map is incredibly detailed — it even includes the location of street lights.
About the speaker
Elizabeth Cox is a Wellington historian who specialises in New Zealand’s social and architectural history. Her previous book, Making Space: A history of New Zealand women in architecture, was published in 2022.
These free Public History Talks are a collaboration between Te Puna Mātauranga o Aotearoa The National Library of New Zealand and Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage.
The talks are recorded and you can find them at the Apple store, Spotify and Podbean #newzealandhistory.
Register for a Zoom link: https://dia-nz.zoom.us/.../WN_lKZ5Kxg4TvSr8t8UffUNLA...

description:
GROUNDWORK: an author talk with Michele Leggott and Catherine Field-Dodgson, Join us to hear authors Michele Leggott and Catherine Field-Dodgson discuss Emily Cumming Harris, the subject of their book 'Groundwork', and one of Aotearoa's most significant female artists of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
Just as Emily Harris’s beautiful paintings occupy a liminal space between scientific botanical illustration and art, so this book occupies a shifting ground between biography and imagineered monograph. The result is often moving and always intriguing. Importantly, it restores to Aotearoa art history a figure who had almost disappeared.
Emily Harris has been examined alongside her artist peers Sarah Featon and Georgina Hetley, but until this book neither her distinctive voice nor her almost 200 surviving images have been heard or seen in any quantity outside of archival or online spaces.
Her life story is remarkable and her diaries, letters, poems and paintings constitute a fascinating legacy. In 'Groundwork', with its compelling text, they are lovingly brought together for the first time.
Michele and Catherine will be bringing copies of Emily's hand-coloured book 'New Zealand Flowers, Berries and Ferns' to display.

Forest & Bird WALK a New Reserve - Mātai Moana / Watts Peninsula, Join us for a guided walk over Mātai Moana / Watts Peninsula (North end of Miramar Peninsula). This guided walk will celebrate the Government announcement (September 2025), that the 72 hectare area is now a Public Reserve and DOC land.
The area's attractions include:
1. strong historical, cultural and military values, (several kainga and pā, and military history from 1880s), and has hosted several prisons, including a prison garden
2. some superb 360 degree views of Wellington Harbour
3. no major animal pest species and while much of the land is grass or in pines, there are several sizable and growing areas of regenerating native bush.
Moderate fitness will be needed. Our walk is expected to take a little over 2.5 hours. It will traverse a mixture of sealed roads and walking tracks with some uneven ground and two quite steep sections, from sea level to 163m above sea level. One section has a gradient of 30 degrees for a short section. There are some stiles to climb over.
Meet opposite the steps up to Massey Memorial at 130 Massey Road, Point Halwsell, Mapuia, Wellington, 6022. This is about 450m south of Point Halswell, and 500m north of the northern end of Shelly Bay. Location of the meeting point: approx 41°17'15" S, 174°49'26.5" E. A Forest & Bird Flag will be on display. See map for meeting spot and car parking suggestions. Please arrive in time to confirm your attendance and receive a quick pre-walk briefing.
Arrive by 12.50 p.m. on Sunday 22 February 2026. Please register on EventFinda in advance - limited to 40 walkers. All aged 10 or more, are welcome - you do not have to be a Forest & Bird member. All children must be accompanied by an adult who takes responsibility for them. Please bring your own sunhat, sunblock, snacks, any personal medications plus water bottle and wear good walking shoes/boots. There is no public transport to the meeting point.
If weather is wet/unsuitable, a decision to postpone will be made by 11:00 a.m. on Sunday 22 February 2026, and a group email will be issued to all those who have registered. Contact Ken New on ken.new@branch.forestandbird.org.nz for any enquiries.
Please register on EventFinda.

description:
Old Jail Museum Open Day, Old Jail Museum Open Day
Did you know Petone was the first place in New Zealand to have a Police force? Find out about this and other interesting Petone stories in the Old Jail Museum.

Come to the Old Jail Museum – a well-preserved former lockup. See an exhibition on Policing in Petone from 1840.

Read about Jackson Street's heritage, plus various Petone stories, including our rich sporting history. It has information on Jackson Street businesses, Petone walking tours, kids activity sheets, and more to take away.

Either our Heritage Office or a JSP Ambassador will be onsite.

Built in 1908 on Elizabeth Street, it was once the most senior station in the Hutt Valley with ten constables and one sergeant. In the early 1950s, the Police Station and Jail were moved behind the old courthouse at 13 Elizabeth Street. Police used the courthouse as an office, but the lockup continued to be used – mainly for intoxicated offenders – until 1978.


Free entry; koha is welcomed.
Event info here: https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/old-jail-museum-open-day-25/


Health & Safety:

must obtain the garden owner's consent if you wish to take cuttings.

description:
Printing With Chine Colle - Creative Arts Holiday Programme for Teens, Welcome to mixed media collage, the printmaker's way. Chine Colle is a printing process in which a thin sheet of paper is printed on and, at the same time, mounted on a sturdier sheet, creating a subtle, delicate backdrop to the printed image. Expanded on, this can include contrasting papers, graphic images, select colour shapes and fabric. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

In this one-day workshop for ages 12+, students will:

- Practice traditional and individual Chinese collage techniques
- Explore the use of delicate papers more responsive to ink and hand printing
- Test and practice mixed media chine colle with images, papers and fabric
- How effective Chinese Collage is as a method of adding colour to prints
- Making and using a damp pack
- Recipes for traditional glues

Bring a water bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy house during break time.

All Aboard

Holiday Programme - Build Your Own Ancient Runes Puzzle Box - CROFTON, Introducing our new updated “Ancient Runes Puzzle Box”. Keep your treasures safe in the coolest way possible. Only you will know the special code to release the catch hidden under the mechanical Iris! This new improved version has 2 code wheels that you can use to set your own unique code, as well as 2 code pins that are stored on the box but have to be inserted correctly to activate the mechanism. If everything is set a hidden push button will then activate a solenoid that releases the catch.

Powered by 4 AAA batteries (provided), you’ll get to solder the components, screw and glue all the intricate pieces together and unwrap the puzzle to learn how it works. And, of course, you'll get to take it home! No previous experience is required and you’re welcome to bring a grown up if you want to.

description:
Pinhole Photography - Three Day Creative Arts holiday programme, Did you know that any object that can be made light tight can be turned into a camera? Come along to this three-day workshop and choose an object – it could be a tea pot, a book, a coffee jar – to turn into a pinhole camera to then create black and white photographs with.

We’ll work in the darkroom and explore the process of loading your camera with silver gelatin paper, before making exposures in the garden around the historic Inverlochy house, testing different angles and perspectives. We’ll then return to the darkroom to develop your photographic negative, and print it as a positive. You’ll leave the course with a series of atmospheric pinhole photographs, having experienced the magic of hands-on darkroom printing.

Bring a water bottle and morning tea. Recommended age for this course is tweens & teens ages 10 and above.

Monday - Wednesday, 22 - 24 September, 10 am - 1 pm daily.

This workshop is part of Inverlochy Art School's September School Holiday Programme. For more teen & tween workshops including pottery, jewellery making, animation and sewing head to the 'Tamariki and Teens' section of our website.

description:
Social Media Marketing Secrets for Small Enterprises: Visual Impact, This course helps small business owners and entrepreneurs unlock the full potential of social media. Each week we’ll cover practical steps to review your current channels, set up strong profiles, and create a tailored content plan that works for your business. You’ll learn how to choose the right platforms, use hashtags effectively, create engaging posts, select visuals that connect with your audience, and understand the role of AI tools. By the end, you’ll walk away with a clear and actionable plan to grow your social media channels and attract the right customers.
Whether you’re starting out or already running a business, a strong social media presence is no longer optional. The challenge is knowing where to focus your efforts when every platform seems to demand something different.
This course is designed to cut through the noise and give you a roadmap that fits your business. Together, we’ll:
Review the main platforms and choose the right ones for your goals
Tailor your profiles so they look professional and trustworthy
Build a realistic content plan you can actually stick to
Learn how to use hashtags and trends to boost reach
Explore how AI can help (and where it can’t)
Understand what visuals work best and how to avoid common pitfalls
Discuss tips for creating engagement and growing a loyal following
The focus is practical and hands-on. Each week you’ll apply the ideas directly to your own business, so by the end of the course you’ll have a solid social media strategy ready to put into action.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

description:
Ring Making Workshop in Wellington, Limited Spaces! One Date Only – Book Now!
Monday, 3 November
Create a unique piece of jewellery using wax and set with gemstones. After the session, each participant's wax piece will be cast in silver, meticulously filed, polished, and mailed to them in a gift box.
In this single-session workshop, you'll be introduced to the lost wax casting process and be guided by a certified jewellery maker in creating a custom-designed ring from wax.
WORKSHOP HIGHLIGHTS:
Creative Experience: Design and create your own sterling silver jewellery with cast-in-place gemstones.
Expert Guidance: Learn from a certified jewellery maker in a supportive and inspiring environment.
All-Inclusive: The workshop provides all the necessary tools and materials, ensuring a seamless experience.
Finished Product: Receive a beautifully handcrafted piece of jewellery, creating lasting memories and a unique keepsake.
WHO SHOULD ATTEND:
Hobbyists and craft enthusiasts
Individuals seeking unique, handmade jewellery
Couples, friends, or mothers & daughters looking for a creative bonding activity
Anyone searching for a unique and thoughtful gift
WHAT TO EXPECT:
Guidance on creating a simple wax band
Stone setting in wax using mixed gemstones
Support in creating a personalised design with stones
INCLUDES IN THE WORKSHOP:
Use of all necessary tools
A selection of gemstones (precious stones available for an extra fee)
Wax for creating jewellery pieces
Sterling silver (up to 15 grams per piece)
Option to order your piece in gold (for an extra fee)
Casting, filing, and polishing of your wax piece
Final product mailed to your provided address
ADDITIONAL INFO:
If you have a specific design or material in mind (perhaps a diamond for an engagement ring?) and would like to discuss it beforehand, please email craftyfingersworkshop@yahoo.com.

Do humans have free will? Philosophy info event, Do you know a pre-uni philosopher? Send them our way on 14 October to hear if humans have free will.
Humans are special. We make choices; we hold each other responsible; we reward good choices and punish bad choices. But humans are parts of the natural world. Our characters are forged by our genetics and environments; our bodies are made of physical particles following physical laws; our choices are caused by factors outside our control. So is our freedom an illusion? What does it really mean to be a human?
Interested in Philosophy as a study subject? Come and hear the perspectives of Philosophy lecturers and students, and join in the discussion.

 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

What you’ll learn
How to create and screenprint your own design using paper stencils
Tips and tricks from Greta’s years of experience as an artist and textile designer

All materials provided, including one tote bag

You’re also welcome to bring your own light-coloured fabric or fabric item to print on, just make sure it’s at least 50% natural fibre (cotton or linen is ideal).

Can I print more than one bag? Or multiple colours?
Once your design is on the screen you can print a few multiples if you'd like.
The workshop is set up for participants to make one bag with a single colour print, but depending on how fast you work, (if there is time) you are welcome to add another colour.

Who it’s for
This workshop is for anyone curious about screenprinting, no experience required.
All ages welcome! (Under 13s will need an adult to join them.)
Accessibility
The space is wheelchair accessible.
The process is adaptable for all abilities. If you can use scissors, that's excellent, tearing paper also works. Greta is happy to help with cutting if needed.

Time: 10.30am - 12.30pm
Location: Mt Cook School, 160 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington
Cost: $85 per person
Class size: Max of 10 participants

Yourself and your ideas!

About Greta
Greta Menzies is an artist and designer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has taught art and design workshops since 2015, in galleries, schools, community studios, and at Massey University. Greta first started screenprinting with stencils in her garage at 17, making hoodies and t-shirts for her mates. Monday 13th October - 10:00am - 12:00pm

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

With a history spanning over 1,400 years, Ikebana is far more than decorative floral design. It is a refined art form that expresses space, balance, seasonality, and life itself. Today, Ikebana is internationally recognised and practiced by enthusiasts around the world.

Through careful techniques such as proper water preparation and pruning, flowers can be enjoyed for weeks, subtly changing their appearance over time.

description:
Lost Wax in Three - Mitsuro Hikime Wax, Discover the magic of Mitsuro Hikime — the beautiful Japanese technique that uses a special stretchy wax to create flowing, organic textures unlike anything else in jewellery-making.

Over three inspiring sessions, you’ll learn how to transform this fascinating material into stunning wearable pieces using the traditional lost wax casting process.

Mitsuro Hikime wax behaves very differently from standard jeweller’s wax. Warm and pliable, it can be stretched, twisted and pulled into delicate ribbons and natural textures that resemble flowing water, bark, roots or molten metal. The results are beautifully organic and wonderfully unpredictable, making every piece completely unique.

During the first two sessions, you’ll learn how to handle and shape this traditional Japanese wax, exploring different techniques to create rings, pendants or small sculptural objects full of movement and texture. Once your designs are complete, your waxes will be professionally cast in the metal of your choice.

There is then a one-week break before the final session to allow time for casting. In the third class, you’ll learn how to cut, file, sand and finish your cast pieces, transforming them into polished jewellery ready to wear, gift or treasure.

This course is suitable for complete beginners as well as more experienced makers wanting to experiment with this exciting and expressive technique. More advanced students are also welcome to use the sessions to develop independent projects in a supportive studio environment.

Included in the class fee are all Mitsuro Hikime waxes, consumables, sandpaper and courier costs.

Please note that casting and metal costs are not included, as these vary depending on the size of your piece and the metal selected. Small castings generally cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costs ranging approximately from $8–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

They will be at our club on Wednesday 26 November at 5.30pm (for a 6pm presentation). It is part of a project on “Science, Culture and Economy – Links between Croatian Communities in the World and the Homeland”.
The presentations are on:
- Brief history of Croatian standard language – Prof. Luka Budak (former Head of Croatian Studies, Macquarie University);
- World-renowned Croatian scientists and inventors – Dr. Marijana Borić, Scientific Advisor (Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts – CASA);
- The Croatian economy from 1992 to the present day – Prof. Tomislava Majić, Senior Lecturer (University North); and
- Croatian language recognition in Australia in 1970s – Prof. Ana Bruning (former lecturer at Croatian Studies, Macquarie University and long-time Croatian language teacher at the Croatian Schools in Sydney.
The presenters acknowledge the support of Croatian Studies Foundation of Australia, Central State Office for Croats Outside of the Republic of Croatia, Foundation of Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts.
Current timings for the event are:
5:30pm - gather for tea/coffee/drinks
6:00pm - Presentations
This will be followed by a question and discussion time, with a light supper and drinks.
All welcome! You don't need to be a member of the Club to attend!

WORKSHOPS (Scroll down for more detailed descriptions of workshops)

Workshop details
Friday 3rd April
10.30am Pole Flow, Leg Rotations & Flexible Hips (Ana)
Leg rotations can create different shapes, lines and feeling to our movement. They can elevate our pole flow and are foundational to many transitions and moves. Leg rotations start from the hips. We can make them more comfortable and access more dramatic shapes by conditioning our hip flexors and increasing our range of motion. In this workshop we will learn:
•Conditioning exercises for our hip flexors that you can add to your regular practice
•The foundational movement of leg rotations and how they can elevate and create variety in our pole moves
•A variety of dance elements that use leg rotations, that you can add to your pole flow or routines
(All levels)
12 noon Belly Dance: Making It Slinky (Pip E-Lysaah)
The magic isn’t in the big tricks. It’s in the pause before them.
In Making It Slinky, we’ll dive into the slow moments that define a performance, the entrance, the exit, and every delicious transition in between. This workshop is all about how you arrive, how you linger, and how you leave them slightly unwell. We’ll explore controlled undulations, weighted steps, breath-led movement, and the art of stretching time so the audience forgets to blink. Less rushing. More reigning.
This is signature muscle isolation and control, the kind that makes a simple belly roll wave feel scandalous. We’ll break down my structured approach to belly rolls, arm waves, and wraps ... not just how to execute them, but how to layer and thread them so nothing ever “stops.” Everything melts, coils, and unwraps with intention. You’ll learn how to build tension through transitions, turning the space between movements into something almost indecent. If you’ve ever been told to “do more,” this workshop is about doing less… slower… and making it hit harder.
(All levels)
1.30pm Sensual Awakening: Unleash your Inner Siren (Vixen Temple)
Get out of your head and into your body with Vixen Temple! In this empowering workshop, you'll explore techniques to tap into your inner sensuality and trust your body. Harness your erotic energy to move with seductive fluidity and hypnotic flow.
(All levels)
3.00pm Nail Your Inverts (Elisa Puccioni)
Elisa will guide you into a series of exercises, precise techniques, and insider tips to help you finally master those elusive inverts and leg hangs. Whether it's refining your form, building strength, or gaining more aerial control, we've got you covered! This workshop is ideal for beginners who are starting with their inverts up to intermediate students that want to polish their inverting techniques. Don't forget to BYH (bring your heels!) for an extra challenge and added flair!
(All levels)
4.30pm Feeling the Floor (Karina Shann)
In this workshop Karina will utilize fundamental floorwork moves such as shoulder stands, rolls, duck dives and body lines to guide you through ways that you can accentuate parts of your body, move with intention and captivate the audience. She’ll teach transitions and combos incorporating the fundamentals that you can take away to elevate your floor game. Heels optional but recommended. Socks, leg warmers optional, knee pads necessary.
(Prerequisite – Backwards & forwards roll)
6.00pm Choreography Kickstarter (Maree & Giada)
This workshop is perfect to get you started on your performance journey.
• Practical exercises to unlock your creativity, start building combos for your routines, and practice transitions between moves.
• Talk through how to structure a routine, performance tips and tricks, how to deal with nerves and much, much more!
This workshop is suitable for students of all levels. If you are currently working on a dance for a show, we can help with that. But you don't have to have a performance in mind to get heaps out of this session!
Saturday 4th April
10.30am Chair Tricks & Choreo (Billie Jean)
A burlesque classic – Express! Let’s get our groove on to this banger. We will learn some cute chair tricks and transitions to sass our way through this choreography. Beginner friendly, this dance is suitable for all levels! Plus, progressions for those who want to get upside down.
Wear comfortable clothes, socks or dance heels.
(All levels)
12 noon Creative Practices for Freestyle (Rachael)
Freestyling is a fantastic way to develop your movement style. This workshop will cover various concepts like tempo, sensation, texture, intention. You’ll learn new approaches for practicing freestyling and have fun while gaining a new appreciation for the practice.
(All levels)
1.30pm Stripper Flow (Maddie May)
Learn how to slink around the pole in your own authentic way, focusing on embellishing movements, fluid transitions and musicality!
(All levels)
3.00pm Fonji 101 (Terumi Isogai)
This is an introduction course for fonji related moves. Starting with preparation exercises to get used to the movement. Learn the techniques to execute fonji safely and effectively!
(Prerequisite: Shoulder mount, preferably aerial)
4.30pm Tumbles & Drops (Terumi Isogai)
You climb up the pole, and now what? Learn fun ways to come down the pole!
(Prerequisite: Aerial invert. Leg hang)

7.30pm Pole Show – “Let There Be Light”
Sunday 5th April
10.30am Booty Electric: Twerkshop (Emma Hopkins)
Come along to Emma’s beginner Twerkshop where you will learn basic twerk moves from the floor to on the pole. We will cover different styles of twerking and then put them together for a sexy, bootiful routine. We need to protect our knees while we are popping it like it's hot so please bring kneepads. Sneakers are also recommended.
(All Levels)
12 noon Bendy Bunnies: Stretch (Judith Dillon)
Level up your flexibility this Easter with fun and creative ways to move your body. Whether you've got a dedicated practice or you've never tried stretching before, all levels are welcome - Judith will adapt poses for every level and ability.
In this workshop we will focus on partner assisted stretches and stretching with props (blocks/wall) We will work on breathing into deep stretches, relaxing into passive holds, as well as muscle activation for some fun duo poses.
(All levels)
1.30pm Hula Hoop 101 (Dylan Daisy)
Learn the basics of hula hooping. Start the spin, maintain your core tension and you’re off! Using different body parts to flow and transition make hula hooping a fun and dynamic art form.
After a lifetime of commanding stages and perfecting her craft, Dylan is a fantastic and skilled hoop performer who has become a favourite in the Wellington performing arts scene. Bring a hoop if you have one (We will supply some).
(All levels)
3.00pm Perfect Pirouettes (Gabrielle McElwee)
Keen to learn some smooth ways to turn, flow and transition around the pole?
Want to improve your dance fluidity?
Then this workshop is for you! Pirouettes are a MUST HAVE for any pole dancer, so this workshop will cover pirouette technique, a variety of fun pirouette patterns & transitions which build in level, ending with a short flow sequence. Socks are recommended.
(All levels)
4.30pm Handstands with Julia (Julia Bromley)
Come and get upside down with Julia! This class workshop will focus on the basic foundations of handstands and will give you skills and drills to continue to work on towards your upside-down goals. You will be guided through exercises and drills to maximise strength and technique needed to begin or extend your handstand journey. Julia has been teaching workshops and private lessons for over 7 years in both circus, pole and dance studios and loves seeing students gain the body awareness and technique to attain their goals!
(All levels)

As part of our 2025 partnership with At the World’s Edge Festival, Orchestra Wellington will host AWE 2025 Festival Artist Yura Lee to present a masterclass for violinists and violists in Wellington.
Anyone can register to attend and observe the masterclass!
Visit https://orchestrawellington.co.nz/event/awe-masterclass-2025 to register to attend and observe the masterclass for FREE!
Violinist/violist Yura Lee is a multifaceted musician, as a soloist and as a chamber musician, and one of the very few that is equally virtuosic on both violin and viola. Her career spans three decades and takes her all over the world, captivating audiences through various musical mediums from baroque to modern, and enjoying a career that spans three decades and takes her all over the world. She has performed with major orchestras including those of New York, Chicago, Baltimore, Cleveland, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and given recitals in London’s Wigmore Hall, Vienna’s Musikverein, Salzburg’s Mozarteum, the Palais des BeauxArts in Brussels, and the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam.
At age 12, she became the youngest artist ever to receive the Debut Artist of the Year prize at the Performance Today awards given by National Public Radio. She is the recipient of a 2007 Avery Fisher Career Grant; she has received numerous other international prizes, including top prizes in the Mozart, Indianapolis, Hannover, Kreisler, Bashmet, and Paganini competitions. Yura Lee was the only first prize winner awarded across four categories at the 2013 ARD Competition in Germany.
An Incredible Partnership with At The World's Edge Festival!
As part of our 2025 partnership with At the World’s Edge (AWE) Festival, Orchestra Wellington is presenting a three-part series featuring AWE 2025 Festival Artist Yura Lee and AWE Artistic Director Benjamin Baker for a mini-series of concerts and a masterclass here in Wellington in addition to featuring these incredible artists' live performances with us on our subscription series concerts in September and October!

description:
24-hour Squash Marathon for Wayne, 24 Hours on Court for Wayne.
This time I’m picking up my squash racket for a challenge like no other: 24 hours of nonstop squash. Why? Because someone I care for has been facing a far tougher battle.
My father-in-law was recently diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). For years he lived undiagnosed, pushing through symptoms without answers. Now that we finally know what he’s fighting, I want to turn my energy into something that can help him—and others—on their journeys.
According to CLL Advocates NZ, only 10-15 people out of 250 on average per year benefit from the budget allocation. And many are not even able to receive the same treatment options here in NZ.
Squash has always been a sport of endurance, resilience, and determination. Playing for 24 hours is my way of honoring his fight, raising awareness, and bringing people together to support the cause.
You can help by:
Donating: Any amount you would like to.
Predicting: Predicting how many points and games will be played in 24 hours.
Joining me on court: Book a slot to play a game, cheer from the sidelines, or come be part of the atmosphere.
Buy raffle tickets, or sponsor a prize towards the raffle.
We would like to give a shout out to our current sponsors;
Hair Phoria,
Aimee Photography,
X-Potential,
Mitchells,
Meaters,
CBD Eatery,
Forrest Wines and
Fat Tony's
No matter how small, your contribution will make a difference. Together we can transform his story of late diagnosis into one of community, awareness, and action.
I’ll be pushing myself through the night, but I won’t be alone—your support will keep me going with every serve, rally, and game. Let’s make this 24 hours count.

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Homewood Airstrip| Roast by the Coast, Enjoy a day out on the Wairarapa Coast with a family-friendly walk and a hearty roast lunch. Situated on working farmland, the Homewood Airstrip walk is a 5km return track that follows a gradual incline to the top, offering sweeping views of land and sea, before an easy downhill return. The gravel track is usually straightforward, but can be slippery or muddy in wet conditions—good footwear and wet-weather gear are recommended. Gates will be open and stock fenced off for the day. Thanks to Tranzit sponsorship the bus fare is significantly reduced for participants.

After your walk, return to the Homewood Storeroom to refuel with a traditional roast lunch of slow-cooked lamb, crispy roast potatoes, and seasonal salad, with an optional slice for dessert.

Walk Format
Travel: 1 hour each way from Masterton (2 hours total)
Arrive: Café at 10am (time for the loo and to collect maps—navigation support by Gavin, our seasoned guide!)
Walk: Depart up the airstrip by 10.30am; allow 2 hours including time to enjoy the views
Lunch: Return to the Storeroom by 12.30pm for a roast lunch
Return: Bus departs from the café at 2pm

This outing is ideal for fit trampers, casual walkers, families, pre-schoolers, and school groups (minimum age 4+). Expect moderate hills and potentially muddy conditions if it rains—but with the right gear, light rain and wind will only add to the adventure.

description:
Greater Wellington Centurion - 2026, Summer is here and that means it is birdie season for Greater Wellington Disc Golf! As such, the club is once again organizing Centurion on Wellington Anniversary.
What is "Centurion"?
It's a social event where teams known as "Car-horts" complete over 100 holes across the Greater Wellington region trying to collect as many birdies as possible. "Car-horts" consist of 2-4 players (or as many as you can fit in your car). Bragging rights are awarded for best individual birdie performance, best total Car-Hort birdie performance, and overall score.
*Can anyone beat Johnny Wake's 58 birdie/2 ace performance?
**Yes, aces/eagles count as 2 birdies!
***Who will hit double digits underpar?
Where is it?
This year, the 108 Holes will be played at Harcourt Park, Hikoikoi Reserve, Poole Crescent Reserve (Wainuiomata), and the Berhampore Hills.
- Holes 1 to 36 are at Harcourt Park (2x Short/"Main Tees")
- Holes 37 to 54 at Poole Crescent Reserve (2x "Main Tees")
- Holes 55 to 72 are at Hikoikoi Reserve (2x "Main Tees")
- Holes 73 to 108 are at Berhampore Hills (2x "Black Tees")
Car-Horts may complete the event in any sequence they wish, but must score the round on UDisc using the hole allocations above.
All disc golfers are welcome to compete, so if you're interested/plan on competing, please post in the event discussion who's in your Car-Hort, as well as your Car-Hort name.
Don't have a Car-hort? No worries! Make a post about seeking a Car-Hort, or reach out to Brady Kuech who is organizing the event.
For those posting on social media (Instagram, Facebook, and Stories), tag @greaterwellingtondiscgolf and #gwcenturion to be featured on our socials. We'd love to share all the action throughout the day.
So charge your phone. Pack a lunch. Slather on your suncream, and nab them birdies!

Steps To Success - The recipe to competing at your best, Steps To Success is a seminar, helping you become the best athlete possible. No matter your level, weather you are a beginner, an amatuer or a pro, this workshop has the recipe to start competing at your best. You don't even have to be competing! You could just want to do better.
What:
This seminar is a fundraiser to get the Rocking Robins Top team to Nationals this year in Rotorua.
When: August 29th 2025 6pm
Where: Tawa Fitness Portal
Cost: $25 Per ticket
Purchase your ticket here: https://docs.google.com/.../1FAIpQLSfMyBy9iQsriz.../viewform
Bonus: Each ticket comes with a $5 voucher to the Fitness Portal Cafe.
Sausage Sizzle: There will be a sausage running during the sausage sizzle so you won't go hungry.
Please make payment into the following account:
Account Name: Rocking Robins Rock N Roll Club
Account #: 06-0773-0877111-00
Particulars: STS
Reference: First + Last Name

What is this event?
Rotate through each 20–30 min session (with 5-min breaks between):
1. Mindset & Visualization – Mental prep and performance focus with Jordan
2. Injury Prevention - Progressive load and how to avoid injury with Devin Glover
3. Fuel your body right - Talking fueling and supplements thanks to Scorpion Supplements with Rebekah Glover and Liz Monrad
BBQ will be running on the night so be sure to bring your loose coins!!
Proceeds from this event go towards helping the Rocking Robins top team get to national in October!!
Meet your hosts:
Jordan Shearer: Coach. Trainer. Space-holder for rebels, dreamers, and high end performers.
Jordan is the founder of Being You, a coaching practice grounded in authenticity, connection, courage, simplicity, and going rogue. She blends her background in mental health, life coaching, and human behavior with no-fluff, deeply human approach to performance. Having competed herself, Jordan understands the pressure that comes with stepping out, showing up, and giving your best when it counts. Jordan has coached competitive gymnasts, doctors, dancers, and first responders (to name a few) - people who need to stay mentally strong in high-performance spaces.
Devin Glover: Owner and Founder of The Fitness Portal Limited. Devin has been a personal trainer for 10+ years, and has competed either Nationally or Internationally in the following sports: Underwater Hockey, Olympic Weightlifting, Rock N Roll Dancing, CrossFit, Swimming and has dabbled in endurance sports like Ironman and Road cycling.
Rebekah Glover: Rebekah has gone through a huge lifestyle transformation. After losing over 30kgs and keeping it off, she became a Weight Watchers coach, then she started personal training in 2021. Rebekah has learnt through trial and error, about how important it is to fuel correctly to achieve your goals and that it isn't always about weight loss. If you you want to perform you need to fuel correctly. She is now an avid runner and competes Nationally in Rock n Roll Dancing, after only three years of dancing she holds one national title, and two regional titles.

description:

Speedway action this Saturday night at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway where the Manawatu Saloon Championship is decided along with the exhilarating side-by-side Sidecar racing action for the AFC Motorcycles Sidecar Best Pairs. Saturday night will also see the return of V8 Modifieds racing wheel to wheel around the Robertson Prestige International Speedway. Fantastic SuperStocks, metal crunching Stockcars and eye-catching Minisprints add to a massive night of entertainment.

A quality field of drivers is expected for the sought after Manawatu Saloon Championship adding to a packed show at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway in the form of Corvettes, Camaros and Mustangs racing wheel-to-wheel. The wide tyres and thundering V8 engines add another style of speedway racing which is proving popular not only with drivers but the spectators alike. The Saloon racing this season has been competitive at the Robertson Prestige International Speedway with local drivers including 7p Clayton More, 57p Calvin Honore, 81p Jonathan Mason, and 242p Ashleigh King all looking to be in contention for the title.

Adding to the exciting programme is the AFC Motorcycles Sidecar Best Pairs which will see some of the country’s best sidecar combinations pair up and battle it out. With 14 combinations confirmed including 5p Wingnut & Sam McNaught, 8p Rob Miller & Jaxon Hannan, 17p Tony Hislop & Aidan Foothead, recent Ray Tarrant Sidecar Memorial winners 27b Craig Boaler & Kayla Meehan all included in the sensational field. The Robertson Prestige International Speedway has seen some spectacular Sidecar racing and this best pair championship is set to deliver this high calibre of entertainment for the fans once again!

With the return of the V8 Modifieds to the Robertson Prestige International Speedway, expect a high calibre of side-by-side racing from these v8 powered race cars with replica fiberglass car bodies and big wings! Drivers including Newton Gordge from Taranaki, Cody Hata from Auckland, 28w Ricky Dykstra and 9e Sheldon Arapere have indicated that they will be in attendance for this momentous return of Modified racing to the Robertson Prestige International Speedway.

Adding to the packed programme this Saturday night, the Superstocks will hit the track with grit, steel, and determination to be at the front of the pack. Metal crunching Stockcars will be battling it out for the chequered flag as well. Both classes race Side-by-side and bumper-to-bumper, these drivers in both classes mean business, with their fearless attitude and willingness to put on a show its anyone’s guess who will carry the chequered flag at the end of the race! Rounding out what is set to be a massive night the Minisprints make their return ahead of their Oval Superstars Tour first round the following weekend.

Classes in action are SuperStocks, Stockcars, Saloons, Sidecars, Modifieds, Minisprints

description:
A Person Shaped Thing - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance, A Person Shaped Thing is a new solo contemporary dance work by Trinity Maydon, exploring the fragile architecture of Self Perception/Presentation - the process of strategically concealing or revealing information in order to influence others' and our own perceptions on ourselves. Even the person you believe yourself to be only exists for you.

We consciously select different versions of ourselves in different rooms. Each version is carefully calibrated. Each gesture considered. A quiet choreography of revealing and concealing.

Drawing on sociologist Erving Goffman’s dramaturgical theories of human interaction, the work examines life as a performance: frontstage and backstage, audience and actor and the constant maintenance of expression control where we learn to play roles before we even realise we are performing them.

The attentive pupil performs attentiveness
until the performance consumes the listening.

In A Person Shaped Thing, identity is not something created, but selected — assembled from external influences, expectations, and the environments we move through. We shapeshift to fit the spaces we enter, adjusting the mask, refining the image, editing the self.

But the performance is exhausting.

What happens when the masks begin to slip?
What remains when the roles fall away?

As the work unfolds, the body becomes a site of tension — caught between authenticity and artifice, between who we are, who we think we are, and who we believe we should be. In the search to “fit into one’s own skin,” we risk becoming estranged from it entirely.

There is no singular, stable self.
At the crux, we are something harder to name —
An unidentifiable, faceless creature.

Blurring the boundaries between performer and performed

Does the performance ever really end?

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance.

About the artist:
Trinity Maydon is a contemporary dance artist originally from Ōtepoti and a graduate of the New Zealand School of Dance. Since graduating in 2024, she has been taking her first steps as a freelance artist, exploring and shaping her unique voice within the art form of dance.

Trinity has always been drawn to the ways in which we use our bodies to tell stories, how we can shape ourselves to physicalize our ideas and express them to the world. She is deeply interested in the lived experience of movement and the connection between mind and body, constantly exploring how embodiment can be a tool for both personal expression and collective storytelling.

Since graduating, Trinity has had the privilege of collaborating on two rave installations with Untitled Warehouse Project— 'Entry' and 'Omnia' (2025). She has also worked alongside Jeremy Beck, teaching throughout Dunedin and performing in Company Beck’s 'Commentary of Dreaming' as part of the 2025 Dunedin Arts Festival.
In 2026, Trinity was immersed in the Fringe Festival, performing in Lyndon Foley’s 'Our Dreaming Bodies' and and was a choreographer in Wellington Community Ballet Theatre's 'Four Questions' in her piece 'Is Santa Claus Real'. She also performed as a guest artist at the Performance Arcade in 'Four Strings – Four Limbs' with Alex Cooper.

A Person Shaped Thing is Trinity’s first full-length work and she is excited to be debuting it as part of this year’s festival.

The ‘Tones of Silence’ -explored through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will explore the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.
"Generally, the older the equipment, the greater the personal input of the photographer is required and therefore the greater the commitment and individuality. Often, you can look at a 19th-century photograph and tell who the photographer is. You certainly can't do that today. It isn't only the camera and lens, but also the type of film (or in those days, glass plate), the developer used and how the print is made onto particular types of paper. Each gives a distinct interpretation".
John Grace - email - 18/06/25
The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend this event and support the Trust in its work.
The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the exhibition events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust.  Please register

Author Event: Simon Winchester – Breath of the Gods, Join us in the bookshop for our first author event of the year with international superstar writer, SIMON WINCHESTER, in conversation with RNZ's Sally Round.

We are beyond lucky to have Simon include Masterton on this tour, with just two other festival attendances in New Zealand.

The writer behind bestselling non-fiction books, Krakatoa, Land, Exactly and more, Winchester is well known for his ability to take a subject and use it to tell a fascinating a broader story about the world.

In his latest book, The Breath of the Gods, he delivers a thought-provoking history, and future, of that unseen but not unfelt presence in our lives – the wind.

Between the wind as a malevolent force and wind as the saviour of our planet, lies a world of fascination, history, literature, science, poetry and engineering, which Simon Winchester explores with the curiosity and vigour that are the hallmarks of his bestselling works.

Join us for what we’re sure will be a fascinating discussion on how this elemental force shapes the world as we know it.

Books will be available to purchase and have signed by Simon on the night.

description:
100 Things, 
3 actors. 60 minutes. 100 things. Can they do it?
100 Things is the craziest improv comedy show in Tāmaki Makaurau, and now it's going on tour!
Imagine if the TV shows Taskmaster and Whose Line Is It Anyway? had a baby ... it'll be kind of like that!
How does it work? In an improv show, the improvisers typically ask the audience for a few suggestions that will inform how the show plays out. In 100 Things, the actors will write down -- you guessed it -- 100 things to incorporate into their show, with a little help from the audience.
ONE HUNDRED THINGS, YOU GUYS. IN A ONE HOUR SHOW. They have to use all 100 of them, or the show will be deemed a catastrophic failure! If they pull it off, they'll have set a world record for most ask-fors used in an improv show.
100 Things has previously applied for and been rejected by the Guinness Book of World Records. The book-keepers over at Guinness may think "most ask-fors used per minute in an improvised comedy show" is not a valid world record category, but we sure do! 100 Things is now driven by a powerful desire to prove the Guinness Book of World Records Wrong. This desire leads the team to amazing new heights of improv skill.
 
In the meantime, 100 Things has collected a range of other accolades! A sold-out season at Dunedin Fringe 2024. Winner of Late Night Knife Fight improv showdown in Tāmaki Makaurau. And nominated for best ensemble at New Zealand Improv Festival 2024!
 
Performed by Rebecca Mary Gwendolon (RAW Comedy finalist), Izzy Renton (Shortland St) and Frankie Browne (Ugly Shakespeare Company): three improvisor besties who can't wait to share this show with you.

Unfortunately, ROADKILL: The Uber-Cool Musical won’t be happening this time around, but we’re already cooking up something even better for the future. All ticket holders will receive a full refund and we can’t wait to welcome you to our next big adventure.
Thank you for your excitement and your support.
ROADKILL The Uber-Cool Musical takes you on a wildly immersive journey through love, life and rock ’n’ roll — all from the back seat of a van. This intimate one-man musical combines humour, heart and unforgettable tunes for an experience like no other.
Strap in for the rollercoaster ride of your life as we take a regular mundane occurrence of driving in an Uber and blow wide open the private life, memories and miss happenings of our hero, and driver, Terry.

Carpool karaoke meets intense love story meets wild murder mystery.

Much more than a musical, its an experience, its a journey and an attraction!

In the space of a usual cabaret show and with the help of the passengers in the van, you will witness and be part of, childhood dreams, births, deaths and marriages, high drama, dark comedy, all sung live with a kickass, original, meatloaf-esque rock soundtrack. Surprises and magic ensues as we push the van, and Terry, to the limits of what is possible.

This will be an intimate, sensory overload, in a van. A full grand musical with all the bells and whistles.

With only 9 seats available each ride, grab your mates and have a private experience in the fast lane!
The hottest ticket in town- be sure to experience the ride of your life!

The show is in the style of a musical crossed with karaoke songs you have never heard before...

description:

The animals of Manor Farm have had enough. They rise up, and build a new world on the promise that all animals are equal. But it won't last.

About this Event

Toi Whakaari: NZ Drama School presents Animal Farm by Van Badham, as part of our 2026 Double Bill season.
The animals of Manor Farm have had enough. They rise up, cast out their oppressor, and build a new world on the promise that all animals are equal. But it won't last.
Van Badham's razor-sharp adaptation of Orwell's enduring fable drags the barnyard into the present tense, where the pigs have podiums, the sheep scroll and share, and the slogans change just fast enough that nobody notices. A savage, darkly comic warning that has never felt more necessary.
Together with Apirana Taylor's Whaea Kairau: Mother Hundred Eater, they form an unmissable double bill from Toi Whakaari: NZ Drama School, one that refuses to look away from the oldest story in the book: who gets power, who loses it, and who pays the price.
We invite you to witness the bold work of our students across Acting, Production, Design, Costume, and Set & Props construction, and come away with more questions, more fire, and more hope than you arrived with.
Performance rights exclusively licensed by Yellow Creative Management

ABOUT THE TEACHER
LIA KELLY is a theatre-maker and musician based in Pōneke. She is an established director, actor, improviser and musician with over a decade of professional work under her belt. She created and directed One Night Band which won 'Most Original Production' at the Wellington Theatre Awards 2023, and her Musical Comedy show Bug Songs not Love Songs won the "Momentous Music" award at NZ Fringe 2026.
THE STAND-BY LIST
PopRox firmly believes that improv is for everyone, especially when it comes to sharing skills and knowledge. So we're offering "the stand-by list" for all our workshops in 2026. We'll giveaway any spots remaining one week before this course, on a first-come-first-serve basis. No need to provide a reason, no questions asked. If the entry fee is a barrier for you to come along, then simply email poproximprov@gmail.com and we'll pop you on the SBL. Everyone on the list will be notified whether there was a place available for them at least 5 days before the course begins.

I Don't Know Much About Art But I Know What I Lick is a show about fine art for messy people.

In I Don't Know Much About Art But I Know What I Lick, Trick of the Light Theatre (The Bookbinder, The Griegol) join forces with internationally acclaimed performance designer Meg Rollandi on a new show for children (5 and under) and their accompanying adults. description:
Amid the Summer's Malice, 
Amid the Summer's Malice is a re-write of A Midsummer Night's Dream that focuses in on agency and consent, while still keeping the humour. Follow Hermia as she navigates escaping an arranged marriage, gets lost in the streets with her friends Lysander and Demetrius, stumbles into Oberon's love potion plot, deals with the fairy king's meddling, and then come out the other side with Lysander happily in love with her, and she is magically drugged to love him back. Classic Midsummer! Meanwhile, poor Richard (just call him Dick) is putting on a one-man show for the big wedding, and of course, nothing could possibly go wrong there either. With all the magical transformations and love-potions, the implications for agency and consent could not be clearer; so come along to see this funny, colourful story told again, in a modern setting with updated language, and with modern issues at the core.
