description:
Modern Heirlooms, Modern Heirlooms brings together the work of Antoinette Ratcliffe and Ben Klocek in a collection of captured moments in time, presented in the vestry at Old St Paul’s.
This intimate space will be the home to taxidermy birds mid-tumble, butterflies set in a world adjacent to our won, and the duo's 2025 collaboration piece, 'Apricity'.
Ratcliffe and Klocek invite you to take a moment with this collection in the peace of the vestry to contemplate the fragility and beauty of the individuals protected under glass.
Ratcliffe only uses ethically sourced animals for her artwork, and all butterflies used in Klocek's artworks are unprotected species collected from sustainable sources.
All works are for sale.
This exhibition, on until 31 March, will take place in Old St Paul's suitably unique octagonal vestry, where visitors could once take in stunning harbour views. The vestry traditionally served as the building's clergy office for 98 years and was a place for officials to change into their ceremonial robes.
Artist bios
Antoinette Ratcliffe completed her Master of Arts at The School of Media Arts (Wintec) in 2011. She began learning taxidermy in 2015 and introduced the media into her practice the following year. Her taxidermy is now held in educational collections around New Zealand, and her art works are held in private collections around the world.
Post-medium artist Ben Klocek creates pieces that explore the contrast between the physical and metaphysical. By utilising paint, ink, assemblage, entomology, and lepidoptery – combined with his interest in the surreal parts of life – he introduces us to scenes that feel natural despite their unlikely combinations.

description:
Botanical insights display - Ancient plants, Ancient plants and a few animals

A boom in ‘modern’ palaeobotany started in the early 19th century and continues to the present day. A pictorial display at Wellington Botanic Garden’s Tree House highlights key discoveries in this long trek, and also gives us a glimpse of some of the animals that shared the world with plants.
The display is in two halves. From 1 November to mid-December, the ‘scene’ is set, and includes a look at the landscape preceding the rise of trees. It then moves on to the Silurian, Devonian and Carboniferous periods, characterised by the appearance of the likes of scale trees, seed ferns and calamites…. and the swamp forests that gave rise to the production of coal.
The mid-December to 31 January half focuses on the Permian period, including Gondwana before its eventual breakup, and the beautiful, strange, gymnosperm Glossopteris that was widespread in the ancient southern continents. It then, finally, progresses to the world of ‘living fossils’ such as ginkgo and the even more primitive horsetails.
A public talk associated with the display will be held at the Tree House on 2 December.

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Millennium Native Forest Reserve, Led by volunteers from the Friends of Millennium Native Forest Reserve, this walk offers a fascinating insight into how a once-degraded farmland has been transformed into a thriving native bush and wetland. The Millennium Native Forest Reserve is a community asset established by Masterton South Rotary on land leased from Masterton Trust Lands Trust. It is maintained by a committee called Friends of Millennium Native Forest Reserve. Walk leaders will share the Reserve’s inspiring history — from its beginnings in 1993 as a community-led project to restore local biodiversity, to its official opening in 2000 as part of a nationwide millennium celebration. QR codes placed at key spots offer short films presented by local college students, bringing the Reserve’s stories, conservation work, and unique ecology to life. Along the way, participants will hear how volunteers have reintroduced native plants and nurtured a habitat for native birds, insects, and aquatic life.

As you explore the urban Reserve’s meandering tracks, keep an eye out for tūī and kererū - with a bit of luck, you might also spot a gecko basking in the sun, a darting skink, long and short finned eels in the waterways, koura beneath the shallows, dragonflies, and even wētā tucked away in the undergrowth. You’ll gain an appreciation for the dedication it takes to maintain the Reserve and discover ways to get involved in its ongoing care.

Walk format:
This easy-paced walk is suitable for all fitness levels and ages. The tracks are 2.6km of largely limed winding tracks, with sections of boardwalks. Note: there is no toilet available at this reserve.

We’ll depart from the Hillcrest St Reserve entrance at 2pm. The group will pause at key points to hear stories, scan QR codes, and observe wildlife. Expect 1 - 1.5hr walk.

Photo credits: Friends of Millennium Native Forest Reserve.
This walk is part of the Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025.

description:
Dragonflies are Amazing and Important - Why? Forest & Bird Talk, Ruary Mackenzie Dodds and his wife Kari de Koenigswarter are rated as Dragonfly Ambassadors by the British Dragonfly Society. Although they have recently been involved in the setting up of a Dragonfly Hotspot at Exbury Gardens in Hampshire, England, their work currently centres on New Zealand where awareness of the significance of dragonflies is possibly behind that of the U.K, which has a growing understanding that dragonflies are a key indicator of the health of waterspaces. In this talk, Ruary takes his listeners back to basics on the amazing life-cycle of these insects. He outlines typical preferred dragonfly habitats, and touches on identification of New Zealand species. In addition to Ruary’s talk, Kari’s larva demonstration table shows actual examples of the larval stages on NZ species.

In their New Zealand work, Ruary and Kari are carrying out survey work on behalf of the Greater Wellington Regional Council, and are preparing a dragonfly education pack for schools. They have also carried out five summer seasons of night-filming an endemic dragonfly species – the Bush Giant – that lives in a burrow! A Radio New Zealand Our Changing World programme has been devoted to their work. (https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/ourchangingworld/546925/dragonflies-masters-of-flight).

Ruary and Kari have been working with dragonflies since 1985. They opened Europe’s first Dragonfly Sanctuary in 1991, and founded the National Dragonfly Biomuseum in Northamptonshire in 1995. They and their team of volunteers continued work with the National Trust at Wicken Fen in Cambridgeshire, and were instrumental in the setting up of the Dragonfly Centre there in 2009. Their adventures were published in Ruary’s memoir, The Dragonfly Diaries (Saraband, 2014). Kari and Ruary have also published a how-to book, Dragonfly-Friendly Gardening (Saraband, 2024). Ruary is a Fellow of the Linnean Society. He has given talks in eight countries. He has appeared on both television and radio, and was awarded BBC Springwatch’s ‘Dragonfly Geek’ award. He has been featured in BBC Wildlife Magazine, The Scottish Field, and in Wildlife Trust and National Trust publications. Kari specializes in the larval stages of odonate life, while – even after over forty years – Ruary’s heart lifts at the sight of a dragonfly in flight, and he loves sharing this enthusiasm with his listeners!

description:
Kaicycle Community Open Day Mei (May) - Climate Festival edition!, Have you been looking for a chance to visit Kaicycle Urban Farm? Come along our Community Open Day in Mei / May, as part of the Climate Festival Pōneke.
9:30am - 12.30pm COMMUNITY WORKING BEE - Registrations required.
Growing local kai in ways that are good for the whenua is climate action. Come and get your hands in the māra, learn some skills, and meet some cool people. Please register at www.kaicycle.org.nz/volunteer
12:30PM - 1:30pm, KAI BREAK
Join us for a shared lunch and a chilled hang out in the māra. Please bring some kai to share if you can.
1:00PM - FARM TOUR
If you haven't been to our urban farm before, this is a great opportunity to find out what we're all about and how our farm and community composting works.
1:30pm - 3.00pm KOHA WORKSHOP: Climate Friendly Composting -
https://www.facebook.com/events/1704614757650028/
Registration required - email community@kaicycle.org.nz to register.
It’s well known that composting is a lot better than throwing food scraps in landfill - reducing greenhouse gas emissions, returning nutrients to the soil, improving soil health and microbiology, sequestering carbon in the soil, and growing more kai. But... composting still produces greenhouse gas emissions. The recipe and the composting method used can hugely affect the amount of greenhouse gases emitted during the decomposition of organic materials, and the quality and biological composition of the resulting compost can have climate implications too.
Join us to learn about a range of composting methods and the climate impact they have, and find out what practical techniques you can use to minimise emissions from composting at home and make the most healthy compost possible.

description:
Resilience and Emissions Reduction Workshop for Not-For-Profits | Blenheim, Ready your not-for-profit for the future
Do you know you need to take action to address climate change but don’t know where to start?
Do you want to strengthen your organisations’ planning and readiness for change?
Do you want practical tools and support to measure, assess, and report on your organisations’ impact?

In partnership with Rātā Foundation, our Earth+ Resilience and Emissions Reduction programme has been designed to flip the script on climate change, centering your organisation as agents of change and kitting you with the tools, support and community to make a difference; and it’s free of charge!
About the programme
With the support of the Terra Nova team and other programme participants, you will be guided to identify how your organisation is uniquely placed to contribute to the resilience and wellbeing of people and planet, and the opportunities and obstacles to creating positive change.
The programme is accessible and suitable for everyone, from those just starting on the journey, to those who have steps in place but are looking to gain access to further resources. This programme is not intended to add extra workload or deliverables for your organisation, it is an offer of support to integrate an Earth+ approach into your BAU; an answer to the question “what can we do about climate change?”
We know that every organisation’s capacity is different, so our support is available for you to utilise it when you need it until the end of 2025. This includes:
Access to a dedicated online community where you can connect with the Terra Nova team, other Rātā grantees and specialised partners. Ask questions, find resources and share your journey.
A toolkit of resources and impact sessions to develop your knowledge and connect you with the expertise and support to build resilience and tackle change in a range of impact areas.
Complementary access to the Cogo carbon emissions measurement tool, providing you the ability to quantify and report on your emissions impact and providing recommended actions for emissions reduction and cost savings, in an easy-to-use format.
It begins with a 1-day interactive workshop to kick things off. By the end of the workshop, you will walk away:
Feeling more empowered about the future, with a deeper understanding of resilience and climate change as it relates to your organisation’s context.
Having explored how you can make change positive and achievable, centered on the needs of your community and team. 
With free access to Cogo carbon manager, an emissions profile, report of your carbon footprint and practical action you can take to reduce your emissions.
Having built a network of support and gained free-to-use practical tools and templates.
Note: we will be running multiple workshops throughout the year; you only need to attend one workshop to join the programme. If you prefer an alternate date, please head to our Humanitix profile to find the corresponding event. 
The programme is fully funded for not-for-profit organisations and registrations are now open for 2025! Register for the programme and secure your spot in a workshop through this Humanatix event, and a member of the Terra Nova team will be in touch to confirm your enrollment. For more information about the programme and workshop, visit the Terra Nova website.
We look forward to welcoming you into our community of changemakers!

description:
Destination Earth, Expect your senses to be stirred in a new art installation. Destination Earth aims to inspire climate action through art. It incorporates satellite data, real-time generative music, and responds to audience movement in real-time. Using video and immersive sound, audiences will be challenged to reconsider the rhythm of living as humans. 
You are invited to dive into the flow of the Southern Ocean and explore the pulse of the Antarctic circumpolar current. Participate by adjusting your walking patterns and breathing to ‘regenerate’ the world around you. Motion sensors will pick up your activity and adjust the environment to suit. At a sensorial level the effects of climate change will come to life. 

Destination Earth is a collaboration between Cellule Studio (UK) and Victoria University of Wellington. The work, by artist Salome Bazin, mixes art, science, and technology. It emphasises the urgent need to slow down human activity.  

A bi-cultural perspective is also central to the experience. Māori symbolic views of the ocean are included, offering a richer narrative of the global climate.
 
Image credit: Cellule Studio, directed by Salomé Bazin.

description:
Wellington Climate Fresk Workshop, Do you want to be part of the solution to tackle climate change but don’t have the time to become a climate scientist? Join us for a 3-hour interactive workshop to explore the causes and consequences of climate disturbances.
Based on the IPCC report and played by over 2 million people worldwide, this collaborative workshop allows you to understand the key issues of climate change to empower you to take action.
How it works:
The workshop is based on a 42-card game. Each card represents an element, a cause or a consequence of climate change.
In teams, guided by your facilitator, you are encouraged to find the cause-effect relationship between the different components of climate change. Collective intelligence will get you from one deck of card to the next!
This step-by-step reconstruction provides keys to understand the complexity and develop an overview of climate change.
Agenda:
Introduction, 15 mins
Fresk Card Game, 1 1/2 hours
Debrief and Actions, 1 hour 15 mins
Climate Fresk is an excellent opportunity to understand the key elements of climate change and what you can do to be part of the solution. No previous climate knowledge is needed.

Tea, coffee and snacks will be served during the short break. Workshop run by Climate Training Co. Ltd. Donations welcome!

description:
Dragonflies & Damselflies are Amazing and Important - Forest&bird Talk, Ruary Mackenzie Dodds and his wife Kari de Koenigswarter are rated as Dragonfly Ambassadors by the British Dragonfly Society. Although they have recently been involved in the setting up of a Dragonfly Hotspot at Exbury Gardens in Hampshire, England, their work currently centres on New Zealand where awareness of the significance of dragonflies is possibly behind that of the U.K, which has a growing understanding that dragonflies are a key indicator of the health of waterspaces. In this talk, Ruary takes his listeners back to basics on the amazing life-cycle of these insects. He outlines typical preferred dragonfly habitats, and touches on identification of New Zealand species. In addition to Ruary’s talk, Kari’s larva demonstration table shows actual examples of the larval stages on NZ species.

In their New Zealand work, Ruary and Kari are carrying out survey work on behalf of the Greater Wellington Regional Council, and are preparing a dragonfly education pack for schools. They have also carried out five summer seasons of night-filming an endemic dragonfly species – the Bush Giant – that lives in a burrow! A Radio New Zealand Our Changing World programme has been devoted to their work. (https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/ourchangingworld/546925/dragonflies-masters-of-flight).

Ruary and Kari have been working with dragonflies since 1985. They opened Europe’s first Dragonfly Sanctuary in 1991, and founded the National Dragonfly Biomuseum in Northamptonshire in 1995. They and their team of volunteers continued work with the National Trust at Wicken Fen in Cambridgeshire, and were instrumental in the setting up of the Dragonfly Centre there in 2009. Their adventures were published in Ruary’s memoir, The Dragonfly Diaries (Saraband, 2014). Kari and Ruary have also published a how-to book, Dragonfly-Friendly Gardening (Saraband, 2024). Ruary is a Fellow of the Linnean Society. He has given talks in eight countries. He has appeared on both television and radio, and was awarded BBC Springwatch’s ‘Dragonfly Geek’ award. He has been featured in BBC Wildlife Magazine, The Scottish Field, and in Wildlife Trust and National Trust publications. Kari specializes in the larval stages of odonate life, while – even after over forty years – Ruary’s heart lifts at the sight of a dragonfly in flight, and he loves sharing this enthusiasm with his listeners!

description:
Botanical Insights talk - Ancient plants, This talk, which partners a major pictorial display at the Tree House, starts with a look at landscapes preceding the rise of trees. It then focuses on the Silurian, Devonian and Carboniferous geological periods, characterised by the appearance of the likes of scale trees, seed ferns and calamites.….and the swamp forests that gave rise to the production of coal. Then it advances to the Permian period, including Gondwana prior to its eventual breakup, and the beautiful, strange, gymnosperm Glossopteris that was widespread in the ancient southern continents, embracing what is now New Zealand/Aotearoa. Finally, it progresses to the world of ‘living fossils’ such as ginkgo and the even more primitive horsetails. Attention will be drawn to some of the animals that populated this ancient world.

Located in the Treehouse Seminar Room, Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.
Free of charge. You’re welcome to bring along your own ‘brown bag’ lunch to enjoy during the talk.

The speaker is Reg Harris, a volunteer guide [botany] at Wellington Botanic Garden.
Reg delivers botany lectures for diverse audiences, delving into plant interactions, adaptive radiation, tropisms, and more. As a dedicated volunteer guide at Wellington Botanic Garden (WBG), he pioneered collaborations between WBG and Victoria University, organising annual field labs for biology students.

description:
Wairarapa Walking Festival 2025: Waiohine to Holdsworth Overnight, Note this is an overnight stay, starting from 9am Friday 21st November and finishing on Saturday 22nd November.
This guided overnight hike is the perfect introduction to tramping in the Tararua Ranges. Beginning with a spectacular crossing of the Waiohine Gorge suspension bridge — 94 metres long and 35 metres high — the walk follows fairly gentle terrain alongside the Waiohine River, through lush native bush, and without any steep climbs.

After a 9 am bus departure from Tranzit in Masterton, we travel to the Waiohine road-end (pickup available along the way at Carterton Station, timed to meet the train from Wellington) and set off on an 8 km walk to Tōtara Flats Hut. This Department of Conservation hut has bunkrooms with mattresses, cooking stoves, rainwater taps, a woodstove, and a long-drop toilet. We have booked most of the hut’s 26 bunks. On Day 2, wake to the sound of native birds before continuing on an 11 km walk to Holdsworth Lodge, where the bus will return us to Masterton.

What to bring: Good shoes or boots, rain jacket, backpack, sleeping bag (in a waterproof bag), overnight clothes, toiletries, any personal medications, food, cooking pot, plate, cutlery, toilet paper, water bottle, and snacks. Optional: togs and towel, battery bank. All rubbish must be carried out.

Important:
If you would like extra information and your gear checked, please attend an information session with your walk leader on Sunday 2nd November 6pm, at the Carterton Courthouse.
Must have a good level of fitness. Dogs are not permitted. There are no river crossings except by bridge, but one section requires walking along the riverbank to avoid a slip. If the river is too high, the walk will enter and return via Holdsworth. The walk leader will carry a Personal Locator Beacon, lighter, newspaper for the woodstove, and a basic first aid kit. No refunds except in exceptional circumstances or if the walk is cancelled.

description:
Evening meeting - A mycology of New Zealand in 10 fungi, Speaker: Dr Geoff Ridley. Fungi are often overlooked. Most people only become aware of them when there is a problem, the bathroom ceiling goes mouldy, the roses need spraying because of the black spot, mushrooms sprout all over the lawn. The bigger role that fungi play in our lives is missed. This is the story of ten little-known fungi that are important biologically, culturally, historically, and economically in Aotearoa.
Geoff is a mycologist who studied the larger fungi in the Ōrongorongo Valley for his PhD at Victoria University of Wellington, and as a forest mycologist and pathologist at the Forest Research Institute in Rotorua. He currently works in the nationally significant collections of fungi held by Manaaki Whenua – Landcare Research. His personal interest is in discovering the fungi of the Kaiwharawhara Valley in Wellington.

description:
Electrify Porirua: how to save money on your energy bills feat. Mike Casey, It keeps getting more expensive to heat our homes and water, cook our meals and get around. But there is a way to avoid those rising costs and Electrify Porirua will show you how.  
Most Porirua homes could be saving thousands on their energy bills each year, while also slashing emissions, simply by upgrading their gas and petrol machines to the electric equivalents available today - and ideally powering them with solar and batteries for more self-sufficiency in case of power cuts or natural disasters.
Porirua has crossed the “electrification tipping point” where homes, farms and businesses can now save money and reduce their emissions by going electric. It’s a massive win-win and a lot of people don’t know about the potential savings that are hiding in their cupboards, kitchens and driveways. 
Rewiring Aotearoa is trying to change that and we’re supporting grassroots action across the country. Community electrification groups are popping up all over the place and helping to raise awareness about the benefits for their local region and helping locals through the process. Now, it’s time to bring the buzz to Porirua.
Come along to hear from Mike Casey, who is saving tens of thousands a year on his all-electric solar-powered cherry orchard, and find out how electrifying Porirua is the smartest, cheapest, and healthiest way to power our lives.

Healing Trauma and the Nervous System- Ancient wisdom for modern resilience
Stress and struggle leave their mark on both body and mind, sometimes in ways we can’t easily undo. Just as knots form in the body, impressions and tensions accumulate in the mind. While we can’t change the past, the Bhagavad-gita teaches that we can shape our future—what we choose to cultivate now carries us forward.
In this one-hour workshop, we’ll explore how philosophical and spiritual wisdom can help us rise above the tangles of trauma and anxiety. Through practical insights, open discussion, and guidance from the Gita’s philosophy, we’ll look at how to build resilience—not only by steadying the nervous system, but by exploring the deeper self beyond the changing body and mind.
Meet your host, Sivananda
Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. description:
Well Elders: A Masterclass in promoting wellbeing in older people - Te-Whanganui-a-Tara - Wellington (WE2026/03), Aotearoa-New Zealand’s population is ageing rapidly. There are more and more people living into old age. The World Health Organisation has identified that as the baby boomer generation ages, many will enjoy reasonable physical health, however mental health issues, in particular depression and anxiety, will be a prevalent health issue. Therefore promoting mental wellbeing must be a major focus for those working with older people.
A older person's sense of wellbeing is determined by proven social, economic and cultural factors that either positively or negatively impact on older people. It is much broader than a wellness approach. How best to address factors such as loneliness, diminishing physical health, income and food security, significant loss, elder abuse, the invisibility of older people, cultural alienation and impacts of rural to urban migration and immigration from the Pacific Islands in the 1950's and 60's using a wellbeing framework will be a focus of the workshops.
However, while promoting wellbeing is an effective strategy in mitigating the impact of mood and anxiety disorders in older people, it should not be the primary aim of wellbeing promotion. The emphasis must be on ageing well and thriving elders.
Hear from an experienced wellbeing specialist who has lectured and implemented numerous wellbeing programmes at the local, national and international levels.
Over recent years there has been a greater awareness of the fundamental role that wellbeing plays in enabling individuals and communities to thrive. Take the opportunity to learn how older peoples' workers and agencies can put wellbeing at the heart of what they do that enables older people to thrive. This workshop provides a comprehensive overview of the research, evidence and latest international thinking on promoting wellbeing in older people as applied to the Aotearoa-New Zealand context
Well elders: thriving through participating and contributing
Informed by social, cultural and environmental determinants, adopting a wellbeing framework enable workers and agencies to identify how they can be "agents of wellbeing" for older people and how to incorporate wellbeing outcomes into their work. Based on these determinants and frameworks it is possible to develop an evidence-based programme logic with clear wellbeing outcomes and indicators and evaluation tools. An overview of the determinants and outcomes will be covered in the workshop.
Mental wellbeing is not just the responsibility of the health sector, the workshop is ideal training for anyone working with older people in:
aged care facilities
churches
community based older people agencies
local government
older persons' mental health services
primary health care
The training does not offer a ready-made older peoples' wellbeing package but rather helps participants to:
understand the underlying theory, principles and best practice in promoting mental wellbeing,
identify the enablers and disablers of wellbeing in older people,
to move from an outputs to outcomes focus in designing wellbeing programmes or activities

TAKING A STAND AGAINST AGEISM AND PROMOTING POSITIVE AGEING

description:
CBT skills for physical health practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand, Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT) is a psychological intervention initially developed for emotional disorders. It is now widely used in supporting people to deal with the challenges of physical ill-health. Professionals from various backgrounds can learn to use a simplified CBT skills set, and use of these skills enables them to be more effective in managing aspects of their patients’ distress.
The training is a mix of theory, skills demonstration and skills practice, giving participants a better understanding of the applicability of the skill set in their area of practice and providing some skills to take away. Training sessions are spaced to allow participants to use their new skills in their clinical practice. Each participant reflects on their learning and their work with a specific patient, and the whole group reflects on lessons learned. In this way, learning remains rooted in participants’ clinical practice. These CBT courses are consistently evaluated highly by participants.
The Course
Teaching will be commenced with 2 days of in person sessions. 19th and 20th Feb 2026 at Mary Potter Hospice, Wellington and subsequently 2 sessions on-line via Zoom. These will be either 18th or 19th March an 22nd or 23rd April 2026.
Attendance at all sessions is mandatory to complete the course.
The courses cost is $850 per person (incl GST).
The Trainers
Kathy Burn was a Clinical Nurse Specialist in Palliative Care who went on to train in CBT and to develop the CBT service at St Christopher’s Hospice, London. She now works in CBT in chronic pain, and she teaches and supervises CBT trainees at the institute of Psychiatry, London.
Kathryn Mannix was a Palliative Medicine Consultant and CBT therapist. She developed ‘CBT First Aid’ to enable palliative care clinicians to adapt skills from CBT into their clinical practice. She is an author. There are insights into her use of CBT in her books With the End in Mind and Listen.
Terms and Conditions
Attendance: In order to create a learning community for each course, it is important that each person on a course attends every session and is able to join in the discussions by keeping up with the course. By accepting a place on a particular course, you agree to attend all the sessions, to arrive on time, and to work alongside your group members during the session to support each other's learning. Each session builds on the last, and you'll be asked to put your new learning into practice in- between sessions. Building learning groups in this way means we can't add new trainees after a course has begun.
We are not able to run catch-up sessions for sessions missed. If you miss sessions, you may be asked to withdraw from the course and no refunds will be given.
Refunds/Canellations: Once you sign up and pay, we won't be able to refund your payment unless we can reallocate your place to another person before the course begins. The deadline for cancelling your place is 28 days before the day and time of the first session. If you cancel and we can fill your place with another person, we'll offer you the choice of a refund or a place on a future course, if places are available. We will do our best to fill your place, but we can't promise this. Refunds will incur an administration fee.
Dates and Times of Sessions: all dates and times are given in NZ time, and this varies over the year. It is up to you to check the correct time in your time zone: you may find this website useful to check your own time zone with Auckland NZ time on each specific date: https://www.worldtimebuddy.com/
Trainers: we have a team of trainers, all of whom are experienced CBT therapists and trainers, and all are familiar with applying CBT in physical health settings. Different sessions may be taught by different trainers, or by 'guest appearances' by some of our team. The team of trainers will ensure there is continuity of content and of learning as the course progresses.
Special circumstances: Sometimes, life events appear unexpectedly. If something unexpected prevents you from attending, please let us know as early as you can, and we will give consideration to how we might be able to support you to continue your training if that is what you wish to do.

This will be a gentle Somatic Breathwork workshop designed to help you regulate your nervous system, decompress emotionally, and find embodied clarity. Using nose-dominant breathing techniques, optional mouth exhales, and gentle somatic movements, this session will support you in releasing tension and building to a potential cathartic experience.

Who this is for
This workshop is perfect for:
•⁠ ⁠Those feeling stressed or overwhelmed
•⁠ ⁠Individuals experiencing wired-and-tired fatigue
•⁠ ⁠Anyone struggling with overthinking or racing thoughts
•⁠ ⁠People facing sleep disruptions or insomnia

•⁠ ⁠Improved sleep quality
•⁠ ⁠A lifted mood
•⁠ ⁠Greater emotional range without feeling overwhelmed

Yoga mats are provided but you are most welcome to bring:
•⁠ ⁠Additional yoga mat
•⁠ ⁠Warm layers and socks
•⁠ ⁠Water bottle
•⁠ ⁠Small towel
•⁠ ⁠Optional eye mask or light scarf
•⁠ ⁠Journal and pen
•⁠ ⁠If you tend to feel cold, consider bringing a blanket

Pre-class prep
•⁠ ⁠Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
•⁠ ⁠Hydrate well throughout the day.
•⁠ ⁠Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
•⁠ ⁠Limit caffeine intake 4 hours prior.
•⁠ ⁠Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
•⁠ ⁠If you have health conditions, check with your provider.
•⁠ ⁠Feel free to share any concerns with Lynn before the session at {{hi@lynofuro.co.nz}}.

Contraindications and safety
Breathwork can alter your breath rate and surface emotions. It may not be suitable for those who are pregnant, have serious cardiovascular issues, uncontrolled blood pressure, or a history of seizures. This practice is not medical care. We offer a conservative track with nasal-only breathing and smaller ranges of motion, along with breaks as needed.

Aftercare
Post-workshop, we encourage you to drink water, eat nourishing food, engage in simple movements or a short walk, and journal any insights. Emotional waves can continue for 24 to 48 hours, so reach out if you need support.

Facilitator
Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach specializing in breathwork and Reiki, focusing on corporate burnout, chronic pain, and stress. Her approach is nurturing and gentle, ensuring a supportive environment for all participants.

description:
Confident & Competent Suicide Prevention Training Series - Tāmaki Makaurau-Auckland (CC2026/03), CONFIDENT AND COMPETENT SUICIDE PREVENTION TRAINING
To reduce the high rates of suicide in this country a workforce confident and competent in assessing risk and providing ongoing support to suicidal people is essential.
Recent coroners’ findings highlighted the need for workers in the health, social services and counselling/psychotherapy sectors to regularly update their knowledge and competency in suicide risk assessment and intervention. This training should be a core component of practitioners’ ongoing professional development. Advanced practitioners such as counsellors, psychotherapists and clinicians should not only be knowledgeable about suicide risk assessment but also highly competent in undertaking an assessment and assessing the level of risk. The training attended should match the worker's scope of practice. Those working in the non-mental health sectors must be also be competent in making an informed referral to crisis services.They must also be up to date in their competency and capability to engage with the suicidal individual.
This advanced-level workshop address the concerns raised by coroners and are designed for clinicians counsellors and psychotherapists. Rather than a siloed approach to assessment and support strategies, this training emphasises the interconnection of the two and presents them as part of the continuum of suicide intervention and care.
Designed specifically for the New Zealand context, this training is being recommended by counsellors all over the country as a must attend workshop.

description:
Answering the unanswerable: Counselling people and whānau bereaved through suicide - Tāmaki Makaurau - Auckland (ATU2026/04), The Lasting Impact of Suicide on Whānau and Communities
The impact of suicide on whānau, hapū, friends, colleagues, and communities is profound and enduring. Many individuals experience a complicated grieving process, further complicated by the stigma surrounding suicide and mental health issues.
Suicide also poses an increased risk of subsequent suicides within families. Intergenerational suicide contagion is recognised as a significant risk factor, with some studies indicating that a family history of suicide can raise the risk by as much as tenfold. Counselling should focus on addressing intergenerational suicide and suicide clusters; as Shneidman stated, postvention is "prevention for the next generation."
It is vital for counsellors assisting those grieving a suicide loss to be adept not only in bereavement support but also in helping individuals and families find meaning in the loss in ways that minimise the risk of suicide contagion within the family.

description:
Men's Circle: Authentic Conversations, Men’s Circle: Authentic Conversations

In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.

This is a free event, with an optional plant-based dinner available for $15. While there’s no obligation to stay for dinner, sharing a meal together offers a meaningful way to strengthen connections. Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply—offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.

The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings, and encourage personal growth—free from societal pressures to be stoic or self-reliant. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.

Structure of the Circle

Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.

A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.

Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.

Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.

Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.

No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.

Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.

Circle Agreements

Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.

Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.

Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."

No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.

Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group, but keep others' details private.

Meet Andre and Sri Jiva, your hosts

Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human—how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

description:
Beyond Behaviour: Supporting Neurodiverse Young People, Overview








Unlock fresh insights, practical strategies, and a deeper understanding of neurodiversity through this thought-provoking training
Beyond Behaviour: Supporting Neurodiverse Young People
Unlock fresh insights, practical strategies, and a deeper understanding of neurodiversity through this engaging and thought-provoking learning experience. Brought to you by Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective, this workshop is for anyone who works with, supports, influences, or cares for young people. Whether you're a youth worker, social worker, teacher, mentor, coach, parent, caregiver, or community practitioner, you'll gain valuable tools to strengthen relationships, foster belonging, and better support neurodiverse rangatahi to thrive. If supporting young people is part of your world, this is a learning opportunity you won't want to miss.

This interactive workshop explores the intersection of neurodiversity, trauma-sensitive practice, and effective youth development. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how trauma impacts the nervous system, and how power, privilege, communication styles, and adult behaviour can either support or hinder a young person’s sense of safety and connection. The workshop provides practical strategies for showing up as a safe, responsive adult, with a focus on both verbal and non-verbal communication.

The second part of the workshop focuses on practitioner wellbeing, helping participants recognise the importance of boundaries, sustainability, and preventing burnout in youth-focused roles. Through guided reflection, a meditative boundary-setting exercise, and an art-based activity, participants will develop a personalised visual resource that helps them identify and manage their own energy levels. Attendees will leave with greater self-awareness, practical tools, and a stronger foundation for supporting neurodiverse young people while sustaining their own wellbeing.

Made possible thanks to support from Department of Internal Affairs and Rata Foundation. Free for Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective Members.

Meet your kaiako;

Elana Cohen
Elana is a local occupational therapist with 22 years of experience working with neurodivergent people. Her practice is focused on empowering people to know themselves deeply and equipping the adults around young people to best set up supportive environments for youth to thrive. She is affirming of neurodivergent identities and trauma-sensitive. In addition to her Masters degree in occupational therapy, Elana has done advanced training in trauma, attachment, autism, and sensory processing and regularly presents on these topics.

Meagan Goodman
Meg (they/she) had the privilege of growing up on a small island in the Pacific Northwest of the US where they spent their growing up years playing in nature. Meg moved to Aotearoa in 2011 and deeply resonates with holistic approaches to wellbeing such as Te Whare Tapa Whā. Meg has worked in a diversity of roles within the public health sector, including establishing a youth mental health service across Te Tau Ihu (Top of the South Island). Meg is an active researcher and has focused on topics such as Rainbow youth experiences of accessing mental health services in the Nelson/Tasman region, and exploring the community construct of Queer Joy in an international mixed-method study. Meg is passionate about supporting people in the queer and neurodivergent communities and applies an intersectional lens to understanding experiences of distress and trauma.

Are traditional notions of masculinity meeting the needs of men in 2026? How the changes in men’s roles and identity contribute to suicide in men.
A vision for men’s wellbeing: An holistic approach to conceptualising men’s wellbeing and key mental wellbeing messages for men.
IT'S TIME FOR A SERIOUS RETHINK IN HOW WE PREVENT MALE SUICIDE AND TO TAKE SUICIDE IN MEN OUT OF THE TOO HARD BASKET

BE PART OF THE SOLUTION
IN THIS MONTH OF MOVEMBER TAKE THE OPPORTUNITY TO PARTICIPATE  IN A WORKSHOP WITH INTERNATIONALLY RESPECTED AND AWARD WINNING MALE SUICIDE PREVENTION SPECIALIST BARRY TAYLOR
It matters that men are able to optimise their wellbeing.  Well men contribute to well whānau, communities, workplaces, economy and society.
Drawing on his lived experience and his extensive experience in engaging, assessing and supporting suicidal men of different cultures, age groups, genders and sexualities, he offers practical and time proven approaches to both preventing male suicide, engaging with a suicidal man and effective initiatives to optimise men's wellbeing.
"Helping men and boys to transition from sad blokes to well men must be our focus"

description:
Men’s Circle: Real Conversations, Men’s Circle: Real Conversations
In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.

About this Event

Men’s Circle: Real Conversations
In a society where men are expected to always have it together, this space is for being honest, not perfect.
This is a free offering but there’s the option to stay for an amazing plant-based dinner ($15). There’s no pressure to join, but sitting down to eat together is a simple, powerful way to deepen the sense of connection. Andre & Sri Jiva aren’t running this circle for profit and they are genuinely invested in creating real, meaningful spaces for men to connect.
The Men’s Circle is a gathering where men are able to connect in a safe, supportive space to share experiences, express emotions, and foster personal growth. Free from societal expectations of stoicism or self-sufficiency. Through open sharing and mutual support, participants are empowered to build resilience, self-reflection, and a stronger sense of identity and purpose.
Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the personholding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is op-tional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking,interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicitedadvice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fosteringtrust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share whats alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements topromote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicitedadvice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group, but keep others details private.




Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!

What’s on the menu?
Creamy Farfalle Pasta with Plant-Based Bacon
Toasted Bruschetta with “Cheese”, Tomato and Parsley
Fresh Salad with Balsamic Vinegar
Berry Vanilla Muffins with Whipped Cream




Meet Your Hosts: Andre and Sri Jiva
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human—how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

description:
Yoga Nidra, Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

This workshop explores why our thoughts get stuck in loops of worry, doubt, and replay. You’ll also learn how the body and nervous system become conditioned to repeat these mental patterns, creating the familiar cycle of racing thoughts and restless emotions.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll not only understand the deeper roots of over-thinking, but you’ll also walk away with simple, repeatable techniques to interrupt mental loops, ease the nervous system, and create a lasting sense of inner peace.

Waking up tired, even after a full night’s sleep
Overthinking decisions and feeling emotionally reactive
Craving peace but feeling disconnected from your body
Often feeling “on” and unable to fully relax

Through guided somatic breathwork, gentle movement, and nervous system education, you’ll be supported to safely release stored tension, calm your system, and access clarity from within.

Contraindications for Breathwork:
Breathwork can be a powerful tool but may not be suitable for everyone. Please consult your healthcare provider before participating if you have:
Cardiovascular issues (e.g., high blood pressure, heart disease)
Respiratory conditions (e.g., asthma, COPD)
A history of seizures or epilepsy
Diagnosed mental health conditions (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder)
Pregnancy (some breath patterns may need modification)
Recent surgery or physical injuries that limit movement
You are always welcome to participate in the somatic and movement elements without engaging in deep breathwork—your safety and well-being are our priority.

Lynofuro is an Integrative Somatic Coach and Breathwork Facilitator who helps intuitive, high-performing women overcome emotional burnout and restore energetic balance. Her work blends somatics, breath, and energy alignment to support lasting transformation.

description:
F*ck the Small Talk: Wellington #10, Sign up here: https://luma.com/ftstwellington10
F*ck the Small Talk has traveled the world from Berlin, Melbourne, London, Lisbon, and Mexico City, to Lisbon and is now coming to Wellington!

WHAT'S THIS ABOUT?
FTST is a one-of-a-kind social experience where strangers come together for an afternoon of meaningful, fun, and deep conversation. It’s also just a different & cool way of meeting new people by getting a bit out of your comfort zone and skipping the small talk!
Join us for games, talks, and connections with friends you haven’t met yet. Join if you get annoyed after being asked what you do, where you are from, and how long you have been in Wellington every single time you meet someone. If you feel that there are better questions in life then this is the place for you.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
We start with a short & sweet intro talk followed by a few light-hearted group games to warm up. Don't worry, nothing too awkward! After that, we split you up into small groups and start with the conversation rounds (with 3-4 people). We'll have awesome question cards that will guide the flow of the conversation. You’ll never have to speak in public if you don’t want to!

HOW TO JOIN?
Take 2 minutes to fill out our form

https://luma.com/ftstwellington10
Our events are limited to 30 handpicked guests to ensure a cozy atmosphere. We prioritize a balance in gender and cultural diversity, making each gathering a unique blend of perspectives! If you're invited you'll receive an invite with a special link via our ticketing platform Luma

HOW MUCH IS IT?
The cost to attend is NZD 23 (early llama) - NZD 25 (general llama) and includes the following:
3 hours of facilitated and curated activities
Light snacks to keep the energy going (only if outdoors)
A space to meet new people in the least boring way possible
Supporting our mission to slowly eliminate small talk around the world
Also includes those pesky ticket fees!

WHERE IS IT?
We host our events in awesome cafes, rooftops, and bars across the city. We only reveal the location to ticket holders 24 hours before the event.

WHAT THEY SAY
“Great way to connect with people in a more meaningful way. Get to the heart of the matter, dive straight into what really counts!” - Matthias

“This is the kind of activity humanity needs every weekend. Thank you for all.” - Sonya

“F*ck the Small Talk changes the narrative from "Where are you from?" to "When was the last time you laughed uncontrollably?" and I think that's beautiful.” - Monika

“I loved F*ck the small talk, I was a little bit nervous at first but they are pros at making you feel comfortable with the rest of the group, the activities are really fun and I enjoyed every second (consider that the one who's saying this is very, very shy). Give it a try!” - Brenda

"it’s a wonderful experience, it’s like being a kid again, when you were at the park, playing with other kids, and just decided you were going to be best friends for the next hours. Maybe you’ll never see those kids again. But that hour was amazing because you both opened up and trusted each other." - Sara

“Lively, interesting, introspective, completely open and no judgement. Everyone that joined was ready for great conversation and helped with different perspectives. So much fun! I can't wait for the next one! “ - Yaz

Check out our 100+ Google reviews: https://goo.gl/maps/TpZy77bfPFkGoikn7

FAQ
• Can I come alone?
Of course, in fact, we encourage it! 99% of people do.

• I signed up but never got an invite. Why?
We usually get a high volume of sign-ups yet we like to keep it cozy & only about 30 people. We believe this is a good number to ensure an awesome experience! Please try again next time if do not receive an invite - no hard feelings

• Why do you charge?
We value our time and put a lot of love, planning, and effort into creating & designing these experiences.
This is our project/business and what we give to the world and we think everything should be a fair exchange! However, money should never be the reason for people not to attend. If you can’t afford it simply get in touch with us

• I'm digging this! Can I get involved somehow?
Sure thing, send us a message!

• Can I bring my cute dog/llama?
It depends on where the event is! Message us to make sure. But it's always a YES in our hearts.

• Can I get a refund if I can't make it?
Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds or ticket transfers to another event date if you cannot attend with a notice of less than 5 days notice. BUTTTT feel free to pass on your ticket to a friend, provided they also sign up for the form
--

Two nights, one ticket, endless Halloween chaos in Wellington. Join both crawls with drinks, music, and costume madness.

About this Event


🎃🍺 Halloween Madness Weekend Pass 2025 – Wellington 🎃🍺

Two nights of crawls. One ticket. Zero excuses.
Halloween in Wellington isn’t just one party — it’s a whole weekend. With the Halloween Madness Weekend Pass, you’ll unlock access to two epic bar crawls:
Friday, October 31st → Haunted Halloween Bar Crawl
Saturday, November 1st → Beer & Spirits: Halloween Booze Crawl

Double the venues, double the specials, double the fun. Whether you’re into pumpkin brews, tequila shots, or just want an excuse to rock your scariest (or funniest) costume twice, this pass is your best deal for Halloween weekend.




WHAT’S INCLUDED
✔️ Entry to both Friday & Saturday night crawls

✔️ Crawl-only drink deals at every stop
✔️ Digital crawl map to guide your night

HOW THE WEEKEND FLOWS
👉 Wristband Pickup: Check in between 7:30–10:30 PM each night at the opening venue to collect your pass.
👉 Bar Hopping: From 8:30–11:30 PM, explore multiple walkable venues — pubs, clubs, and breweries — all offering specials.
👉 The Last Stop: Each crawl closes at a featured nightclub from 11:30 PM–2:00 AM with DJs and dance floors packed.




WEEKEND VIBE
👻 Costumes aren’t required but highly encouraged — expect the streets to be packed with zombies, witches, superheroes, and some of the funniest DIY outfits you’ll see all year.
⚡ Early bird tickets start at just $25 for the full weekend. Prices rise as Halloween gets closer — secure your spot now.


PARTICIPATING VENUES
The full lineup of bars and clubs will be released closer to the event. Expect high-energy DJs, themed rooms, and Halloween drink specials at every stop.




⚠️ EVENT RULES & DISCLAIMER

ENTRY REQUIREMENTS
18+ Only: All guests must be 18 years or older with a valid government-issued photo ID. No exceptions.
Wristbands Required: Your wristband is your ticket. Present your Eventbrite ticket/QR code at check-in to claim it. Wristbands must be worn the entire night for access to crawl venues. If you miss the pickup window (before 10:30 PM at the listed check-in), you forfeit entry.


CRAWL GUIDELINES
On-Time Check-In: Arrive during designated hours (7:30–10:30 PM). Late arrivals cannot be accommodated.
Proxy Pickup: If you can’t make it, you may authorize a friend to collect your wristband.
Venue Timing: Specials and entry are only valid during the timeframes listed on the Digital Bar List.
Day-Of Updates: Always check the Digital Crawl Map on event day for the latest venue info, changes, or closures.
Self-Guided Crawl: No hosts will lead groups. Use the crawl map to navigate between bars.
Venue Capacity: If a location is full, you may have to wait. Access is not guaranteed at every bar.


VENUE POLICIES
Right to Refuse: Venues may deny entry or remove anyone due to intoxication, dress code violations, offensive costumes, or inappropriate behavior.
Security Checks: Wristbands do not exempt you from ID or bag checks. Standard venue security applies.
Drink Specials: Offered at the discretion of participating bars; they may change or end without notice.
Venue Awareness: If staff aren’t aware of the crawl, contact the rep listed on the crawl map. If unavailable, proceed to another participating venue.


TICKET & EVENT TERMS
All Sales Final: No refunds, exchanges, or transfers. If the event is canceled outright (without reschedule), refunds excluding fees will be processed automatically.
Rain or Shine: Crawl will proceed regardless of weather. Venues and lineup are subject to change.
Late / Wrong Venue: Tickets are valid only during scheduled crawl hours. No refunds for late arrivals or showing up at the wrong check-in.
Costume Policy: No weapons or weapon-like props. Offensive costumes are prohibited and may result in denied entry.


LIABILITY WAIVER
By purchasing a ticket, you acknowledge that participation is at your own risk. Risks include but are not limited to: injury, illness, property damage, theft, accidents, alcohol-related incidents, or death.
You hereby release, waive, and discharge Events Per Se, its owners, staff, contractors, sponsors, affiliates, and participating venues from all claims or liability, whether caused by negligence or otherwise, for any injury, loss, illness, or death occurring before, during, or after the event.
You further agree to indemnify and hold harmless Events Per Se and all released parties from any expenses, claims, or legal costs arising from your actions during the crawl.
By attending, you confirm you’ve read, understood, and agreed to these terms in full.

description:
Athol McCredie - Spencer Digby Studio Collection, Athol McCredie is Curator of Photography at Te Papa. He will talk about the Spencer Digby Studio collection held by Te Papa. The studio was founded in 1931 by Spencer Digby and was taken over by Ron and Inge Woolf in 1960, who ran it under the same name until the mid-1970s.
It was a portrait studio where anybody who was anyone in (or visiting) Wellington was photographed, from prime ministers to debutantes.
Athol will also talk about early twentieth-century photographer Leslie Adkin, the subject of his most recent book, ‘Leslie Adkin: Farmer Photographer’.
Thursday, October 9th, Tararua Tramping Club (4 Moncrieff St, Mt Victoria), Doors Open at 7pm
If you’re curious about the Wellington Photographic Society, you’re welcome to attend two meetings for free before deciding whether to join. It’s a great way to meet the community and see what we’re all about!
https://wps.wps.org.nz/

description:
Unity Book Club February 2025 | Service, About the book: 
What's this book about? Is there a restroom? Do you have gluten-free bagels? Do you work here? Do you have a restroom? Do I buy books or rent books or what?
The worst thing about a bookshop is the customers. Then there's the gift-wrapping, the invoicing, the stock takes. The Yelp reviews that inevitably contribute to self-loathing.

In his late forties, Sean is still a frustrated bookseller who should have written his novel already. Instead, he spends his days drowning in his overwhelming sense of contempt -for LA, for its readers, for its casual disdain for service. And what, or whom, is he serving anyway?

Biting, hilarious and self-aware, John Tottenham's debut novel is a razor-sharp dissection of the modern scourges of gentrification, male vanity, jealousy and the worth of literature in a digital age.

Melissa and Eden will be hosting our monthly book club to discuss some of the excellent recently released books.

In February we will be discussing Service by John Tottenham.

description:

After a sold-out run in February, the Ruapehu Mountaineer is back. If you’ve been thinking about it, now’s the time to lock in a seat.

This is a full-day steam-hauled rail journey through the Central North Island to Mt Ruapehu. You’ll travel in comfortable heritage carriages with large viewing windows, an open-air viewing platform, and a café carriage onboard. It’s an easy, relaxed way to take in some of the best scenery on the network, from the Kapiti Coast through the Manawatū and across the Mangaweka viaducts.

At Ohakune, you’ll transfer by coach up to Whakapapa Village, where you’ve got a few hours to do your own thing. Grab lunch, take in the alpine views, or add on the Sky Waka gondola for a trip up the mountain.

It’s a long but rewarding day, and a pretty unique way to experience Mt Ruapehu. Ideal for families, groups, or anyone keen on a proper steam day out.

The folks at Forever GM have come through with a crowdpleaser!

Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Flagons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s own Beer Engine is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too. There are a couple of reasons for that:

1. D&D is for the whole family and...

2. It’s at a bar (and who abandons their kids at a bar?!)

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together. And the tavern keeper will have special barbecue and butterbeer for sale for all ages feasting!

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

The inaugural Dungeons and Flagons sold out in a week - so book fast, adventurer!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle) but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

description:
The Inevitabilism Panel, We're told AI is Progress, progress that cannot be stopped, that it will change the way we work and live, from business to education and the commons. But who says? Whose progress and whose AI is it anyway? Is societal progress really bound to technological innovation, or are there other ways of reading - and even shaping - positive social change?
Technological Determinism is described as the belief system that social progress is driven by technological innovation, which in turn follows an "inevitable" course." This panel will take a good hard look at this 'inevitabilism' - its forces and politics - with a view to our shared future in Aotearoa and the Pacific.
Join us for a rigorous evening of discussion with a view to how we might gain more understanding - and more say - as to the reach and influence new technologies have over our autonomy, dignity, communities and cultures.

There will be two sessions on 12 November at Rydges Wellington CBD - 10am and 2pm.
The presentation includes:
Safe access and effective engagement of male survivors with support services
Dispelling some of the common myths about male victims of sexual harm
Navigate the misunderstandings that create barriers to engagement with support services
Highlight the role of lived experience as an effective engagement model
Collaboration and partnerships to welcome and embrace cultural and gender diversity within the male survivor community
Supporting complex trauma requires a shared response from several organisations, each with different skills and experience – no single agency or organisation can do it alone.

description:
Project Management 101, Dates:Wednesday 5 November, 9am-4.30pm & Thursday 6 November , 9am-4.30pm
Presenter: Paul Sutton, Nonsuch.
This two-day instructor led course has been designed to introduce the concepts of Project Management to help ensure a common understanding – regardless of whether you are a project manager, sponsor, team member or coordinator. The course covers the unique language, principles and tools of project management and builds a case for their application back at the workplace. This course will ensure you are equipped to manage your projects efficiently and successfully.
Ideal for individuals who have no previous experience with project management, or those looking for a refresher. Also ideal for those wishing to develop an understanding of project management as they progress into Project Administration and/or Project Coordination.
Learning Outcomes
At the completion of the 2-day course, you will:
Have a common understanding of what a project is and how it is different from day-to-day, business as usual work
Understand key terminology, principles and tools related to project management including how adaptive (Agile) and predictive (Waterfall) methodologies are different and how they work together
Understand the difference between project objectives, outputs, and outcomes
Learn and practice how to plan a project, based an output planning approach utilising Output Breakdown Structures, Output Flow Diagrams
Learn how to produce a project schedule including various estimation techniques
Gain practical techniques related to time, scope, cost, and quality
Learn practical techniques related to resourcing and costing on projects
Understand the importance of project quality and how to plan for it
Understand your role in a project and learn tips and techniques to help you manage your time and priorities
Understand a typical project organisation and the roles and responsibilities for each member of the Project Team and Project Steering Committee
Learn about the importance of stakeholders and how to use a stakeholder analysis to produce a robust Communications & Engagement Plan
Gain awareness of Risk Management including the difference between risks and issues
Have a general understanding of benefits, their importance to projects, and how to identify and quantify them
Talk through lots of real-life project examples to cement the learnings and identify traps to avoid.
Have a general understanding of the differences between project, programme, and portfolio management
No prerequisite is required for attendance on this session, but any prior experience or knowledge of project management will be a definite advantage
This session is a mixture of theory and discussion and practical group-based learning involving post-it notes, markers, flip chart paper. An easy to understand and practical case study is used throughout the course. No laptops are required, all learning resources are supplied.

Click Here for more info and to register

Purpose in the Public Sector, "I work in the public sector because I want to make a positive contribution and make a difference in my community and in New Zealand"

description:
YEPN Wellington - Sustainable Aviation Fuel: A Strategic Approach, The Young Energy Professionals Network is pleased to invite you to our next Wellington event, proudly hosted by Z Energy at their waterfront offices.
This event will feature a panel discussion on one of the toughest – and most important – challenges in the energy transition: decarbonising aviation through Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)*.
Aviation is one of the most challenging sectors to decarbonise and by 2050, it could contribute more than a third of Aotearoa New Zealand’s total emissions. Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is emerging as a critical decarbonisation tool, and momentum is building both locally and globally.
In this session, we’ll bring together voices from across the aviation ecosystem – industry leaders, suppliers and customers – to explore how SAF is being adopted, scaled and supported in Aotearoa and overseas. From feedstocks and policy settings to operational realities and investment signals, we’ll unpack what’s driving demand, what barriers remain, and where the biggest opportunities lie.
Whether you're curious about the technology, the economics, or the practicalities of adoption, this is your chance to take a deep dive into an important fuel in the energy transition.
Panelists include:
Julian Hughes, GM Supply, Z Energy
Billie Moore, Chief Executive, NZ Airports Association
Peter van Cingel, Business Development Manager, Channel Infrastructure NZ

Drinks and nibbles provided
Spaces are limited — register below to secure your spot.
* 'Sustainable Aviation Fuel' is an industry term used to describe fuels manufactured using waste and purpose grown feedstocks, including used cooking oil (UCO), tallow and canola oil, and can provide carbon emissions reductions on a life cycle basis.

description:
Dare to Lead™ | Wellington | 25-27 February, Dare to Lead™ | Wellington | 25-27 February
Dare to Lead is the ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures, and organisational change.

About this Event


The ultimate starting point for brave leaders, courageous cultures and organisational change.


"Highly recommend."
"Inspiring."
"An amazing experience."
"One 'aha moment' after the other."

Founded on the research of Dr. Brené Brown, Dare to Lead™ is an empirically based courage-building programme, delivered by Boma New Zealand CEO and Certified Dare to Lead™ Facilitator Kaila Colbin.
Brené has spent two decades studying shame and more than seven years specifically looking at leadership. During her research, she interviewed leaders from all over the world — from Fortune 100 companies, non-profits, public sector entities, and more — and asked one question: what is the future of leadership?
Remarkably, their answers pointed to one thing: we need braver leaders.


We need more courage.

The most significant finding from Brené’s latest research, and the foundation of Dare to Lead™, is that courage is a collection of four skill sets that are teachable, measurable, and observable.


After completing the three-day Dare to Lead™ programme you'll understand how to:
Effectively navigate vulnerability and unlock change
Turn values from fluffy language into tangible, practical behaviours
Build a common culture of trust in your team
Cultivate the skills to rise from setbacks and be more resilient


This curriculum is essential for teams who want to:
Be better equipped to deal with difficult conversations
Reduce unhealthy and unproductive behaviour
Be more creative and innovative
Build resilience and improve alignment
Foster a culture of accountability and trust


This experience is for you if:
You're in a position of leadership within your organisation
You see the potential in people and processes, and are willing to take responsibility for achieving that potential
You’re passionate about accelerating performance in yourself and others
You have to navigate organisational change as part of your role

Pōneke Leader Learning & Doing Day (Sep 2025), Often, the best folk to learn from (and commiserate with) are other leaders. But since we're so busy in the doing, we don't often have the time or ability to take a full day off from work to dedicate to learning new things.... and sometimes conferences can be hit and miss on content.
Last year we created a Leader Learning & Doing Day, where you can come and co-work in the same space as a bunch of other founders and leaders, and also go to mini unconference sessions during the day that are set by you. You share/learn/discuss the things that matter to you most - with other folk that are going through it. We had sessions ranging from how to use AI in your org, founder transitions, and even a photographer taking new head shots for folk. 
The price of the ticket covers a koha to the venue and for some coffee/snacks. You can choose to come to all the sessions, or just one or two of them, and you'll have access to coffee and wifi throughout the day. 

Below is our plan for the day:
9:30am - Arrival & coffee
9:45am - Welcome, Introduction round & Agenda Setting
10:30am - Session 1
11:30am - Session 2
12:30pm - Lunch
1:30pm - Session 3
2:30pm - Farewell/head out for a drink (or home - you choose!)
